title.zh: 卷三十五 列傳第二十三: 王慧龍 鄭羲
title.en: Volume 35 Biographies 23: Wang Huilong, Zheng Xi
title.raw: 卷三十五 列傳第二十三: 王慧龍 鄭羲 Volume 35 Biographies 23: Wang Huilong, Zheng Xi

sentences.zh: 王慧龍 鄭羲

translations.literal: Wang Huilong; Zheng Xi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huilong and Zheng Xi

sentences.zh: 北史卷三十五

translations.literal: Northern History, Volume Thirty-Five
translations.idiomatic: History of the Northern Dynasties, Volume 35

sentences.zh: 列傳第二十三

translations.literal: Biographies, Number Twenty-Three
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 23

sentences.zh: 王慧龍玄孫松年五世孫劭鄭羲孫述祖從曾孫道邕道邕子譯譯叔祖儼儼族孫偉

translations.literal: Wang Huilong's great-grandson Songnian, fifth-generation descendant Shao; Zheng Xi's grandson Shuzu, great-great-grandson Dao Yong, Dao Yong's son Yi, Yi's grand-uncle Yan, Yan's clansman Wei
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huilong: great-grandson Songnian, fifth-generation descendant Shao. Zheng Xi: grandson Shuzu, great-great-grandson Dao Yong, Dao Yong's son Yi, Yi's grand-uncle Yan, Yan's clansman Wei

sentences.zh: 王慧龍，太原晉陽人，晉尚書僕射愉之孫，散騎常侍郎緝之子也。

translations.literal: Wang Huilong was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan, grandson of Jin Minister of Works Wang Yu, and son of Wang Ji, Attendant Cavalier in Regular Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Huilong, a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan, was grandson of the Jin Minister of Works Wang Yu and son of Wang Ji, Attendant Cavalier in Regular Attendance.

sentences.zh: 幼聰慧，愉以為諸孫之龍，故名焉。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and bright; Yu took him to be the dragon among all his grandsons, and so gave him that name.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was exceptionally bright; Yu regarded him as the dragon among his grandsons and named him accordingly.

sentences.zh: 初，宋武微時，愉不為之禮，及得志，愉闔家見誅。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Song Wudi was still obscure, Yu did not show him courtesy; when Wudi gained his aim, Yu's entire household was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Wu of Song was still obscure, Yu had shown him no courtesy; once Wu gained power, Yu's entire family was put to death.

sentences.zh: 慧龍年十四，為沙門僧彬所匿，因將過江。

translations.literal: Huilong was fourteen; he was hidden by the monk Seng Bin and thus was taken across the river.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong was fourteen when the monk Seng Bin concealed him and helped him cross the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 津人見其行意匆匆，疑為王氏子孫。

translations.literal: The ferryman saw his manner hurried and suspected he was a descendant of the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: The ferryman saw him hurrying along and suspected he was a Wang clansman.

sentences.zh: 彬稱為受業者，乃免。

translations.literal: Bin claimed he was a disciple receiving instruction, and so they were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Bin said he was a student under instruction, and they were let go.

sentences.zh: 既濟，遂西上江陵，依叔祖忱故吏荊州前中從事習辟強。

translations.literal: Once across, he went west to Jiangling and relied on Xi Biqiang, a former subordinate of his granduncle Chen, formerly Attendant of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing, he made his way west to Jiangling and stayed with Xi Biqiang, a former aide of his granduncle Chen who had served as Attendant in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時刺史魏詠之卒，辟強與江陵令羅修、前別駕劉期公、土人王騰等謀舉兵，推慧龍為盟主，克日襲州城。

translations.literal: At that time the provincial inspector Wei Yongzhi died; Biqiang with Jiangling magistrate Luo Xiu, former Vice Administrator Liu Qigong, local notable Wang Teng, and others plotted to raise troops, making Huilong league leader, with a fixed day to storm the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: When the inspector Wei Yongzhi died, Biqiang joined Jiangling magistrate Luo Xiu, former vice administrator Liu Qigong, local leader Wang Teng, and others in a plot to raise troops. They made Huilong their league chief and set a day to seize the provincial city.

sentences.zh: 而宋武聞詠之卒，亦懼江陵有變，遣其弟道規為荊州，眾遂不果。

translations.literal: But when Song Wudi heard of Yongzhi's death he also feared trouble at Jiangling and sent his younger brother Daogui to Jingzhou; the masses then did not carry out the plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Song heard that Yongzhi had died, he too feared unrest at Jiangling and sent his younger brother Daogui to take charge of Jingzhou. The plot then came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 羅修等將慧龍又與僧彬北詣襄陽。

translations.literal: Luo Xiu and the others escorted Huilong, and with Seng Bin he went north to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xiu and his party escorted Huilong north to Xiangyang, again accompanied by Seng Bin.

sentences.zh: 晉雍州刺史魯宗之資給慧龍，送度江，遂奔姚興。

translations.literal: Jin Inspector-General of Yongzhou Lu Zongzhi furnished supplies to Huilong and sent him across the river; he then fled to Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zongzhi, Jin inspector-general of Yongzhou, supplied Huilong and sent him across the river; he then fled into the service of Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 自言也如此。

translations.literal: Thus he spoke of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his own account of these events.

sentences.zh: 姚泓滅，慧龍歸魏。

translations.literal: When Yao Hong was destroyed, Huilong returned to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: After Yao Hong was overthrown, Huilong came over to the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 明元引見與言，慧龍請效力南討。

translations.literal: Emperor Mingyuan received him in audience and conversed with him; Huilong requested to serve in the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Mingyuan received him in audience and spoke with him; Huilong asked to be employed in the southern campaigns.

sentences.zh: 言終，俯而流涕，天子為之動容。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he bowed his head and wept; the Son of Heaven was moved on his account.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished, he bowed his head and wept; the emperor was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「朕方混一車書，席捲吳會，卿情計如此，豈不能相資以眾乎？

translations.literal: He said: "I am now about to unify script and carriage, sweep up Wu and Kuaiji—with your sentiments so set, can I not supply you with troops?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I am about to unite the realm under one script and one rule and sweep through Wu and Kuaiji. With your feelings so disposed, can I not give you an army to serve your purpose?"

sentences.zh: 」然亦未之用。

translations.literal: " Nevertheless he was not yet employed.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet he was not put to use.

sentences.zh: 後拜洛城鎮將，鎮金墉。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Pacifies the City and garrisoned Jin Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed general who pacified the city and stationed at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 會明元崩，太武初即位，咸謂南人不宜委以師旅之任，遂停前授。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingyuan died and Emperor Taiwu first took the throne, all said southerners should not be entrusted with military command, and his earlier appointment was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan died and Emperor Taiwu first acceded, everyone said southerners should not be given command of armies, and his earlier appointment was set aside.

sentences.zh: 初，崔浩弟恬聞慧龍王氏子，以女妻之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Cui Hao's younger brother Tian heard that Huilong was a Wang clansman and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Cui Hao's younger brother Tian learned that Huilong was of the Wang clan and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 浩既婚姻，及見慧龍，曰：「信王家兒也。

translations.literal: After the marriage, when Hao met Huilong he said: "Truly a son of the Wang house."
translations.idiomatic: Once the marriage was made, Hao met Huilong and said, "He is truly a son of the Wang house."

sentences.zh: 」王氏世齇鼻，江東謂之「齇王」。

translations.literal: " The Wang clan for generations had saddle noses; east of the Yangtze they were called the "Saddle-Nose Wangs."
translations.idiomatic: " The Wangs for generations had prominent saddle noses; in the lower Yangtze region they were called the "Saddle-Nose Wangs."

sentences.zh: 慧龍鼻漸大，浩曰：「真貴種矣！

translations.literal: Huilong's nose gradually grew larger; Hao said: "A true noble breed!"
translations.idiomatic: Huilong's nose gradually grew more prominent; Hao said, "A true noble strain!"

sentences.zh: 」數向諸公稱其美。

translations.literal: " He repeatedly praised him to the various nobles.
translations.idiomatic: " He praised Huilong again and again to the court nobles.

sentences.zh: 司徒長孫嵩聞之不悅，言于太武，以其嗟服南人則有訕鄙國化之意。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Changsun Song heard this with displeasure and spoke to Emperor Taiwu, saying that Hao's admiration of southerners showed intent to mock and belittle the nation's culture.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Changsun Song took offense and told Emperor Taiwu that Hao's admiration for southerners amounted to scorning the customs of the state.

sentences.zh: 太武怒，召浩責之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu was angry and summoned Hao to rebuke him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu was enraged and summoned Hao to reproach him.

sentences.zh: 浩免冠陳謝得釋。

translations.literal: Hao removed his cap and apologized and was released.
translations.idiomatic: Hao removed his cap, apologized at length, and was let off.

sentences.zh: 慧龍由是不調。

translations.literal: Because of this Huilong was not given an active post.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong was passed over for active appointment.

sentences.zh: 久之，除樂安王范傅，領並、荊、揚三州大中正。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made tutor to Prince Fan of Le'an and concurrently Grand Rectifier for Bing, Jing, and Yang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed tutor to Prince Fan of Le'an and concurrently grand rectifier for Bing, Jing, and Yang provinces.

sentences.zh: 慧龍抗表，願得南垂自效，崔浩固言之，乃授南蠻校尉、安南大將軍左長史。

translations.literal: Huilong submitted a memorial resisting the appointment, wishing to serve on the southern frontier; Cui Hao firmly spoke for him, and he was then made Colonel of Southern Barbarians and Senior Commander under the General Who Pacifies the South.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong memorialized in protest, asking to serve on the southern frontier; Cui Hao pressed his case, and he was appointed colonel of the southern barbarians and senior commander under the general who pacified the south.

sentences.zh: 及宋荊州刺史謝晦起兵江陵，引慧龍為援。

translations.literal: When Song Inspector of Jingzhou Xie Hui raised troops at Jiangling, he called on Huilong as ally.
translations.idiomatic: When Xie Hui, Song inspector of Jingzhou, raised troops at Jiangling, he sought Huilong as an ally.

sentences.zh: 慧龍督司馬靈壽等一萬人，拔其思陵戍，進圍項城。

translations.literal: Huilong directed Sima Lingshou and others—ten thousand men—in storming the Siling garrison and advancing to besiege Xiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong led Sima Lingshou and ten thousand men, captured the Siling garrison, and advanced to besiege Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 晦敗，乃班師。

translations.literal: When Hui was defeated, he withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui was defeated, Huilong withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 後宋將王玄謨寇滑台，詔假慧龍楚兵將軍，與安頡等同討之。

translations.literal: Later when Song general Wang Xuemo attacked Huatai, an edict made Huilong acting General of Chu Troops to join An Fu and others in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Song general Wang Xuemo attacked Huatai, an edict appointed Huilong acting general of Chu troops to join An Fu and others in repelling him.

sentences.zh: 相持五十餘日，諸將以賊盛，莫敢先，慧龍設奇兵大破之。

translations.literal: They faced each other more than fifty days; the generals, seeing the enemy strong, dared not advance first; Huilong deployed irregular troops and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: The two sides faced each other for more than fifty days; the other generals, seeing how strong the enemy was, dared not strike first, but Huilong deployed an irregular force and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 太武賜以劍馬錢帛，授龍驤將軍，賜爵長社侯，拜滎陽太守，仍領長史。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu granted sword, horses, money, and silk, appointed him General of Dragon Ferocity, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Changshe, made him Administrator of Xingyang, and he still held the post of senior commander.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taiwu rewarded him with sword, horses, money, and silk, appointed him general of dragon ferocity, enfeoffed him as Marquis of Changshe, made him administrator of Xingyang, and left him in charge as senior commander.

sentences.zh: 在任十年，農戰並修，大著聲績，招攜邊遠，歸附者萬餘家，號為善政。

translations.literal: During ten years in office he cultivated both agriculture and warfare, won great renown, and won over distant border peoples—more than ten thousand households came to submit, and his rule was called good government.
translations.idiomatic: In ten years in office he developed both farming and defense, won great renown, and drew in distant border peoples; more than ten thousand households submitted to him, and his administration was praised as exemplary.

sentences.zh: 其後宋將到彥之、檀道濟頻頓淮、潁，大相侵掠；

translations.literal: Thereafter Song generals Dao Yanzhi and Tan Daoji frequently encamped on the Huai and Ying rivers and launched large-scale raids;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Song generals Dao Yanzhi and Tan Daoji repeatedly camped on the Huai and Ying and launched major raids;

sentences.zh: 慧龍力戰，屢摧其鋒。

translations.literal: Huilong fought fiercely and repeatedly blunted their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong fought hard and repeatedly broke their momentum.

sentences.zh: 彥之與友人蕭斌書曰：「魯軌頑鈍，馬楚粗狂，亡人之中，唯王慧龍及韓延之可為深憚。

translations.literal: Yanzhi wrote to his friend Xiao Bin: "Lu Gui is obstinate and dull, Ma Chu is crude and wild; among the lost men, only Wang Huilong and Han Yanzhi are to be deeply feared."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi wrote to his friend Xiao Bin, "Lu Gui is stubborn and dull, Ma Chu is coarse and reckless; among the defectors, only Wang Huilong and Han Yanzhi are truly to be feared."

sentences.zh: 不意儒生懦夫，乃令老子訝之。

translations.literal: "I never expected a Confucian weakling would make this old man gasp."
translations.idiomatic: "I never thought a bookish weakling would leave me gasping."

sentences.zh: 」宋文縱反間，雲慧龍自以功高而位不至，欲引寇入邊，因執安南大將軍司馬楚之以叛。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wen of Song spread counter-intelligence saying Huilong, believing his merit high but rank inadequate, wished to lure invaders into the border and had seized Sima Chuyi of the General Who Pacifies the South and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wen of Song spread disinformation claiming that Huilong, resentful that his merit outstripped his rank, meant to lure the enemy across the border and had seized Sima Chuyi, senior commander under the general who pacified the south, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 太武聞曰：「此必不然，是齊人忌樂毅耳。

translations.literal: Emperor Taiwu heard and said: "This surely cannot be so—it is Qi people jealous of Yue Yi."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu heard this he said, "That cannot be true; it is like the people of Qi envying Yue Yi."

sentences.zh: 」乃賜慧龍璽書曰：「義隆畏將軍如虎，欲相中害，朕自知之。

translations.literal: " He then granted Huilong an imperial letter saying: "Yilong fears you, General, like a tiger and wishes to harm you in the middle; I know this myself."
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent Huilong an imperial letter: "Yilong fears you, General, as a tiger fears its hunter and means to destroy you by intrigue; I know this for myself."

sentences.zh: 風塵之言，想不足介意也。

translations.literal: "Dusty rumors—I trust you will not mind them too much."
translations.idiomatic: "Rumors borne on the wind—I trust you will not take them to heart."

sentences.zh: 」宋文計既不行，復遣刺客呂玄伯購慧龍首二百戶男、絹一千匹。

translations.literal: " When Emperor Wen's scheme failed, he again sent the assassin Lü Xuanbo offering two hundred household males and a thousand bolts of silk for Huilong's head.
translations.idiomatic: " When Emperor Wen's plot failed, he sent the assassin Lü Xuanbo with a bounty of two hundred household males and a thousand bolts of silk for Huilong's head.

sentences.zh: 玄伯為反間來，屏人有所論。

translations.literal: Xuanbo came as a double agent; he dismissed attendants to speak privately.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo came as a double agent and, dismissing attendants, spoke with Huilong in private.

sentences.zh: 慧龍疑之，使人探其懷有尺刀。

translations.literal: Huilong suspected him and had someone search his bosom—a foot-long knife was found.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong grew suspicious and had him searched; a foot-long knife was found in his robe.

sentences.zh: 玄伯叩頭請死。

translations.literal: Xuanbo knocked his head and begged for death.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanbo kowtowed and begged to be put to death.

sentences.zh: 慧龍曰：「各為其主也，吾不忍害此人。

translations.literal: Huilong said: "Each serves his own master; I cannot bear to harm this man."
translations.idiomatic: Huilong said, "Each man serves his own lord; I cannot bring myself to harm this man."

sentences.zh: 」左右皆言義隆賊心未巳，不殺玄伯，無以創將來。

translations.literal: " His attendants all said Yilong's treacherous heart was not yet exhausted; if Xuanbo were not killed, there would be no warning to the future.
translations.idiomatic: " His attendants all said Yilong's treachery was not yet spent and that unless Xuanbo were killed there would be no deterrent for the future.

sentences.zh: 慧龍曰：「死生有命，彼亦安能害我。

translations.literal: Huilong said: "Life and death have their mandate; how could he harm me?"
translations.idiomatic: Huilong said, "Life and death are ordained by fate; how could he harm me?"

sentences.zh: 且吾方以仁義為幹鹵，又何憂乎刺客。

translations.literal: "Moreover I am just now taking benevolence and righteousness as my rampart—why worry about assassins?"
translations.idiomatic: "Besides, I am just now making benevolence and righteousness my rampart—why should I fear assassins?"

sentences.zh: 」遂舍之。

translations.literal: " He then released him.
translations.idiomatic: " He let him go.

sentences.zh: 時人服其寬恕。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his clemency.
translations.idiomatic: People of the day admired his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 慧龍自以遭難流離，常懷憂悴，乃作《祭伍子胥文》以寄意焉。

translations.literal: Huilong, considering himself exiled through hardship, was often burdened with grief; he composed "A Text Sacrificing to Wu Zixu" to express his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Huilong, having suffered exile and hardship, was often weighed down with sorrow and wrote "A Sacrificial Text for Wu Zixu" to give voice to his feelings.

sentences.zh: 生一男一女，遂絕房室，布衣蔬食，不參吉事，舉動必以禮。

translations.literal: He had one son and one daughter, then ceased marital relations, wore plain cloth and ate plain food, did not attend auspicious affairs, and in conduct always observed ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He had one son and one daughter, then ceased conjugal life, wore plain cloth and ate simple food, avoided auspicious gatherings, and in all his conduct observed ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 太子少傅游雅言於朝曰：「慧龍，古之遺孝也。

translations.literal: Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent You Ya said at court: "Huilong is a surviving type of ancient filial piety."
translations.idiomatic: Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent You Ya said at court, "Huilong is a living remnant of the filial devotion of antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」撰帝王制度十八篇，號曰《國典》。

translations.literal: " He compiled eighteen chapters on imperial institutions, entitled National Institutions.
translations.idiomatic: " He compiled eighteen chapters on imperial institutions under the title National Institutions.

sentences.zh: 真君元年，拜使持節、甯南將軍、武牢鎮都副將，未至鎮而卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenjun he was appointed with Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the South, and Deputy Commander of the Garrison at Wulao, and died before reaching his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenjun he was appointed with staff of authority as general who pacified the south and deputy commander of the Wulao garrison, but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 臨沒，謂功曹鄭曄曰：「吾羈旅南人，恩非舊結，蒙聖朝殊特之慈，得在疆場效命，誓願鞭屍吳市，戮墳江陰。

translations.literal: On the verge of death he told Merit Officer Zheng Ye: "I am a southern man in exile; grace was not an old bond, yet I received the court's extraordinary kindness and could serve on the frontier. I vowed to whip the corpse in Wu market and destroy the tomb on Jiang's north bank."
translations.idiomatic: As death approached he told merit officer Zheng Ye, "I am a southerner living in exile; my ties to the court were not old, yet I received its extraordinary kindness and was able to serve on the frontier. I swore to lash the enemy's corpse in the markets of Wu and raze their tombs on the north bank of the Yangtze."

sentences.zh: 不謂嬰此重疾，有心莫遂，非唯仰愧國靈，實亦俯慚后土。

translations.literal: "I did not expect to fall into this grave illness; my heart cannot be fulfilled—this fails not only the nation's spirits above but also shames the earth below."
translations.idiomatic: "I did not expect to be struck down by this grave illness; my heart's purpose cannot be fulfilled. This shames not only the spirits of the state above but also the earth below."

sentences.zh: 修短命也，夫復何言！

translations.literal: "Fate is short—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: "My allotted span is brief—what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 身歿後，乞葬河內州縣之東鄉，依古墓而不墳，足藏發齒而已。

translations.literal: "After my body is gone, I beg burial in the eastern district of a county in Henei, beside ancient tombs without a mound—enough only to hold hair and teeth."
translations.idiomatic: "After my death, I beg to be buried in the eastern township of a county in Henei, beside an ancient tomb without a mound—enough only to hold my hair and teeth."

sentences.zh: 庶其魂而有知，猶希結草之報。

translations.literal: "If my spirit has awareness, I still hope for the repayment of the knotted grass."
translations.idiomatic: "If my spirit has awareness, I still hope for the repayment of the knotted grass."

sentences.zh: 」時制，南人入國者，皆葬桑乾。

translations.literal: " At that time the rule was: all southerners entering the state were buried at Sanggan.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the regulation was that all southerners who entered the state were buried at Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 曄等申遺意，詔許之。

translations.literal: Ye and others reported his last wishes; an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ye and the others reported his last wishes, and an edict granted them.

sentences.zh: 贈安南將軍、荊州刺史，諡穆侯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jingzhou, with posthumous title Marquis Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed general who pacified the south and inspector of Jingzhou, with the posthumous title Marquis Mu.

sentences.zh: 吏人及將士共於墓所起佛寺，圖慧龍及僧彬像而贊之。

translations.literal: Officials and soldiers together built a Buddhist temple at the tomb site and painted images of Huilong and Seng Bin with eulogies.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and soldiers together built a Buddhist temple at the tomb and painted images of Huilong and Seng Bin with laudatory inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 呂玄伯感全宥之恩，留守墓側，終身不去。

translations.literal: Lü Xuanbo, moved by the grace of complete pardon, remained by the tomb and never left in his lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Xuanbo, moved by Huilong's complete sparing of his life, kept watch beside the tomb and never left it for the rest of his days.

sentences.zh: 子寶興襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Baoxing inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baoxing inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 寶興少孤，事母至孝。

translations.literal: Baoxing lost his father young and served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing lost his father while still young and served his mother with the utmost filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 尚書盧遐妻，崔浩女也。

translations.literal: The wife of Minister Lu Xia was Cui Hao's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Minister Lu Xia was a daughter of Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 初，寶興母及遐妻俱孕，浩謂曰：「汝等將來所生，皆我之自出，可指腹為親。

translations.literal: Earlier, both Baoxing's mother and Xia's wife were pregnant; Hao said: "Those you will bear in the future are all my own issue—let us betroth them by touching bellies."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, both Baoxing's mother and Xia's wife were pregnant. Hao said, "The children you will bear are all of my own blood; let us betroth them while still in the womb."

sentences.zh: 」及昏，浩為撰儀，躬自監視，謂諸客曰：「此家禮事，宜盡其美。

translations.literal: " At dusk Hao drafted the ceremony and personally supervised it, telling the guests: "This family's ritual affair should be carried through with full beauty."
translations.idiomatic: " At dusk Hao drew up the ceremony and supervised it in person, telling the guests, "This family's ritual should be carried out with every refinement."

sentences.zh: 」及浩被誅，盧遐後妻寶興從母也，緣坐沒官。

translations.literal: " When Hao was executed, Lu Xia's later wife—Baoxing's mother's sister by marriage—was implicated and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: " When Hao was executed, Lu Xia's later wife—Baoxing's aunt by marriage—was implicated by association and reduced to servitude.

sentences.zh: 寶興亦逃避，未幾得出。

translations.literal: Baoxing also fled; not long after he got out.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxing also went into hiding, but before long he escaped.

sentences.zh: 盧遐妻時官賜度斤鎮高車滑骨，寶興盡賣貨產，自出塞贖之以歸。

translations.literal: When Xia's wife was sent by office to Du Jin town and Gaoche Huagu, Baoxing sold all his property and went beyond the frontier himself to ransom her and bring her home.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia's wife was assigned by the authorities to Du Jin town in the Gaoche Huagu region, Baoxing sold all his property, went beyond the frontier himself, ransomed her, and brought her home.

sentences.zh: 州辟中從事、別駕，舉秀才，皆不就。

translations.literal: The province appointed him Attendant and Vice Administrator and nominated him as xiucai; he accepted none of these.
translations.idiomatic: The province offered him posts as attendant and vice administrator and nominated him as xiucai, but he accepted none of them.

sentences.zh: 閉門不交人事。

translations.literal: He shut his door and would not engage in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He shut his door and refused all worldly entanglements.

sentences.zh: 襲爵封長社侯、龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: He inherited the title and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changshe and General of Dragon Ferocity.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the title and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Changshe and appointed general of dragon ferocity.

sentences.zh: 卒，子瓊襲爵。

translations.literal: He died; his son Qiong inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: He died, and his son Qiong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 瓊字世珍，孝文賜名焉。

translations.literal: Qiong styled Shizhen; Emperor Xiaowen bestowed the name upon him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong, styled Shizhen, received his given name as a gift from Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 太和九年，為典寺令六十年，降侯為伯。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe he became Director of the Palace Temple; at age sixty his marquisate was reduced to a countship.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taihe he was appointed director of the palace temple; at the age of sixty his marquisate was reduced to a countship.

sentences.zh: 帝納其長女為嬪，拜前將軍、并州大中正。

translations.literal: The emperor took his eldest daughter as concubine; he was appointed General of the Van and Grand Rectifier of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his eldest daughter as a concubine and appointed him general of the van and grand rectifier of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 正始中，為光州刺史，有受納響，為中尉王顯所劾，終得雪免。

translations.literal: In the Zhengshi era he was Inspector of Guangzhou; there were reports of accepting bribes; he was impeached by Chief Censor Wang Xian but was ultimately cleared and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengshi era he served as inspector of Guangzhou; reports of bribery reached the court, and chief censor Wang Xian impeached him, but in the end he was cleared and released from office.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，除左將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era he was made General of the Left and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shengui era he was appointed general of the left and inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 去州歸京，多年沈滯。

translations.literal: After leaving his province he returned to the capital and for many years languished without promotion.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving his province he returned to the capital and languished for many years without advancement.

sentences.zh: 所居在司空劉騰宅西，騰雖勢傾朝野，初不候之。

translations.literal: His residence was west of Minister of Works Liu Teng's mansion; though Teng's power bent the court, at first he did not call on him.
translations.idiomatic: His home lay west of Minister of Works Liu Teng's mansion; though Teng's power dominated the court, Qiong at first never called on him.

sentences.zh: 騰既權重，吞併鄰宅，增廣舊居，唯瓊終不肯與，以此久見屈抑。

translations.literal: Once Teng's authority grew heavy, he annexed neighboring houses and expanded his old residence; only Qiong refused to yield, and for this he was long suppressed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Teng's power was fully established, he annexed neighboring properties and enlarged his old residence, but Qiong alone refused to sell, and for this he was kept down for years.

sentences.zh: 瓊女適范陽盧道亮，不聽歸其夫家。

translations.literal: Qiong's daughter married Lu Daoliang of Fanyang but was not permitted to return to her husband's house.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong's daughter married Lu Daoliang of Fanyang, but Qiong would not let her go to her husband's household.

sentences.zh: 女卒，哀慟無已，瓊仍葬之別所，塚不即塞，常於壙內哭泣，久之乃掩，當時深怪之。

translations.literal: When the daughter died he mourned without end; Qiong still buried her in a separate place, the mound not immediately sealed, and often wept inside the vault—only after a long time was it covered; people of the time found this deeply strange.
translations.idiomatic: When the daughter died he mourned without cease. Qiong buried her in a separate place, left the mound unsealed, and often wept inside the tomb chamber; only after a long interval was it closed. People of the day found this deeply strange.

sentences.zh: 加以聾疾，每見道俗，乞丐無已，造次見之，令人笑愕。

translations.literal: Added to this he had deafness; whenever he saw clergy or laity he begged without cease; meeting him casually made people laugh in astonishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was also deaf, and whenever he met clergy or laypeople he begged without end; an encounter with him on the street could leave people laughing in disbelief.

sentences.zh: 道逢太保、廣平王懷，據鞍抗禮，自言馬瘦；

translations.literal: On the road he met Grand Tutor and Prince Huai of Guangping; he reined his saddle and returned salute, saying his horse was lean;
translations.idiomatic: On the road he met Grand Tutor Prince Huai of Guangping, reined in his saddle, returned the salute from horseback, and said his horse was too thin;

sentences.zh: 懷即以誕馬並乘具與之。

translations.literal: Huai immediately gave him his birth horse together with riding gear.
translations.idiomatic: Huai at once gave him his own foaling mare together with saddle and harness.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣尚書令李崇，騎馬至其黃閣，見崇子世哲，直問繼伯在否。

translations.literal: Once he called on Minister of Works Li Chong, riding to his yellow gate; he saw Chong's son Shizhe and directly asked whether Jibo was present.
translations.idiomatic: Once he called on Minister Li Chong, riding his horse right up to the yellow gate; he saw Chong's son Shizhe and asked outright whether Jibo was there.

sentences.zh: 崇趨出，瓊乃下。

translations.literal: Chong hastened out; Qiong then dismounted.
translations.idiomatic: Chong hurried out to meet him, and only then did Qiong dismount from his horse.

sentences.zh: 崇儉而好以紙帖衣領，瓊哂而掣去之。

translations.literal: Chong was frugal and liked to paste paper on his collar; Qiong sneered and tore it off.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was thrifty and liked to paste paper patches on his collar; Qiong laughed at him and ripped them away.

sentences.zh: 崇小子青肫嘗盛服，寵勢亦不足恨。

translations.literal: Chong's young son Qingtun once wore splendid dress; favor and power were still not enough to be regretted.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's young son Qingtun once dressed in splendid robes, yet even favor and power were scarcely worth envying.

sentences.zh: 領軍元叉使奴遺瓊馬，瓊並留奴。

translations.literal: Commander-in-chief Yuan Cha sent a slave to present Qiong with a horse; Qiong detained both.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha sent a slave to present Qiong with a horse; Qiong kept both the horse and the slave.

sentences.zh: 王誦聞之笑曰：「東海之風，於茲墜矣。

translations.literal: Wang Song heard it and laughed, saying: "The wind of the Eastern Sea has fallen here."
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Song heard of it he laughed and said, "The free spirit of the Eastern Sea has come to ruin here."

sentences.zh: 」孝昌三年，除鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫、中書令。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaochang he was removed and made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Purse, and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaochang he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East, made Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Purse, and named Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時瓊子遵業為黃門郎，故有此授。

translations.literal: At that time Qiong's son Zunye was Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, and for this reason he received the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Qiong's son Zunye was serving as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, and it was for this reason that he received the appointment.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征北將軍、中書監、并州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously awarded General Who Campaigns North, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, and Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made General Who Campaigns North, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, and Governor of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 自慧龍入國，三世一身，至瓊始有四子。

translations.literal: Since Huilong entered the realm, three generations had but one son each; only with Qiong did four sons appear.
translations.idiomatic: From the time Huilong entered the realm, three generations had produced only one son each; not until Qiong did the family have four sons.

sentences.zh: 長子遵業，風儀清秀，涉歷經史。

translations.literal: The eldest son Zunye had refined bearing and graceful appearance, and was versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Zunye was graceful in bearing and well versed in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 位著作佐郎，與司徒左長史崔鴻同撰起居注。

translations.literal: He held the post of Assistant Gentleman of the Writing Office, and together with Chief Clerk on the Left of the Minister of Works Cui Hong compiled the Diary of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Assistant Gentleman of the Writing Office and, together with Chief Clerk on the Left of the Minister of Works Cui Hong, compiled the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 遷右軍將軍、兼散騎常侍，慰勞蠕蠕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Army and Acting Regular Attendant, to console the Rouran.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General of the Right Army and Acting Regular Attendant and sent to console the Rouran.

sentences.zh: 乃詣代京，采拾遺文，以補起居所闕。

translations.literal: He then proceeded to the capital at Dai, gathering lost texts to supplement gaps in the diary.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to the capital at Dai, collected lost documents, and used them to fill gaps in the diary.

sentences.zh: 與崔光、安豐王延明等參定服章。

translations.literal: Together with Cui Guang, Prince Yanming of Anfeng, and others he helped fix regulations for robes and insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Cui Guang, Prince Yanming of Anfeng, and others, he helped revise regulations for court dress and insignia.

sentences.zh: 及光為孝明講《孝經》，遵業預講，延業錄義，並應詔作《釋奠侍宴詩》。

translations.literal: When Guang lectured on the "Classic of Filial Piety" for Emperor Xiaoming, Zunye took part in the lecture, Yan Ye recorded the meaning, and both by imperial order composed "Poems on Attending the Banquet at the Sacrifice to Confucius."
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Guang lectured on the "Classic of Filial Piety" for Emperor Xiaoming, Zunye joined the lecture, Yan Ye recorded its meaning, and both composed "Poems on Attending the Sacrifice to Confucius Banquet" by imperial command.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「英英濟濟，王家兄弟。

translations.literal: People of the time said: "Splendid and imposing are the Wang brothers."
translations.idiomatic: People of the day said, "Splendid and imposing are the Wang brothers."

sentences.zh: 」轉司徒左長史、黃門郎，監典儀注。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk on the Left of the Minister of Works and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, overseeing ceremonial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Clerk on the Left of the Minister of Works and Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, with charge over ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 遵業有譽當時，與中書令陳郡袁翻、尚書琅邪王誦並領黃門郎，號曰三哲。

translations.literal: Zunye enjoyed renown in his day; together with Palace Attendant Yuan Fan of Chen commandery and Minister Wang Song of Langya, all holding the post of Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, they were styled the Three Philosophers.
translations.idiomatic: Zunye enjoyed great renown in his day. Together with Palace Attendant Yuan Fan of Chen and Minister Wang Song of Langye, all serving as Gentlemen at the Yellow Gate, they were known as the Three Philosophers.

sentences.zh: 時政歸門下，世謂侍中、黃門為小宰相。

translations.literal: At that time political power rested with the Gate Office; the world called Attendants-in-Chief and Gentlemen at the Yellow Gate "lesser chancellors."
translations.idiomatic: At the time real power lay with the Gate Office, and people called the Attendants-in-Chief and Gentlemen at the Yellow Gate "lesser chancellors."

sentences.zh: 而遵業從容恬素，若處丘園。

translations.literal: Yet Zunye was leisurely, calm, and plain, as if dwelling in hills and gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zunye remained easy and unassuming, as though he lived in seclusion among hills and gardens.

sentences.zh: 嘗著穿角履，好事者多毀新履以學之。

translations.literal: He once wore sandals with upturned corners; many enthusiasts ruined new shoes to imitate him.
translations.idiomatic: He once wore sandals with upturned toes, and so many admirers ruined new shoes trying to copy him.

sentences.zh: 以胡太后臨朝，天下方亂，謀避地，自求徐州。

translations.literal: Because Empress Dowager Hu held court and the realm was in turmoil, he plotted to escape and personally requested Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: With Empress Dowager Hu regent and the realm falling into chaos, he sought a place of refuge and asked to be sent to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「王誦罷幽州始作黃門，卿何乃欲徐州也？

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Wang Song finished Youzhou before becoming Gentleman at the Yellow Gate—why do you want Xuzhou?"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "Wang Song had to leave Youzhou before he became Gentleman at the Yellow Gate—why are you already asking for Xuzhou?"

sentences.zh: 更待一二年，當有好處分。

translations.literal: Wait another year or two and you will surely receive a fine assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Wait another year or two and you will surely receive a better appointment.

sentences.zh: 」遵業兄弟並交遊時俊，乃為當時所美。

translations.literal: Zunye and his brothers all associated with the outstanding men of the age, and were admired by their contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Zunye and his brothers all moved in the circle of the day's leading men and were widely admired.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮入洛，兄弟在父喪中，以于莊帝有從姨兄弟之親，相率奉迎，俱見害河陰。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, the brothers were in mourning for their father; having a cousin relationship with Emperor Zhuang through his mother's clan, they went together to welcome him, and all were killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong entered Luoyang, the brothers were still in mourning for their father. Because they were cousins to Emperor Zhuang on his mother's side, they went out together to welcome Rong and were all killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 議者惜其人才，而譏其躁競。

translations.literal: Commentators lamented their talents yet criticized their rash ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators lamented their wasted talent but criticized their rash ambition.

sentences.zh: 贈并州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Governor of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 著《三晉記》十卷。

translations.literal: He wrote the "Record of the Three Jin" in ten fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the "Record of the Three Jin" in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子松年，少知名，齊文襄臨并州，辟為主簿。

translations.literal: His son Songnian was known from youth; when Wenxiang of Qi came to Bingzhou he recruited him as chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His son Songnian was known from an early age. When Wenxiang of Qi came to Bingzhou he recruited him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 累遷通直散騎常侍，副李緯使梁。

translations.literal: He rose through successive posts to Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Cavalier, and as deputy to Li Wei served as envoy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to Regular Attendant of the Direct and Upright Cavalier and, as Li Wei's deputy, served as envoy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 使還，歷位尚書郎中。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he served in succession as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: After the mission returned he served in succession as Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 魏收撰《魏書》成，松年有謗言。

translations.literal: When Wei Shou finished compiling the "Book of Wei," Songnian made slanderous remarks.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Shou finished compiling the "Book of Wei," Songnian spoke against it.

sentences.zh: 文宣怒，禁止之，仍加杖罰。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenxuan was angry, imprisoned him, and additionally imposed beating with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan was furious, had him imprisoned, and also ordered him beaten with the staff.

sentences.zh: 歲餘得免，除臨漳令。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was released and appointed Magistrate of Linzhang.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was released and appointed magistrate of Linzhang.

sentences.zh: 遷司馬、別駕、本州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Administrator, Assistant Governor, and Great Rectifier of his home province.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Administrator, Assistant Governor, and Regional Rectifier of his home province.

sentences.zh: 孝昭擢拜給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao elevated him to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhao promoted him to Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 帝每賜坐，與論政事，甚善之。

translations.literal: The emperor often granted him a seat and discussed state affairs with him, holding him in high regard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often gave him a seat and discussed state affairs with him, and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 孝昭崩，松年馳驛至鄴都宣遺詔。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao died, Songnian raced by post relay to Ye to proclaim the final edict.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao died, Songnian raced by post relay to Ye to proclaim the late emperor's final edict.

sentences.zh: 發言涕泗，迄于宣罷，容色無改，辭吐諧韻，宣訖號慟，自絕於地，百官莫不感慟。

translations.literal: As he spoke tears flowed; until the proclamation was finished his countenance did not change and his words kept their rhythm—but when the announcement ended he wailed in grief and fell senseless to the ground; none of the officials failed to be deeply moved.
translations.idiomatic: As he spoke tears streamed down his face; until the proclamation ended his expression did not change and his words kept their measured rhythm. But when the announcement was finished he wailed in grief and collapsed to the ground, and every official present was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 還晉陽，兼侍中，護梓宮還鄴。

translations.literal: Returning to Jinyang, he concurrently served as Attendant-in-Chief and escorted the imperial coffin back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Jinyang, he also served as Attendant-in-Chief and escorted the imperial coffin back to Ye.

sentences.zh: 諸舊臣避形跡，無敢盡哀，唯松年哭必流涕，朝士咸恐。

translations.literal: The senior ministers held back and dared not fully mourn, but only Songnian wept with streaming tears; court officials were all afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The senior ministers held themselves in check and dared not mourn fully, but Songnian wept with streaming tears, and the court officials were all afraid.

sentences.zh: 武成雖忿松年戀舊情切，亦雅重之。

translations.literal: Although Wucheng resented Songnian's intense attachment to the former reign, he still held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Although Wucheng resented Songnian's intense loyalty to the former reign, he still held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 以本官加散騎常侍，食高邑縣幹。

translations.literal: On his original post he was additionally made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, drawing salary from Gaoyi county.
translations.idiomatic: He retained his original post while also being made Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, with salary drawn from Gaoyi county.

sentences.zh: 參定律令，前後大獄多委焉。

translations.literal: He took part in fixing laws and statutes; major trials before and after were largely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in revising laws and statutes, and major trials before and after were largely entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He also served as Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He also served concurrently as Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 發晉陽之鄴，在道遇疾卒。

translations.literal: He set out from Jinyang toward Ye; on the road he met illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: While traveling from Jinyang to Ye he fell ill on the road and died.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，并州刺史，諡曰平。

translations.literal: He was posthumously awarded Minister of the Civil Office, Governor of Bing Province, with the posthumous name Ping.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of the Civil Office and Governor of Bing Province, with the posthumous name Ping.

sentences.zh: 第二子劭最知名。

translations.literal: His second son Shao was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Shao was the most famous.

sentences.zh: 劭字君懋，少沈默，好讀書。

translations.literal: Shao, style Junmao, was silent from youth and loved reading books.
translations.idiomatic: Shao, whose style was Junmao, was quiet from youth and loved to read.

sentences.zh: 仕齊，累遷太子舍人，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: He served Qi, rising through posts to Crown Prince's Attendant, awaiting imperial orders at the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: He served Northern Qi, rising through successive posts to Crown Prince's Attendant and awaiting imperial orders at the Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 時祖孝征、魏收、陽休之等嘗論古事，有所遺忘，討閱不能得。

translations.literal: When Zu Xiaozheng, Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi and others discussed antiquities and forgot something, they could not find it despite searching.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Xiaozheng, Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, and others discussed antiquities and forgot some detail, they could not find it even after searching.

sentences.zh: 問劭，劭具論所出，取書驗之，一無舛誤。

translations.literal: They asked Shao; he fully stated where it came from, they fetched books to verify, and not one error appeared.
translations.idiomatic: They asked Shao, who cited the source in full; when they fetched books to check, not a single error appeared.

sentences.zh: 自是大為時人所許，稱其博物。

translations.literal: From then on he was greatly acknowledged by contemporaries, who praised his broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he was widely admired, and people praised his encyclopedic learning.

sentences.zh: 後遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was promoted to Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 齊滅入周，不得調。

translations.literal: When Qi fell and he entered Zhou, he received no appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell and he entered Zhou, he received no government post.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝受禪，授著作佐郎，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the abdication he was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Writing Office, then left office on account of his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui accepted the throne he was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Writing Office, then left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 在家著《齊書》，時制禁私撰史，為內史侍郎李元操所奏。

translations.literal: At home he wrote the "Book of Qi"; private history-writing was forbidden at the time, and Internal History Gentleman Li Yuancao impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: At home he wrote the "Book of Qi," but private history-writing was forbidden at the time, and Internal History Gentleman Li Yuancao reported him.

sentences.zh: 上怒，遣收其書，覽而悅之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and ordered his books seized; but on reading them he was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and ordered his manuscript seized, but on reading it he was delighted.

sentences.zh: 於是起為員外散騎侍郎，修起居注。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was raised to Extraordinary Attendant of the Cavalry and compiled the Diary of Activity and Repose.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was recalled as Extraordinary Attendant of the Cavalry and put in charge of compiling the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 劭以上古有鑽燧改火之義，近代廢絕，於是上表請變火曰：「臣謹案《周官》：'四時變火，以救時疾。

translations.literal: Shao, because in antiquity there was the doctrine of boring wood to obtain fire and changing fire, which in recent times had been abandoned, thereupon submitted a memorial requesting change of fire, saying: "Your subject respectfully examines the 'Offices of Zhou': 'In the four seasons change fire to remedy seasonal illness.'"
translations.idiomatic: Shao observed that in antiquity there was the practice of boring wood for fire and changing fire by season, but that in recent times it had been abandoned. He therefore submitted a memorial on changing fire, saying, "Your subject respectfully notes in the 'Offices of Zhou': 'Change fire in the four seasons to remedy seasonal illness.'"

sentences.zh: '明火不數變，時疾必興。

translations.literal: 'If the bright fire is not changed in number, seasonal illness is sure to arise.'
translations.idiomatic: 'If the hearth fire is not changed at the proper intervals, seasonal illness is sure to break out.'

sentences.zh: 聖人作法，豈徒然也？

translations.literal: The sages established regulations—was it for nothing?
translations.idiomatic: The sages established these rules—surely not in vain?

sentences.zh: 在晉時，有人以洛陽火度江者，世世事之，相續不滅，火色變青。

translations.literal: In Jin times, someone brought Luoyang fire across the river; generation after generation served it, continuing unextinguished, and the fire's color turned blue-green.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times someone brought fire from Luoyang across the Yangzi; for generations the family tended it without letting it die out, until the flame turned bluish-green.

sentences.zh: 昔師曠食飯，雲是勞薪所爨，晉平公使視之，果然車輞。

translations.literal: Formerly when Shi Kuang ate rice, he said it was cooked with exhausted firewood; Duke Ping of Jin sent someone to look and indeed it was a wagon wheel rim.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Shi Kuang ate his rice he said it had been cooked with exhausted firewood; Duke Ping of Jin sent someone to investigate and found it was indeed a wagon wheel rim.

sentences.zh: 今溫酒及炙肉，用石炭、木炭火、竹火、草火、麻荄火，氣味各不同。

translations.literal: Now for warming wine and roasting meat, stone coal, charcoal fire, bamboo fire, grass fire, and hemp-stalk fire are used—the odors each differ.
translations.idiomatic: Today wine is warmed and meat roasted with stone coal, charcoal, bamboo, grass, and hemp-stalk fires, each producing a different odor.

sentences.zh: 以此推之，新火舊火，理應有異。

translations.literal: By this inference, new fire and old fire ought rationally to differ.
translations.idiomatic: From this one may infer that new fire and old fire ought naturally to differ.

sentences.zh: 伏願遠遵先聖，于五時取五木以變火。

translations.literal: I humbly wish to follow the former sages afar and at the five seasons take the five kinds of wood to change fire.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty will follow the ancient sages and, at the five seasons, take the five kinds of wood to change the fire.

sentences.zh: 用功甚少，救益方大。

translations.literal: The labor required is very slight, the benefit to be rescued is very great.
translations.idiomatic: The effort required would be slight, but the benefit to public health would be great.

sentences.zh: 縱使百姓習久，未能頓同，尚食內廚及東宮諸王食廚，不可不依古法。

translations.literal: Even if the common people, long accustomed, cannot at once comply, the imperial kitchen and the kitchens of the Eastern Palace and the princely sons should not fail to follow the ancient method.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the common people, long accustomed to the old ways, cannot change all at once, the imperial kitchen and the kitchens of the Eastern Palace and the princes should not fail to follow the ancient method.

sentences.zh: 」上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 劭又言上有龍顏戴幹之表，指示群臣。

translations.literal: Shao also said the emperor bore on his face the marks of a dragon countenance and the tian-gan on his head, and pointed this out to the assembled ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Shao also said that the emperor's face showed the marks of a dragon countenance and that he wore the Heavenly Stem on his brow, and pointed this out to the assembled ministers.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，賜物數百段，拜著作郎。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, bestowed several hundred lengths of goods, and appointed him Gentleman of the Writing Office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted, rewarded him with several hundred lengths of goods, and appointed him Gentleman of the Writing Office.

sentences.zh: 上表言符命曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial on portents and fate, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial on portents and the Mandate of Heaven, saying:

sentences.zh: 昔周保定二年，歲在壬午，五月五日，青州黃河變清，十里鏡澈。

translations.literal: Formerly in the second year of Baoding of Zhou, the year being in ren-wu, on the fifth day of the fifth month, the Yellow River in Qing province turned clear, for ten li like a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, in the second year of Baoding of Northern Zhou, a ren-wu year, on the fifth day of the fifth month the Yellow River in Qing province turned clear, and for ten li its waters were bright as a mirror.

sentences.zh: 齊氏以為己瑞，改元，年曰河清。

translations.literal: The Qi house took it as their own auspice, changed the reign title, and the year was called River Clear.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Qi took it as their own auspicious omen, changed the reign title, and named the era River Clear.

sentences.zh: 是月，至尊以大興公始作隨州刺史。

translations.literal: That same month the Supreme One, as Duke of Daxing, first became Governor of Sui province.
translations.idiomatic: That same month the future emperor, then Duke of Daxing, first took office as governor of Sui province.

sentences.zh: 歷年二十，隋果大興。

translations.literal: After twenty years Sui indeed greatly rose.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years later Sui did indeed rise to greatness.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案《易·坤靈圖》曰：「聖人受命，瑞必先見於河。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully examines the "Kun Ling Diagram" of the "Changes": "When a sage receives the Mandate, auspices must first appear in the river."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject respectfully notes what the "Kun Ling Diagram" of the "Changes" says: "When a sage receives the Mandate, auspicious signs must first appear in the river."

sentences.zh: 」河者最濁，未能清也。

translations.literal: The river is the most turbid and could not become clear.
translations.idiomatic: The river is the murkiest of waters and could not clear itself on its own.

sentences.zh: 竊以靈貺休祥，理無虛發；

translations.literal: I venture that numinous gifts and blessed omens, by principle, are not sent forth in vain;
translations.idiomatic: I venture to believe that numinous gifts and blessed omens do not appear without reason;

sentences.zh: 河清啟聖，實屬大隋。

translations.literal: River clear to inaugurate the sage truly belonged to Great Sui.
translations.idiomatic: the clearing of the river that heralded a sage truly belonged to Great Sui.

sentences.zh: 午為鶉火，以明火德；

translations.literal: Wu is the Quail Fire, manifesting the virtue of fire;
translations.idiomatic: The wu year corresponds to the Quail Fire asterism, manifesting the virtue of fire;

sentences.zh: 仲夏火王，亦明火德。

translations.literal: Midsummer when fire is king also manifests the virtue of fire.
translations.idiomatic: and midsummer, when fire reigns supreme, likewise manifests the virtue of fire.

sentences.zh: 月五日五，合天地數，既得受命之辰，允當先見之兆。

translations.literal: The fifth month, fifth day, five and five, matching heaven and earth's numbers—having already obtained the time of receiving the Mandate, it truly ought to be the omen seen beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth month on the fifth day, with five doubled, matches the numbers of heaven and earth. Having already obtained the moment of receiving the Mandate, it was fitting that the omen should appear in advance.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，邵州人楊令悊近河得青石圖一、紫石圖一，皆隱起成文，有至尊名，下云「八方天心」。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, Yang Lingti of Shao province obtained near the river one green stone diagram and one purple stone diagram; both had raised inscriptions, bore the Supreme One's name, and below read "Heart of Heaven in the Eight Directions."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era, Yang Lingti of Shao province found near the river one green stone chart and one purple stone chart, both bearing raised inscriptions with the emperor's name and the words "Heart of Heaven in the Eight Directions."

sentences.zh: 永州又得石圖，剖為兩段，有楊樹之形，黃根青葉。

translations.literal: Yong province again obtained a stone diagram, split into two sections, with the form of a poplar tree, yellow roots and green leaves.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong province another stone chart was found, split into two pieces showing the form of a poplar tree with yellow roots and green leaves.

sentences.zh: 汝水得神龜，腹下有文曰「天卜楊興」。

translations.literal: At the Ru River a divine turtle was obtained; beneath its belly was writing saying "Heaven divines Yang's rise."
translations.idiomatic: At the Ru River a divine turtle was found with writing on its belly that read, "Heaven divines the rise of Yang."

sentences.zh: 安邑掘地得古鐵板，文曰「皇始天年，齎楊鐵券，王興」。

translations.literal: At Anyi, digging the earth, an ancient iron plate was obtained; the writing said "Imperial beginning, heavenly year, bearing Yang's iron tally, the king rises."
translations.idiomatic: At Anyi an ancient iron plate was unearthed bearing the inscription, "In the imperial beginning and heavenly year, bearing Yang's iron tally, the king shall rise."

sentences.zh: 同州得石龜，文曰「天子延千年，大吉」。

translations.literal: Tong province obtained a stone turtle; the writing said "The Son of Heaven extends a thousand years, great auspice."
translations.idiomatic: In Tong province a stone turtle was found inscribed with the words, "The Son of Heaven extends his reign a thousand years—great auspice."

sentences.zh: 臣以前之三石，不異《龍圖》。

translations.literal: Your subject considers the three stones above no different from the "Dragon Diagram."
translations.idiomatic: Your subject believes that the three stone charts mentioned above are no different from the "Dragon Diagram."

sentences.zh: 何以用石？

translations.literal: Why use stone?
translations.idiomatic: Why should stone be used?

sentences.zh: 石體久固，義與上名符合。

translations.literal: Stone's substance is long enduring and firm; the meaning matches the Supreme One's name.
translations.idiomatic: Stone is enduring and firm by nature, and its meaning accords with the emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 龜腹七字何以著龜？

translations.literal: Why inscribe the seven characters on the turtle's belly on a turtle?
translations.idiomatic: Why should the seven characters be inscribed on a turtle?

sentences.zh: 龜亦久固，兼是神靈之物。

translations.literal: The turtle is also long enduring and firm, and moreover is a numinous thing.
translations.idiomatic: The turtle is likewise enduring, and moreover is a numinous creature.

sentences.zh: 孔子歎河不出圖，洛不出書。

translations.literal: Confucius lamented that the river did not yield a diagram and the Luo did not yield a book.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius lamented that the Yellow River did not yield a diagram and the Luo did not yield a book.

sentences.zh: 今于大隋聖世，圖書屢出。

translations.literal: Now in the sage age of Great Sui, diagrams and books repeatedly appear.
translations.idiomatic: But in the sage age of Great Sui, such charts and books have appeared again and again.

sentences.zh: 建德六年，亳州大周村有龍鬥，白者勝，黑者死。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiande, at Dazhou village in Bozhou, dragons fought; the white one prevailed, the black one died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiande, at Dazhou village in Bozhou two dragons fought; the white dragon prevailed and the black dragon died.

sentences.zh: 大象元年夏，熒陽汴水北有龍鬥。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Daxiang, north of the Bian River at Yingyang, dragons fought.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the first year of Daxiang, north of the Bian River at Yingyang, dragons were seen fighting.

sentences.zh: 初見白氣屬天，自東方曆陽武而來。

translations.literal: At first white vapor connected with heaven, coming from the east through Liyang and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: At first a white vapor rose to the sky, advancing from the east through Liyang and Wu.

sentences.zh: 及至，白龍也，長十許丈。

translations.literal: When it arrived, it was a white dragon, more than ten zhang in length.
translations.idiomatic: When it drew near, it proved to be a white dragon some thirty meters long.

sentences.zh: 有黑龍乘雲而至，雲雨相薄，乍合乍離，自午至申，白龍升天，黑龍墜地。

translations.literal: A black dragon came riding clouds; clouds and rain pressed together, now joining now separating; from the wu hour to the shen hour the white dragon ascended to heaven and the black dragon fell to earth.
translations.idiomatic: A black dragon came riding the clouds. Cloud and rain closed in upon one another, now joining, now parting. From noon until late afternoon the white dragon rose to heaven and the black dragon crashed to earth.

sentences.zh: 謹案：龍，君象也。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully notes: the dragon is the image of the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully observe that the dragon symbolizes the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 前鬥于亳州周村者，蓋象至尊以龍鬥之歲為亳州總管，遂代周有天下。

translations.literal: The earlier fight at Zhou village in Bozhou surely images the Most Exalted, in the year of the dragon fight made Inspector-General of Bozhou, then replacing Zhou and possessing all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier battle at Zhou village in Bozhou surely foreshadowed His Majesty: in the year of that dragon fight he became inspector-general of Bozhou, then supplanted Zhou and took possession of the realm.

sentences.zh: 後鬥于熒陽者，熒字三火，明火德之盛也。

translations.literal: The later fight at Yingyang: the character ying has three fires, clearly manifesting the fullness of the virtue of fire.
translations.idiomatic: The later battle at Yingyang is significant because the character ying contains three instances of the fire radical, plainly manifesting the fullness of fire's virtue.

sentences.zh: 白龍從東方來，曆陽武者，蓋象至尊將登帝位，從東第入自崇陽門也。

translations.literal: The white dragon came from the east, passing through Liyang and Wu, surely imaging the Most Exalted about to ascend the imperial throne, entering from the Eastern Residence through the Chongyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The white dragon came from the east, passing through Liyang and Wu, and surely foretold His Majesty's ascent to the throne: he would enter from the Eastern Residence through the Chongyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 西北升天者，當乾位天門。

translations.literal: Ascending to heaven in the northwest corresponds to the qian position, the Heavenly Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Its ascent to heaven in the northwest corresponds to the qian trigram's position, the Heavenly Gate.

sentences.zh: 《坤靈圖》曰：「聖人殺龍，龍不可得而殺，皆感氣也。

translations.literal: The 'Kun Ling Tu' says: "The sage slays the dragon; the dragon cannot be slain by killing—all are moved by qi."
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal 'Kun Ling Tu' says, "The sage slays the dragon, yet the dragon cannot truly be killed by force; all such events are stirred by cosmic qi."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「泰，姓商名宮，黃色，長八尺，六十世。

translations.literal: " It also says: "Tai: surname Shang, given name Gong, yellow color, eight chi in height, sixty generations."
translations.idiomatic: It also says, "Tai: surname Shang, given name Gong, yellow in color, eight feet tall, sixty generations."

sentences.zh: 河龍以正月辰見，白龍與五黑龍鬥，白龍陵，故泰人有命。

translations.literal: The river dragon appears in the first month at the chen hour; the white dragon fights five black dragons; the white dragon ling, therefore the people of Tai have the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The river dragon appears in the first month at the chen hour; the white dragon battles five black dragons and prevails, and therefore the people of Tai receive Heaven's Mandate.

sentences.zh: 」謹案此言，皆為大隋而發也。

translations.literal: " Your subject respectfully notes: these words all issue forth for Great Sui.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully observe that every one of these passages was uttered on behalf of Great Sui.

sentences.zh: 「聖人殺龍」者，前後龍死是也。

translations.literal: "The sage slays the dragon" means the earlier and later deaths of the dragons.
translations.idiomatic: "The sage slays the dragon" refers to the deaths of the dragons in the earlier and later battles.

sentences.zh: 「姓商」者，皇家於五姓為商也。

translations.literal: "Surname Shang" means the imperial house among the five surnames is Shang.
translations.idiomatic: "Surname Shang" means that among the five great clans the imperial house belongs to the Shang category.

sentences.zh: 「名宮」者，武元皇帝諱于五聲為宮。

translations.literal: "Given name Gong" means Emperor Wu Yuan's taboo name among the five tones is gong.
translations.idiomatic: "Given name Gong" means that Emperor Wu Yuan's personal name corresponds to the gong note among the five tones.

sentences.zh: 「黃色」者，隋色尚黃。

translations.literal: "Yellow color" means Sui esteems yellow.
translations.idiomatic: "Yellow color" means that Sui honors yellow as its dynastic color.

sentences.zh: 「長八尺」者，武元皇帝身長八尺。

translations.literal: "Eight chi in height" means Emperor Wu Yuan's body was eight chi in height.
translations.idiomatic: "Eight feet tall" refers to Emperor Wu Yuan, who stood eight feet in height.

sentences.zh: 「河龍以正月辰見」者，《泰》，正月卦，龍見之所于京師為辰地。

translations.literal: "The river dragon appears in the first month at the chen hour" means the hexagram Tai is the first-month hexagram; the place where the dragon appears in the capital region is the chen quarter.
translations.idiomatic: "The river dragon appears in the first month at the chen hour" refers to the hexagram Tai, which governs the first month; the site of the dragon's appearance in the capital corresponds to the chen direction.

sentences.zh: 「白龍與黑龍鬥」者，亳州、熒陽龍鬥是也。

translations.literal: "The white dragon fights the black dragon" means the dragon fights at Bozhou and Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: "The white dragon fights the black dragon" refers to the dragon battles at Bozhou and Yingyang.

sentences.zh: 勝龍所以白者，楊姓納音為商，至尊又辛酉歲生，位皆在西方，西方白色也。

translations.literal: The reason the victorious dragon was white: the Yang surname's na-yin tone is shang; the Most Exalted was also born in the xinyou year; their positions are all in the west, and the west's color is white.
translations.idiomatic: The victorious dragon was white because the Yang clan's na-yin classification is shang, His Majesty was born in a xinyou year, and all these associations lie in the west, whose color is white.

sentences.zh: 死龍所以黑者，周色黑。

translations.literal: The reason the dead dragon was black: Zhou's color was black.
translations.idiomatic: The defeated dragon was black because Zhou's dynastic color was black.

sentences.zh: 所以稱五者，周閔、明、武、宣、靖凡五帝；

translations.literal: The reason it says five: the Zhou emperors Min, Ming, Wu, Xuan, and Jing—five emperors in all;
translations.idiomatic: The text speaks of five because there were five Zhou emperors—Min, Ming, Wu, Xuan, and Jing;

sentences.zh: 越、陳、代、越、滕五王一時伏法，亦當五數。

translations.literal: the princes of Yue, Chen, Dai, Yue, and Teng were executed at one time, also matching the number five.
translations.idiomatic: and the princes of Yue, Chen, Dai, Yue, and Teng were executed at the same time, likewise matching the number five.

sentences.zh: 「白龍陵」者，陵猶勝也。

translations.literal: "The white dragon ling": ling is like sheng, victory.
translations.idiomatic: "The white dragon ling" means that ling signifies victory.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄說「陵」當為「除」，凡鬥能去敵曰除。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan said "ling" should read "chu"; in any fight, being able to remove the enemy is called chu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explained that ling should be read as chu, meaning in combat to remove one's foe.

sentences.zh: 臣以「泰人有命」者，泰之為言，通也，大也，明其人道通德大，有天命也。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that "the people of Tai have the Mandate" means tai as a word is tong, penetrating, and da, great—making clear that their human way penetrates and their virtue is great, and they possess Heaven's Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: I take "the people of Tai receive the Mandate" to mean that tai signifies penetration and greatness, showing that their human way is all-encompassing, their virtue is vast, and Heaven's Mandate is theirs.

sentences.zh: 《乾鑿度》曰：「泰表戴幹。

translations.literal: The 'Qian Zao Du' says: "The outward mark of Tai wears the gan."
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal 'Qian Zao Du' says, "The outward mark of the people of Tai wears the Heavenly Stem."

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注云：「表者，人形體之彰識也。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan annotated: "Biao means the outward distinguishing mark of the human form."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan commented, "Biao means the outward distinguishing mark on the human body."

sentences.zh: 幹，盾也。

translations.literal: Gan is a shield.
translations.idiomatic: Gan means a shield.

sentences.zh: 泰人之表，戴幹。

translations.literal: The outward mark of the people of Tai wears the gan.
translations.idiomatic: The outward mark of the people of Tai wears the gan.

sentences.zh: 」臣伏見至尊有戴幹之表，益知泰人之表，不爽毫釐。

translations.literal: " Your subject humbly sees the Most Exalted has the outward mark of wearing the gan, and all the more knows the outward mark of the people of Tai does not miss by a hair's breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has humbly observed that His Majesty bears the mark of wearing the gan on his brow, which proves all the more that the outward mark of the people of Tai is fulfilled to the last detail.

sentences.zh: 《坤靈圖》所雲，字字皆驗。

translations.literal: What the 'Kun Ling Tu' states, character by character, is all verified.
translations.idiomatic: Every word of the 'Kun Ling Tu' has been fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 緯書又稱漢四百年，終如其言，則知六十世亦必然矣。

translations.literal: The weishu also said Han would last four hundred years, and in the end it was as spoken; thus one knows sixty generations is likewise inevitable.
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal books also predicted that Han would endure four hundred years, and events proved them right; we may therefore be certain that sixty generations will likewise come to pass.

sentences.zh: 昔宗周卜世三十，今則倍之。

translations.literal: Formerly the Zhou of the clan divined thirty generations; now it is doubled.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou of old divined thirty generations for their house; now the span is doubled.

sentences.zh: 《稽覽圖》曰：「太平時，陰陽和合，風雨會同，海內不偏。

translations.literal: The 'Ji Lan Tu' says: "In the age of Great Peace, yin and yang harmonize, wind and rain meet together, and within the seas there is no partiality."
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal 'Ji Lan Tu' says, "In an age of Great Peace, yin and yang are in harmony, wind and rain arrive together, and nothing within the seas is partial."

sentences.zh: 地有阻險，故風有遲疾。

translations.literal: The land has barriers and peril, therefore wind has slowness and swiftness.
translations.idiomatic: Because the land has barriers and rugged terrain, the wind blows now slowly, now swiftly.

sentences.zh: 雖太平之政猶有不能均，惟平均乃不鳴條，故欲風於亳。

translations.literal: Even under the government of Great Peace there are still places that cannot be made even; only when averaged is there no stirring of the branches, therefore one desires wind at Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Even under a government of Great Peace some regions cannot be made perfectly even; only when all is balanced do the branches cease to stir, and therefore the text desires wind at Bo.

sentences.zh: 亳者陳留也。

translations.literal: Bo is Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Bo is another name for Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 」謹案此言，蓋明至尊昔為陳留公世子，亳州總管，遂受天命，海內均同，不偏不党，以成太平之風化也。

translations.literal: " Your subject respectfully notes: these words surely make clear the Most Exalted was formerly heir of the Duke of Chenliu and Inspector-General of Bozhou, then received Heaven's Mandate; within the seas all were alike, without partiality or faction, thereby completing the transforming influence of Great Peace.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully observe that this passage shows how His Majesty was once heir to the Duke of Chenliu and inspector-general of Bozhou, then received Heaven's Mandate; the realm was made uniform, without partiality or faction, and the transforming influence of Great Peace was thereby fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 在大統十六年，武元皇帝改封陳留公。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Datong, Emperor Wu Yuan was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Datong, Emperor Wu Yuan was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 是時，齊國有秘記云：「天王陳留入并州。

translations.literal: At that time Qi had a secret record saying: "The Heavenly King of Chenliu enters Bing province."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qi possessed a secret prophecy saying, "The Heavenly King of Chenliu will enter Bing province."

sentences.zh: 」齊主高洋為是誅陳留王彭樂。

translations.literal: " For this the ruler of Qi, Gao Yang, executed the Prince of Chenliu, Peng Le.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this prophecy, the Qi ruler Gao Yang executed Peng Le, Prince of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 其後，武元皇帝果將兵入并州。

translations.literal: Afterward, Emperor Wu Yuan indeed led troops into Bing province.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Emperor Wu Yuan did indeed lead troops into Bing province.

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，望氣者云「亳州有天子氣」，於是殺亳州刺史紇豆陵恭。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou, observers of qi said "Bozhou has the qi of a Son of Heaven," and thereupon the Inspector of Bozhou, Hedouling Gong, was killed.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Wu of Zhou, diviners of cosmic qi reported that Bozhou bore the aura of an emperor, and the inspector of Bozhou, Hedouling Gong, was therefore executed.

sentences.zh: 至尊代為之。

translations.literal: The Most Exalted replaced him in the post.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty then took his place as inspector.

sentences.zh: 又陳留老子祠有枯柏，世傳云老子將度世，云：「待枯柏生東南枝，回指，當有聖人出，吾道復行。

translations.literal: Moreover, at the Laozi shrine in Chenliu there was a withered cypress; the world transmitted that when Laozi was about to transcend the world he said: "Wait until the withered cypress puts forth a southeast branch that turns back and points—then a sage will appear and my Way will flourish again."
translations.idiomatic: At the Laozi shrine in Chenliu there also stood a withered cypress. Tradition held that when Laozi was about to leave the world he said, "Wait until this withered cypress puts forth a southeast branch that turns back and points—then a sage will appear and my Way will flourish again."

sentences.zh: 」至齊，枯柏從下生枝，東南上指，夜有三童子相與歌曰：「老子廟前古枯樹，東南枝如傘，聖主從此去。

translations.literal: " When Qi came, the withered cypress sprouted branches from below, pointing up to the southeast; at night three boys together sang: "Before Laozi's temple, the ancient withered tree—its southeast branch like an umbrella; the sage lord departs from here."
translations.idiomatic: When Qi ruled, the withered cypress sprouted new branches from its base, pointing toward the southeast. One night three boys sang together, "Before Laozi's temple stands an ancient withered tree; its southeast branch spreads like an umbrella—the sage lord will depart from here."

sentences.zh: 」及至尊牧亳州，親至祠樹之下，自是柏枝回抱，其枯枝漸指西北，道教果行。

translations.literal: " When the Most Exalted governed Bozhou he personally came beneath the shrine tree; from then on the cypress branches turned back and embraced, its withered branches gradually pointed northwest, and the Way of the Dao indeed flourished.
translations.idiomatic: When His Majesty governed Bozhou he came in person to the shrine tree. From that moment the cypress branches turned back upon themselves, the withered limbs gradually pointed northwest, and the Daoist teaching did indeed flourish again.

sentences.zh: 考校眾事，太平主出於亳州陳留之地，皆如所言。

translations.literal: Examining and comparing the many affairs, the lord of Great Peace issuing from the lands of Bozhou and Chenliu—all were as spoken.
translations.idiomatic: When one compares all these events, the lord of Great Peace arising from Bozhou and Chenliu fulfilled every prophecy.

sentences.zh: 《稽覽圖》又云：「政道得，則陰物變為陽物。

translations.literal: The 'Ji Lan Tu' also says: "When the way of government is attained, yin things change into yang things."
translations.idiomatic: The 'Ji Lan Tu' also says, "When the way of government is fully realized, yin things are transformed into yang things."

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注云：「蔥變為韭，亦是。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan annotated: "Scallions changing into leeks is also such a case."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan commented that scallions turning into leeks is another example of the same phenomenon.

sentences.zh: 」謹案自六年以來，遠近山石多變為玉。

translations.literal: " Your subject respectfully notes: since the sixth year, near and far, mountain stones have largely changed into jade.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully observe that since the sixth year stones throughout the realm, near and far, have in many cases turned into jade.

sentences.zh: 石為陰，玉為陽。

translations.literal: Stone is yin; jade is yang.
translations.idiomatic: Stone belongs to yin; jade belongs to yang.

sentences.zh: 又左衛園中，蔥皆變為韭。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the garden of the Left Guard, all scallions changed into leeks.
translations.idiomatic: In the garden of the Left Guard as well, every scallion plant turned into leek.

sentences.zh: 上覽之大悅，賜物五百段。

translations.literal: The emperor, on reading this, was greatly pleased and bestowed five hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial with great delight and rewarded him with five hundred lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 未幾，劭復上書曰：

translations.literal: Before long, Shao again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shao submitted another memorial, saying:
