sentences.zh: 《易·乾鑿度》曰：「《隨》，上六，拘系之，乃從維之，王用享於西山。

translations.literal: The 'Changes: Qian Zao Du' says: "Sui, upper six: 'Bound and tied—then follow and maintain it; the king uses it to offer sacrifice at the Western Mountain.'"
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal 'Qian Zao Du' attached to the Changes says of the hexagram Sui, line six at the top: "Bound and tied—then follow and maintain it; the king uses it to offer sacrifice at the Western Mountain."

sentences.zh: 《隨》者，二月卦。

translations.literal: Sui is the second-month hexagram.
translations.idiomatic: Sui is the hexagram of the second month.

sentences.zh: 陽德施行，蕃決難解，萬物隨陽而出。

translations.literal: The yang virtue is put into practice; frontier barriers are opened and difficulties dissolved; the ten thousand things follow yang and emerge.
translations.idiomatic: Yang virtue is put into practice, frontier barriers are opened and hardships dissolved, and the ten thousand things emerge following the yang force.

sentences.zh: 故上六欲九五拘系之，維持之，明被陽化而欲陰隨從之也。

translations.literal: Therefore upper six desires that nine in the fifth place bind and tie it, maintain it—making clear that having received yang's transformation, yin wishes to follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the top line desires that the fifth line bind and tie it and maintain it—showing that, having been transformed by yang, yin wishes to follow in its train.

sentences.zh: 」《易·稽覽圖》：「《坤》六月，有子女任政，一年傳為《復》。

translations.literal: " The 'Changes: Ji Lan Tu': "Kun, sixth month: there are sons and daughters holding government; after one year it passes to Fu."
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal 'Ji Lan Tu' says, "Kun, the sixth month: sons and daughters hold power; after one year the mandate passes to Fu."

sentences.zh: 五月，貧之從東北來立，大起土邑；

translations.literal: Fifth month: pin zhi comes from the northeast to establish rule, greatly raising earthen cities;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the true man comes from the northeast to take the throne and greatly raises earthen cities;

sentences.zh: 西北地動星墜，陽衛。

translations.literal: in the northwest the earth quakes and stars fall; yang guards.
translations.idiomatic: in the northwest the earth quakes and stars fall, and Yang receives Heaven's protection.

sentences.zh: 《屯》十一月，神人從中山出，趙地動；

translations.literal: Tun, eleventh month: a divine man comes forth from Zhongshan; Zhao lands quake;
translations.idiomatic: Tun, the eleventh month: a divine man comes forth from Zhongshan and the lands of Zhao tremble;

sentences.zh: 北方三十日，千里馬數至。

translations.literal: in the north for thirty days, thousand-li horses arrive repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: for thirty days in the north, thousand-li horses arrive again and again.

sentences.zh: 」謹案：凡此《易緯》所言，皆是大隋符命。

translations.literal: " Your subject respectfully notes: all that these 'Yi Wei' texts speak of are the validating mandates of Great Sui.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully observe that everything these apocryphal texts on the Changes proclaim concerns the validating portents of Great Sui.

sentences.zh: 《隨》者，二月之卦，明大隋以二月即皇帝位也。

translations.literal: Sui is the hexagram of the second month, making clear that Great Sui assumed the imperial throne in the second month.
translations.idiomatic: Sui is the hexagram of the second month, showing that Great Sui assumed the imperial throne in the second month.

sentences.zh: 「陽德施行」者，明楊氏之德教施行於天下也。

translations.literal: "The yang virtue is put into practice" makes clear the Yang clan's virtue and teaching are put into practice throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: "Yang virtue is put into practice" shows that the Yang clan's moral teaching was spread throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 「蕃決難解」者，明當時蕃鄣皆通決，險難皆解散也。

translations.literal: "Frontier barriers are opened and difficulties dissolved" makes clear that at the time all frontier barriers were opened and cleared, and perils and hardships were all dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: "Frontier barriers are opened and hardships dissolved" means that at the time every frontier barrier was opened and every hardship removed.

sentences.zh: 「萬物隨陽而出」者，明天地間萬物盡隨楊氏而出見也。

translations.literal: "The ten thousand things follow yang and emerge" makes clear that throughout heaven and earth the ten thousand things all followed the Yang clan and came forth to be seen.
translations.idiomatic: "The ten thousand things emerge following yang" means that throughout the realm everything emerged under the Yang clan's rule.

sentences.zh: 「上六欲九五拘系之」者，五為王，六為宗廟，明宗廟神靈欲命登九五之位，帝王拘人以禮，系人以義也。

translations.literal: "Upper six desires that nine in the fifth place bind and tie it" means five is the king, six is the ancestral temple—making clear the ancestral temple spirits wished to command ascent to the position of nine-five; the emperor-king binds people by ritual and ties people by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: "The top line desires that the fifth line bind and tie it" means that five signifies the king and six the ancestral temple, showing that the imperial ancestors wished him to ascend the throne; the emperor binds his subjects through ritual and holds them through righteousness.

sentences.zh: 「拘人以禮，系人以義」，此二旬，亦是《乾鑿度》之言。

translations.literal: "Binding people by ritual, tying people by righteousness"—these two phrases are also words of the 'Qian Zao Du.'
translations.idiomatic: "Binding people through ritual and holding them through righteousness"—these two phrases also come from the 'Qian Zao Du.'

sentences.zh: 「維持之」者，明能以綱維持正天下也。

translations.literal: "Maintaining it" makes clear that one is able by the guiding net to maintain and set right all under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: "Maintaining it" shows that he was able to uphold and set right the realm through its governing principles.

sentences.zh: 」被陽化而欲陰隨從之」者，明諸陰類被服楊氏之風化，莫不隨從。

translations.literal: "Having received yang's transformation and wishing yin to follow" makes clear that all yin categories, having received the Yang clan's transforming influence, none failed to follow.
translations.idiomatic: "Having been transformed by yang and wishing yin to follow" means that every yin element, having received the Yang clan's civilizing influence, followed without exception.

sentences.zh: 陰，謂臣下也。

translations.literal: Yin means subordinates and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Yin here refers to ministers and subjects.

sentences.zh: 「王用享於西山」者，蓋明至尊常以歲二月幸西山仁壽宮也。

translations.literal: "The king uses it to offer sacrifice at the Western Mountain" surely makes clear the Most Exalted often in the second month of the year visits the Western Mountain and Renshou Palace.
translations.idiomatic: "The king uses it to offer sacrifice at the Western Mountain" surely refers to His Majesty's custom of visiting the Western Mountain and Renshou Palace every year in the second month.

sentences.zh: 凡四稱「隨」，三稱「陽」，欲美隨楊，丁寧之至也。

translations.literal: In all, sui is named four times and yang three times—wishing to beautify following Yang, to the utmost of earnest repetition.
translations.idiomatic: The text names sui four times and yang three times, lavishing praise on following the Yang clan with the utmost earnest repetition.

sentences.zh: 「《坤》六月」者，坤位在未，六月建未，言至尊以六月生也。

translations.literal: "Kun, sixth month" means kun's position is at wei; the sixth month is established at wei—speaking of the Most Exalted being born in the sixth month.
translations.idiomatic: "Kun, the sixth month" means that kun occupies the wei position and the sixth month is keyed to wei, indicating that His Majesty was born in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 「有子女任政」者，言樂平公主是皇帝子女，而為周後，任理內政也。

translations.literal: "There are sons and daughters holding government" means the Princess of Yueping was the emperor's daughter, yet became empress of Zhou and undertook to govern internal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: "Sons and daughters hold power" refers to the Princess of Yueping, who was the emperor's daughter, became empress of Zhou, and managed internal affairs.

sentences.zh: 「一年傳為《復》」者，《復》是《坤》之一世卦，陽氣初起，言周宣帝崩後一年，傳位與楊氏也。

translations.literal: "After one year it passes to Fu" means Fu is one of Kun's cycle hexagrams, yang qi first arising—speaking of one year after Emperor Xuan of Zhou's death, the throne passing to the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: "After one year the mandate passes to Fu" means that Fu is one of Kun's cycle hexagrams, when yang force first stirs—referring to the transfer of power to the Yang clan one year after Emperor Xuan of Zhou died.

sentences.zh: 「五月，貧之從東北來立」，「貧之」當為「真人」，字之誤也。

translations.literal: "In the fifth month, pin zhi comes from the northeast to establish rule"—"pin zhi" should be "true man," a mistaken character.
translations.idiomatic: "In the fifth month the true man comes from the northeast to take the throne"—the characters pin zhi are a scribal error for zhenren, "true man."

sentences.zh: 言周宣帝以五月崩，真人革命，當在此時。

translations.literal: It speaks of Emperor Xuan of Zhou dying in the fifth month; the true man's revolution ought to be at this time.
translations.idiomatic: It means that Emperor Xuan of Zhou died in the fifth month and that the true man's revolution ought to have taken place at that moment.

sentences.zh: 至尊謙讓而逆天意，故逾年乃立。

translations.literal: The Most Exalted was modest and yielding and went against Heaven's intent, therefore only after more than a year did he establish rule.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty, out of modesty, defied Heaven's intent and therefore did not take the throne until more than a year had passed.

sentences.zh: 昔為定州總管，在京師東北，本而言之，故曰「真人從東北來立」。

translations.literal: Formerly he was Inspector-General of Ding province, northeast of the capital—speaking from the root of the matter, therefore it says "the true man comes from the northeast to establish rule."
translations.idiomatic: He had formerly served as inspector-general of Ding province, which lies northeast of the capital; speaking in fundamental terms, this is why the text says "the true man comes from the northeast to take the throne."

sentences.zh: 「大起土邑」者，大起，即大興城邑也。

translations.literal: "Greatly raising earthen cities" means da qi, that is, greatly raising the city of Daxing.
translations.idiomatic: "Greatly raising earthen cities" means the founding of the great capital at Daxing.

sentences.zh: 「西北地動星墜」者，蓋天意去周授隋，故變動也。

translations.literal: "In the northwest the earth quakes and stars fall" surely means Heaven's intent departed from Zhou and bestowed on Sui, therefore there was change and movement.
translations.idiomatic: "In the northwest the earth quakes and stars fall" surely signifies Heaven's intent to remove Zhou and bestow the mandate on Sui, hence these disturbances.

sentences.zh: 「陽衛」者，言楊氏得天衛助也。

translations.literal: "Yang guards" means the Yang clan received Heaven's guard and assistance.
translations.idiomatic: "Yang guards" means that the Yang clan received Heaven's protection.

sentences.zh: 「《屯》，十一月，神人從中山出」者，此卦動而大亨作，故至尊以十一月被授亳州總管，將從中山而出也。

translations.literal: "Tun, eleventh month, a divine man comes forth from Zhongshan" means this hexagram stirs and great prosperity is achieved; therefore the Most Exalted in the eleventh month was appointed Inspector-General of Bozhou and was about to come forth from Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: "Tun, the eleventh month, a divine man comes forth from Zhongshan" refers to a hexagram of stirring motion and great prosperity; accordingly, in the eleventh month His Majesty was appointed inspector-general of Bozhou and was about to depart from Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 「趙地動」者，中山為趙地，以神人將去，故變動也。

translations.literal: "Zhao lands quake" means Zhongshan is Zhao territory; because the divine man was about to depart, therefore there was change and movement.
translations.idiomatic: "The lands of Zhao tremble" means that because Zhongshan lies in Zhao territory and the divine man was about to depart, the region was shaken.

sentences.zh: 「北方三十日」者，蓋至尊從北方將往亳州之時，停留三十日也。

translations.literal: "In the north for thirty days" surely means when the Most Exalted was going from the north toward Bozhou, he halted for thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: "For thirty days in the north" refers to the thirty days His Majesty paused while traveling from the north toward Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 「千里馬」者，蓋至尊舊所乘騧騮馬也。

translations.literal: "Thousand-li horses" surely means the piebald horses the Most Exalted formerly rode.
translations.idiomatic: "Thousand-li horses" refers to the piebald horses His Majesty once rode.

sentences.zh: 《屯》卦，震下坎上，震于馬為作足，坎于馬為美脊，是故騧馬脊有肉鞍，行則先作弄四足也。

translations.literal: The hexagram Tun has zhen below and kan above; for horses zhen is moving feet, kan is beautiful back—therefore the piebald horse's back has a fleshy saddle, and when walking it first moves and plays with all four feet.
translations.idiomatic: In the hexagram Tun, zhen lies below and kan above; for horses zhen signifies moving feet and kan a fine back—hence the piebald horse's back bears a fleshy saddle, and when it walks it first lifts and plays with all four feet.

sentences.zh: 「數至」者，言歷數至也。

translations.literal: "Arrive repeatedly" means the dynastic count has arrived.
translations.idiomatic: "Arrive repeatedly" means that the dynastic cycle had reached its appointed moment.

sentences.zh: 《河圖·帝通紀》曰：「形瑞出，變矩衡。

translations.literal: The 'Hetu: Di Tong Ji' says: "Formed auspices emerge; the square and balance are changed."
translations.idiomatic: The 'River Chart: Imperial Succession Record' says, "Auspicious forms appear and the measures of rule are transformed."

sentences.zh: 赤應隨，葉靈皇。

translations.literal: The red responds and follows; the leaf, the numinous emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The red omen follows in response; the numinous emperor arises like a leaf.

sentences.zh: 」《河圖·皇參持》曰：「皇辟出，承元訖。

translations.literal: " The 'Hetu: Huang Can Chi' says: "The imperial sovereign emerges; he receives the primordial and brings it to completion."
translations.idiomatic: The 'River Chart: Imperial Canopy Held' says, "The imperial sovereign emerges and receives the primordial beginning through to its completion."

sentences.zh: 道無為，安率。

translations.literal: The Way is non-active; peacefully he leads.
translations.idiomatic: The Way is without forced action; he leads the realm in peace.

sentences.zh: 被遂矩，戲作術。

translations.literal: Clothed in sui ju, playfully he makes methods.
translations.idiomatic: Clothed in the measures of sui, he playfully establishes methods of rule.

sentences.zh: 開皇色，握神日。

translations.literal: Kaihuang's color; he grasps the divine sun.
translations.idiomatic: The color of Kaihuang; he grasps the divine sun.

sentences.zh: 投輔提，象不絕。

translations.literal: He casts fu ti; the image does not cease.
translations.idiomatic: He casts forth his assistants; the imperial image does not perish.

sentences.zh: 立皇后，翼不格。

translations.literal: He establishes the empress; the wings do not overstep.
translations.idiomatic: He establishes the empress, and his supporting ministers do not overstep their stations.

sentences.zh: 道終始，德優劣。

translations.literal: The Way ends and begins; virtue superior and inferior.
translations.idiomatic: The Way has its end and beginning; virtue knows superiority and inferiority.

sentences.zh: 帝任政，河典出。

translations.literal: The emperor personally undertakes government; the river classic emerges.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally governs; the river classic appears.

sentences.zh: 葉輔嬉，爛可述。

translations.literal: Leaves assist, rise; splendid can be recounted.
translations.idiomatic: Aid unites and rises; glory fit to be recorded.

sentences.zh: 」謹案：凡此《河圖》所言，亦是大隋符命。

translations.literal: " Your subject respectfully notes: all that the 'Hetu' speaks here is likewise Great Sui's token of the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully observe that everything spoken here in the River Chart is likewise a prophecy of Great Sui's Mandate.

sentences.zh: 「形瑞出，變矩衡」者，矩，法也；

translations.literal: "When forms and omens emerge, the square and balance change": ju means law;
translations.idiomatic: "When forms and omens emerge, the square and balance change"—ju means law;

sentences.zh: 衡，北斗星名，所謂璿璣玉衡者也。

translations.literal: heng is the name of a star in the Northern Dipper, what is called the xuanji and jade balance.
translations.idiomatic: heng is the name of a Northern Dipper star—the xuanji and jade balance of astronomical lore.

sentences.zh: 大隋受命，形兆之瑞始出，天象則為之變動。

translations.literal: Great Sui received the Mandate; omens of form and sign first emerged, and the heavenly phenomena thereupon changed for it.
translations.idiomatic: When Great Sui received the Mandate, prophetic signs first appeared, and the heavens altered their courses accordingly.

sentences.zh: 北斗主天之法度，故曰矩衡。

translations.literal: The Northern Dipper governs heaven's laws and measures, hence it is called ju-heng.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Dipper presides over heaven's laws and measures, hence the term ju-heng, square and balance.

sentences.zh: 《易緯》：「伏戲，矩衡神。

translations.literal: The 'Yi Wei' says: "Fuxi, god of square and balance.
translations.idiomatic: The apocryphal 'Yi Wei' says, "Fuxi, god of square and balance.

sentences.zh: 」鄭玄注，以為法玉衡之神。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan's commentary takes it as the spirit that governs the jade balance.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary interprets this as the spirit governing the jade balance.

sentences.zh: 與此《河圖》矩衡義同。

translations.literal: The meaning of ju-heng is the same as in this 'Hetu.'
translations.idiomatic: This matches the meaning of ju-heng in the River Chart.

sentences.zh: 「赤應隨」者，言赤帝降精，感應而生隋也。

translations.literal: "Red responds and follows" means that the Red Emperor descended essence, moved by response to give birth to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: "Red responds and follows" signifies that the Red Emperor descended his essence, and by sympathetic response Sui was born.

sentences.zh: 故隋以火德為赤帝天子。

translations.literal: Therefore Sui, with the virtue of fire, is the Son of Heaven of the Red Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Sui, possessing fire's virtue, is son of heaven to the Red Emperor.

sentences.zh: 「葉靈皇」者，葉，合也，言大隋德合上靈天皇大帝也。

translations.literal: "Ye ling huang": ye means unite; it says Great Sui's virtue united with the Great Spirit Heaven Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: "Ye ling huang"—ye means unite—signifies that Great Sui's virtue joined with the Great Spirit Heaven Emperor.

sentences.zh: 又年號開皇，與《靈寶經》之開皇年相合，故曰葉靈皇。

translations.literal: Moreover the era-name Kaihuang joins with the Kaihuang year of the 'Lingbao Jing,' hence it is called ye ling huang.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore the era-name Kaihuang coincides with the Kaihuang year in the Scripture of the Numinous Treasure, hence the phrase ye ling huang.

sentences.zh: 「皇辟出」者，皇，大也；

translations.literal: "The august sovereign emerges": huang means great;
translations.idiomatic: "The august sovereign emerges"—huang means great;

sentences.zh: 辟，君也。

translations.literal: bi means lord.
translations.idiomatic: bi means sovereign.

sentences.zh: 大君出，蓋謂至尊受命出為天子也。

translations.literal: The great lord emerges—this surely means the Most Exalted received the Mandate and emerged as Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The great sovereign emerges—this surely foretells His Majesty receiving the Mandate and ascending as son of heaven.

sentences.zh: 「承元訖」者，言承周天元終訖之運也。

translations.literal: "Receiving the primal cycle to its end" means inheriting the fortune of heaven's primal cycle coming to completion.
translations.idiomatic: "Receiving the primal cycle to its end" means inheriting the cosmic cycle as heaven's primal period reaches its close.

sentences.zh: 「道無為，安率」者，「安」下脫一字，言大道無為，安定，天下率從。

translations.literal: "The Way is non-active, peace leads": below "an" one character is missing; it says the Great Way is non-active, settled in peace, and all under heaven follows in obedience.
translations.idiomatic: "The Way is non-active, peace leads"—one character is missing after "peace"—and signifies that the Great Way acts without forcing, the realm is settled, and all under heaven follows obediently.

sentences.zh: 「被遂矩，戲作術」者，矩，法也，昔遂皇握機矩，伏戲作八卦之術，言大隋被服彼二皇之法術也。

translations.literal: "Clad in Sui's square, Xi devised the method": ju means law; in antiquity Sovereign Sui grasped the pivot-square, Fuxi devised the method of the eight trigrams; it says Great Sui wears those two sovereigns' laws and arts.
translations.idiomatic: "Clad in Sui's square, Xi devised the method"—ju means law—recalling how Sovereign Sui once grasped the cosmic pivot and Fuxi devised the eight trigrams: Great Sui now inherits both sovereigns' laws and arts.

sentences.zh: 「遂皇機矩」，語見《易緯》。

translations.literal: "Sovereign Sui's pivot-square"—the phrase appears in the 'Yi Wei.'
translations.idiomatic: "Sovereign Sui's pivot-square" is a phrase found in the 'Yi Wei.'

sentences.zh: 「開皇色」者，言開皇年易服色也。

translations.literal: "Kaihuang color" means in the Kaihuang year the ceremonial colors were changed.
translations.idiomatic: "Kaihuang color" refers to the change of court vestments in the Kaihuang era.

sentences.zh: 「握神日」者，言握持群神，明照如日也。

translations.literal: "Grasping the gods, the sun" means grasping and holding the host of spirits, bright as the sun.
translations.idiomatic: "Grasping the gods, the sun" signifies holding the host of spirits in hand, brilliant as the sun itself.

sentences.zh: 又開皇以來日漸長，亦其義也。

translations.literal: Moreover since Kaihuang the days have gradually lengthened—this too is its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, since the Kaihuang era the days have gradually lengthened, which likewise fulfills this prophecy.

sentences.zh: 「投輔提」者，言投授政事於輔佐，使之提挈也。

translations.literal: "Cast to the assist, raise" means casting and entrusting government affairs to assistants, making them raise and lead.
translations.idiomatic: "Cast to the assist, raise" means entrusting governance to his ministers and empowering them to lead.

sentences.zh: 「象不絕」者，法象不廢絕也。

translations.literal: "Images not cut off" means the emblems of law are not abolished or severed.
translations.idiomatic: "Images not cut off" means that the symbolic patterns of governance endure unbroken.

sentences.zh: 「立皇后，翼不格」者，格，至也，言本立太子以為皇家後嗣，而其輔翼之人不能至於善也。

translations.literal: "Establish the empress, wings do not arrive": ge means arrive; it says originally the crown prince was established as the imperial house's successor, yet those winging him could not arrive at goodness.
translations.idiomatic: "Establish the empress, wings do not arrive"—ge meaning to reach—signifies that though a crown prince was installed as heir, those who should have supported him failed to achieve virtue.

sentences.zh: 「道終始，德優劣」者，言前東宮道終而德劣，今皇太子道始而德優也。

translations.literal: "The Way ends and begins, virtue superior and inferior" means the former Eastern Palace's Way had ended and virtue was inferior; now the crown prince's Way begins and virtue is superior.
translations.idiomatic: "The Way ends and begins, virtue superior and inferior" means the former crown prince's path had ended and his virtue was wanting, whereas the present crown prince's path begins and his virtue excels.

sentences.zh: 「帝任政，河典出」者，言皇帝親任政事，而邵州河濱得石圖也。

translations.literal: "The emperor personally undertakes government, the river classic emerges" means the emperor personally undertook government affairs, and at Shao prefecture on the river bank the stone chart was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor personally governs, the river classic emerges" means that the emperor took government into his own hands and that a stone River Chart was discovered on the banks of the river at Shao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 「葉輔嬉，爛可述」者，葉，合也；

translations.literal: "Ye assists, rises, splendid can be recounted": ye means unite;
translations.idiomatic: "Ye assists, rises, splendid can be recounted"—ye means unite;

sentences.zh: 嬉，興也。

translations.literal: xi means rise.
translations.idiomatic: xi means flourish.

sentences.zh: 言群臣合心輔佐，以興政教，爛然可紀述也。

translations.literal: It says the ministers united in heart to assist, thereby raising government and teaching, splendidly fit for recording.
translations.idiomatic: It signifies that the ministers united in purpose to support him, raising governance and instruction to a brilliance worth recording.

sentences.zh: 所以於《皇參持》、《帝通紀》二篇，大陳符命者，明皇道帝德盡在於隋也。

translations.literal: Therefore in the two chapters 'Huang Can Chi' and 'Di Tong Ji' he greatly displayed the tokens of the Mandate to make clear that the royal Way and imperial virtue all reside in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Hence in the two chapters 'Huang Can Chi' and 'Di Tong Ji' he laid out the prophecies at length to demonstrate that the royal Way and imperial virtue all belong to Sui.

sentences.zh: 上大悅，以劭至誠，寵錫日隆。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased; because Shao was utterly sincere, favor and gifts daily grew.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased. Finding Shao utterly sincere, he lavished ever greater favor and gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 時有人于黃鳳泉浴，得二白石，頗有文理。

translations.literal: At that time someone bathing at Huangfeng Spring obtained two white stones with considerable pattern and text.
translations.idiomatic: About that time a man bathing at Yellow Phoenix Spring found two white stones marked with considerable patterns and inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 遂附其文以為字，復言有諸物象，而上奏曰：「其大玉有日月、星辰、八卦、五嶽及二麟、雙鳳、青龍、硃雀、騶虞、玄武，各當其方位。

translations.literal: He thereupon attached their markings as characters, further declaring various object-images were present, and memorialized: "The larger jade has sun, moon, stars, the eight trigrams, the five sacred peaks, two qilin, paired phoenixes, azure dragon, vermilion bird, zouyu, black tortoise—each in its proper position.
translations.idiomatic: He then construed their markings as written characters, claimed further that they bore images of various auspicious creatures, and memorialized: "The larger stone bears the sun, moon, stars, the eight trigrams, the five sacred peaks, two qilin, paired phoenixes, the azure dragon, vermilion bird, zouyu, and black tortoise—each positioned in its proper place.

sentences.zh: 又有五行、十日、十二辰之各，凡二十七字。

translations.literal: There are also the five phases, ten days, and twelve chronograms—twenty-seven characters in all.
translations.idiomatic: It also bears the five phases, the ten heavenly stems, and the twelve earthly branches—twenty-seven characters in all.

sentences.zh: 又有'天門、地戶、人門、鬼門閉'九字。

translations.literal: There are also nine characters: 'Heaven Gate, Earth Door, Human Gate, Ghost Gate closed.'
translations.idiomatic: There are also nine characters reading 'Heaven Gate, Earth Door, Human Gate, Ghost Gate closed.'

sentences.zh: 又有卻非及二鳥。

translations.literal: There are also quefei and two birds.
translations.idiomatic: There are also quefei demons and two birds.

sentences.zh: 其鳥皆人面，則《抱樸子》所謂千秋萬歲者也。

translations.literal: These birds all have human faces—the so-called "thousand autumns, ten thousand years" of the 'Baopuzi.'
translations.idiomatic: These birds all bear human faces—the creatures called "thousand autumns, ten thousand years" in the 'Baopuzi.'

sentences.zh: 其小玉亦有五嶽、卻非、虯、犀之象。

translations.literal: The smaller jade also has images of the five peaks, quefei, dragons, and rhinoceroses.
translations.idiomatic: The smaller stone likewise bears the five peaks, quefei, dragons, and rhinoceroses.

sentences.zh: 二玉俱有仙人玉女乘雲控鶴之象。

translations.literal: Both jades alike have images of transcendent maidens riding clouds and guiding cranes.
translations.idiomatic: Both stones alike depict immortals and jade maidens riding clouds and guiding cranes.

sentences.zh: 別有異狀諸神，不可盡識，蓋是風伯、雨師、山精、海若之類。

translations.literal: Separately there are various gods of strange forms, impossible to identify fully—presumably wind lords, rain masters, mountain spirits, sea gods, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Other strange divine figures appear as well, too many to identify—presumably wind lords, rain masters, mountain spirits, sea gods, and such beings.

sentences.zh: 又有天皇大帝、皇帝及四帝坐，鉤陳、北斗、三公、天將軍、土司空、老人、天倉、南河、北河、五星、二十八宿凡四十五官。

translations.literal: There are also the Great Heaven Emperor, the Emperor, and the seats of the Four Emperors, Gouchen, Northern Dipper, Three Dukes, Heavenly General, Earth Minister, Old Man, Heavenly Granary, Southern River, Northern River, Five Stars, and Twenty-Eight Lodges—forty-five asterisms in all.
translations.idiomatic: It also depicts the Great Heaven Emperor, the Emperor, the thrones of the Four Emperors, Gouchen, the Northern Dipper, the Three Dukes, Heavenly General, Earth Minister, Old Man Star, Heavenly Granary, Southern River, Northern River, the five planets, and the twenty-eight lodges—forty-five celestial offices in all.

sentences.zh: 諸字本無行伍，皆往往偶對。

translations.literal: The characters originally had no ranks or files; they were merely often paired by chance.
translations.idiomatic: The characters originally had no fixed order; they merely happened to fall into paired arrangements.

sentences.zh: 于大玉則有皇帝日名，並臨南面，與日字正鼎足。

translations.literal: On the great jade there is the emperor's sun-name, both overlooking the south face, forming a tripod with the character for sun.
translations.idiomatic: On the larger stone appear the emperor's name and the character for sun, both facing south in a tripartite arrangement with the sun character.

sentences.zh: 復有老人星，蓋明南面象日，而長壽也。

translations.literal: There is again the Old Man star, surely making clear the south-facing image of the sun and long life.
translations.idiomatic: The Old Man star appears as well, evidently signifying that the south-facing sun image portends longevity.

sentences.zh: 皇后二字在西，上有月形，蓋明象月也。

translations.literal: The two characters for empress are in the west, above them a moon shape, surely making clear the image of the moon.
translations.idiomatic: The two characters for empress lie to the west, with a moon shape above them, plainly signifying the moon.

sentences.zh: 于次玉，則皇帝名與九千字次比，兩楊字與萬年字次比，隋與吉字正並，蓋明長久吉慶也。

translations.literal: On the secondary jade the emperor's name and the nine-thousand-character follow in sequence; the two Yang characters and the ten-thousand-years character follow in sequence; Sui and the auspicious character stand directly beside each other—surely making clear lasting fortune and celebration.
translations.idiomatic: On the smaller stone the emperor's name follows the nine-thousand character in sequence; the two instances of Yang follow the ten-thousand-years character; Sui stands directly beside the auspicious character—evidently portending enduring fortune and celebration.

sentences.zh: 」劭復回互其字，作詩二百八十篇奏之。

translations.literal: " Shao again rearranged the characters and composed two hundred eighty poems, which he presented.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then recombined the characters and composed two hundred eighty poems, which he presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上以為誠，賜帛千匹。

translations.literal: The emperor considered it sincere and bestowed a thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as proof of sincerity and rewarded him with a thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 劭於是采人間歌謠，引圖書讖緯，依約符命，捃摭佛經，撰為《皇隋靈感志》合三十卷，奏之。

translations.literal: Shao thereupon gathered folk songs from among the people, cited charts, books, prophecies, and weft texts, drew upon tokens of the Mandate, collected Buddhist sutras, and compiled the 'Huang Sui Ling Gan Zhi' in thirty fascicles total, which he presented.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then collected popular ballads, drew on charts, books, apocrypha, and prophecy texts, aligned them with tokens of the Mandate, culled passages from Buddhist scriptures, and compiled the 'Records of the Numinous Responses of Imperial Sui' in thirty fascicles, which he presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上令宣示天下。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered it proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered it disseminated throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 劭集諸州朝集使，洗手焚香，閉目讀之。

translations.literal: Shao gathered the regional assembly envoys from all prefectures, washed his hands, burned incense, closed his eyes, and read it.
translations.idiomatic: Shao assembled the regional envoys posted to court, washed his hands, burned incense, closed his eyes, and chanted the text aloud.

sentences.zh: 曲折其聲，有如歌詠，經涉旬朔，遍而後罷。

translations.literal: Bending and folding his voice like song and chant, passing through ten days and a month, only when he had gone through it entirely did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: He modulated his voice like a sacred chant, and for more than a month read through the entire work before stopping.

sentences.zh: 上益喜，賞賜優洽。

translations.literal: The emperor grew still more pleased; rewards and gifts were generous and fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still more delighted and lavished generous rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 及文獻皇后崩，劭復上言：「佛經說人應生天上及上品上生無量壽國之時，天佛放大光明，以香花妓樂來迎之。

translations.literal: When Empress Wen passed away, Shao again submitted: "The Buddhist sutras say that when a person should be born in heaven or in the highest grade of highest rebirth in the Land of Infinite Life, heaven and Buddha cast forth great brightness and come to welcome with incense, flowers, musicians, and dancers.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Wen died, Shao memorialized again: "Buddhist scriptures teach that when a soul merits rebirth in heaven or the highest grade of the Land of Infinite Life, heaven and Buddha pour forth great radiance and welcome the departed with incense, flowers, musicians, and dancers.

sentences.zh: 如來以明星出時入涅盤。

translations.literal: The Tathagata entered nirvana when the bright star appeared.
translations.idiomatic: The Tathagata entered nirvana at the hour when the morning star appeared.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大行皇后，聖德仁慈；

translations.literal: Your subject humbly considers: the late empress, sage in virtue and benevolent;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe that the late empress was sage in virtue and benevolent in nature;

sentences.zh: 福善禎符，備諸秘記，皆云是妙善菩薩。

translations.literal: fortunate in goodness with auspicious signs, complete in secret records—all say she was Bodhisattva Miaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: blessed in goodness and marked by auspicious omens recorded in secret texts—all affirm that she was Bodhisattva Miaoshan.

sentences.zh: 臣謹案：八月二十二日，仁壽宮內再雨金銀之花；

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully notes: on the twenty-second day of the eighth month, within Renshou Palace golden and silver flowers rained twice;
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that on the twenty-second day of the eighth month golden and silver flowers twice rained down within Renshou Palace;

sentences.zh: 二十三日，大寶殿后，夜有神光；

translations.literal: on the twenty-third, behind the Great Treasure Hall at night there was divine light;
translations.idiomatic: on the twenty-third, behind the Great Treasure Hall, divine light appeared at night;

sentences.zh: 二十四日卯時，永安宮北，有自然種種音樂，震滿虛空。

translations.literal: on the twenty-fourth at the mao hour, north of Yong'an Palace, there was spontaneously all manner of music shaking and filling the void.
translations.idiomatic: on the twenty-fourth at dawn, north of Yong'an Palace, music of every kind arose spontaneously, reverberating through the heavens.

sentences.zh: 至五更中，奄然如寐，便即升遐。

translations.literal: By mid-fifth watch she suddenly seemed to sleep, and at once ascended to the distant realm.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifth watch she had suddenly fallen as if asleep and at once departed this life.

sentences.zh: 與經文所說，事皆符驗。

translations.literal: Compared with what the sutras say, the events all match in verification.
translations.idiomatic: Every one of these events corresponds to the scriptures' prophecies.

sentences.zh: 臣又以愚意思之，皇后遷化不在仁壽大興宮者，蓋避至尊常居正處也。

translations.literal: Your subject further reflects with foolish thought: that the empress's transformation and departure was not at Renshou or Daxing Palace surely means avoiding the Most Exalted's regular dwelling in the principal place.
translations.idiomatic: I further venture this interpretation: that the empress did not die at Renshou or Daxing Palace was surely to avoid the place where His Majesty ordinarily resided.

sentences.zh: 在永安宮者，象京師永安門，平生所出入也。

translations.literal: Being at Yong'an Palace images the capital's Yong'an Gate, where she passed in and out throughout her life.
translations.idiomatic: Her death at Yong'an Palace symbolizes the capital's Yong'an Gate, through which she had passed all her life.

sentences.zh: 後升遐後二日，苑內夜有鐘聲二百餘處，此則生天之應，顯然也。

translations.literal: Two days after her ascension to the distant realm, within the park at night there were bell sounds at more than two hundred places—this is plainly the response of birth in heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Two days after her passing, bells rang at more than two hundred places within the imperial park by night—plain evidence of her rebirth in heaven.

sentences.zh: 」上覽之，且悲且喜。

translations.literal: " The emperor read it, both grieving and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial, grieving and yet consoled in equal measure.

sentences.zh: 時蜀王秀以罪廢，上謂劭曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Shu, Xiu, was deposed for his crime; the emperor said to Shao: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: About then Prince Xiu of Shu was deposed for his crimes. The emperor said to Shao, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 」吾有五子，三子不才。

translations.literal: " I have five sons; three sons lack talent.
translations.idiomatic: I have five sons, and three of them are worthless.

sentences.zh: 」劭進曰：「自古聖帝明王，皆不能移不肖之子。

translations.literal: " Shao advanced and said: "From antiquity sage emperors and enlightened kings have all been unable to move unworthy sons.
translations.idiomatic: Shao replied, "Since antiquity even sage emperors and enlightened kings have been unable to reform unworthy sons.

sentences.zh: 黃帝二十五子，同姓者二，餘各異德。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons; two shared his surname; the rest each had different virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons, but only two shared his surname; the rest possessed virtues unlike his own.

sentences.zh: 堯十子，舜九子，皆不肖。

translations.literal: Yao had ten sons; Shun had nine sons—all unworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Yao had ten sons and Shun had nine, and all were unworthy.

sentences.zh: 夏有五觀，周有三監。

translations.literal: Xia had the Five Guans; Zhou had the Three Jians.
translations.idiomatic: Xia had the Five Guans and Zhou had the Three Overseers.

sentences.zh: 」上然其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his argument.

sentences.zh: 後上夢欲上高山而不能得，崔彭捧腳，李盛扶肘，乃得上。

translations.literal: Later the emperor dreamed he wished to ascend a high mountain but could not; Cui Peng held his feet, Li Shen supported his elbow, and only then could he ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor dreamed of climbing a high mountain but could not manage it until Cui Peng supported his feet and Li Shen steadied his elbow, enabling him to reach the summit.

sentences.zh: 因謂彭曰：「死生當與爾俱。

translations.literal: He thereupon said to Peng: "In life and death I shall be with you.
translations.idiomatic: He then told Peng, "In life and death I shall remain with you.

sentences.zh: 」劭曰：「此夢大吉。

translations.literal: " Shao said: "This dream is greatly auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Shao declared, "This dream is most auspicious.

sentences.zh: 上高山者，明高崇大安，永如山也。

translations.literal: Ascending a high mountain means manifesting lofty elevation, great peace, enduring as the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Climbing a high mountain signifies exalted stature, great peace, and endurance everlasting as the mountain itself.

sentences.zh: 彭猶彭祖，李猶李老，二人扶侍，實為長壽之征。

translations.literal: Peng is like Peng Zu; Li is like Old Li; the two persons supporting and attending are truly a sign of long life.
translations.idiomatic: Peng evokes Peng Zu the immortal and Li evokes Old Li; that these two men supported him is truly an omen of longevity.

sentences.zh: 」上聞之，喜見容色。

translations.literal: " The emperor heard it, and joy appeared in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, the emperor's face brightened with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 其年，上崩，未幾，崔彭亦卒。

translations.literal: That year the emperor passed away; before long Cui Peng also died.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the emperor died, and soon afterward Cui Peng died as well.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，漢王諒作亂，帝不忍誅。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne; the Prince of Han, Liang, rebelled; the emperor could not bear to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Prince Liang of Han rose in rebellion, but the emperor could not bring himself to execute him.

sentences.zh: 劭上書曰：「臣聞黃帝滅炎，蓋雲母弟；

translations.literal: Shao submitted a memorial: "Your subject has heard that the Yellow Emperor destroyed Yan—yet Yan was his mother's younger brother;
translations.idiomatic: Shao memorialized: "I have heard that the Yellow Emperor destroyed Yan, though Yan was his mother's younger brother;

sentences.zh: 周公誅管，信亦天倫；

translations.literal: the Duke of Zhou executed Guan—yet truly this too was heaven's kin;
translations.idiomatic: that the Duke of Zhou executed Guan, though Guan too was bound to him by the ties of heaven;

sentences.zh: 叔向戮叔魚，仲尼謂之遺直；

translations.literal: Shu Xiang executed Shu Yu—yet Confucius called it leaving straightness behind;
translations.idiomatic: that Shu Xiang put his brother Shu Yu to death, which Confucius praised as preserving integrity;

sentences.zh: 石蠟殺石厚，丘明以為大義。

translations.literal: Shi Zhu executed Shi Hou—yet Qiu Ming considered it great righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: that Shi Zhu killed his son Shi Hou, which Zuo Qiuming judged an act of supreme righteousness.

sentences.zh: 此皆經籍明文，帝王常法。

translations.literal: These are all clear passages in the classics, the constant method of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: These are all explicit lessons in the classics—the constant law of sage rulers.

sentences.zh: 今陛下置此逆賊，度越前聖。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty spares this traitor-rebel, surpassing the former sages.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty now spares this rebel, exceeding even those ancient sages in mercy.

sentences.zh: 謹案：賊諒毒被生靈者也。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully notes: the rebel Liang's poison spreads over living beings.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully observe that the rebel Liang's poison has spread across the living world.

sentences.zh: 古者同德則同姓，德不同則異姓，故黃帝有二十五子，其得姓者十有四人，唯青陽、夷鼓與黃帝同為姬姓。

translations.literal: In antiquity those of the same virtue shared the same surname; those of different virtue had different surnames. Thus the Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons; fourteen received surnames; only Qingyang and Yibo shared with the Yellow Emperor the surname Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity those who shared virtue shared a surname, while those of differing virtue bore different surnames. The Yellow Emperor had twenty-five sons, fourteen of whom received surnames, but only Qingyang and Yibo shared the Ji clan name with the Yellow Emperor.

sentences.zh: 諒既自絕，請改其氏。

translations.literal: Liang has already severed himself—your subject requests that his clan be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liang has severed himself from the imperial house, I beg that his clan name be changed.

sentences.zh: 」劭以此求媚，帝依違不從。

translations.literal: " Shao sought favor thereby; the emperor hesitated and did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Shao sought favor with this memorial, but the emperor wavered and did not comply.

sentences.zh: 後遷秘書少監，卒於官。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 劭在著作，將二十年，專典國史，撰《隋書》八十卷。

translations.literal: Shao was in the Compilation Office nearly twenty years, exclusively in charge of the national history, and compiled the 'Sui Shu' in eighty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Shao spent nearly twenty years in the Compilation Office, where he supervised the national history and compiled eighty fascicles of the History of Sui.

sentences.zh: 多錄口敕。

translations.literal: He recorded many oral edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Much of it consisted of verbatim records of oral edicts.

sentences.zh: 又采迂怪不經之語，及委巷之言，以類相從，為其題目。

translations.literal: He also gathered absurd, unorthodox sayings and alley gossip, arranging them by category under their respective titles.
translations.idiomatic: He also collected bizarre and unorthodox tales along with street gossip, grouping them by category under various titles.

sentences.zh: 詞義繁雜，無足稱者。

translations.literal: The language and meaning are prolix and messy, not worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: The prose is prolix and confused, and the work is not worth commending.

sentences.zh: 遂使隋代文武名臣善惡之跡，堙滅無聞。

translations.literal: Thus the deeds, good and ill, of the civil and military worthies of the Sui age were buried and lost to hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the deeds, good and ill, of Sui's civil and military worthies were buried in oblivion.

sentences.zh: 初撰《齊志》為編年體二十卷，復為《齊書》，紀傳一百卷，及《平賊記》三卷，或文詞鄙野，或不軌不物，駭人視聽，大為有識嗤鄙。

translations.literal: At first he drafted the 'Qi Zhi' in annalistic form, twenty fascicles; then he produced the 'Qi Shu' in annals-and-biographies form, one hundred fascicles, and the 'Ping Zei Ji' in three fascicles. Some passages were crude in diction, others irregular and unseemly, shocking to eye and ear, and widely mocked by the discerning.
translations.idiomatic: He first drafted the Annals of Qi in twenty fascicles of annalistic form, then produced a History of Qi in one hundred fascicles of annals-and-biographies format, along with a Record of Pacifying Rebels in three fascicles. Some passages were crude, others bizarre and unseemly, shocking to read or hear, and men of judgment widely scorned them.

sentences.zh: 然其指摘經史謬誤，為《讀書記》三十卷，時人服其精博。

translations.literal: Yet in pointing out errors in the classics and histories he compiled the 'Dushu Ji' in thirty fascicles, and men of his day admired its precision and breadth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in exposing errors in the classics and histories he compiled thirty fascicles of Reading Notes, and contemporaries admired his precision and erudition.

sentences.zh: 爰自志學，暨於暮齒。

translations.literal: From the age of fifteen on, down to his old age.
translations.idiomatic: From his fifteenth year to his old age.

sentences.zh: 篤好經史，遺略世事。

translations.literal: He was devoted to the classics and histories and neglected worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to the classics and histories and paid little heed to worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 用思既專，性頗恍忽，每至對食，閉目凝思，盤中之肉，輒為僕從所啖。

translations.literal: His thoughts were so concentrated that his nature grew rather absent-minded. Whenever he sat down to eat, he would close his eyes and ponder; the meat on his plate was then eaten by his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: His concentration was so complete that he grew absent-minded. At meals he would close his eyes and lose himself in thought, and the meat on his plate would be eaten by his attendants.

sentences.zh: 劭弗之覺，唯責肉少，數罰廚人。

translations.literal: Shao did not notice, but only blamed the scant meat and repeatedly punished the cooks.
translations.idiomatic: Shao noticed nothing and only complained that there was too little meat, repeatedly punishing the kitchen staff.

sentences.zh: 廚人以情白劭，劭依前閉目，伺而獲之。

translations.literal: The cooks told Shao the truth; Shao closed his eyes as before and waited until he caught them.
translations.idiomatic: The cooks told him what was happening. Shao closed his eyes as before and waited until he caught them in the act.

sentences.zh: 廚人方免笞辱。

translations.literal: Only then were the cooks spared beating.
translations.idiomatic: Only then were the cooks spared a beating.

sentences.zh: 其專固如此。

translations.literal: Such was his fixity of mind.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the fixity of his devotion.

sentences.zh: 遵業弟廣業，性沈雅，涉曆書傳，位太尉祭酒，遷屬。

translations.literal: Zunye's younger brother Guangye was of a grave and refined nature, versed in books and records, and held the post of libationer at the Grand Marshal's office before being transferred to an attendant post.
translations.idiomatic: Zunye's younger brother Guangye was grave and refined, well read in books and records, served as libationer at the Grand Marshal's office, and was later transferred to an attendant post.

sentences.zh: 卒于太中大夫，贈徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He died as Grand Master of Palace Affairs and was posthumously made Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died while serving as Grand Master of Palace Affairs and was posthumously appointed Inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 子乂，有儀望，以幹用見稱，卒于南钜鹿太守。

translations.literal: His son Yi had a dignified bearing and was praised for practical ability; he died as Administrator of Southern Julu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi had a dignified presence and was known for practical ability; he died while serving as Administrator of Southern Julu.

sentences.zh: 廣業弟延業，博學多聞，頗有才藻，位中書郎。

translations.literal: Guangye's younger brother Yanye was broadly learned and well informed, with considerable literary talent, and held the post of Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye's younger brother Yanye was broadly learned and well informed, possessed considerable literary talent, and served as Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 河陰之役，遂亡骸骨。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Heyin his bones were lost.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Heyin he was killed and his remains were never recovered.

sentences.zh: 乂無子，贈齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Yi had no son and was posthumously made Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yi left no son and was posthumously appointed Inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 延業弟季和，位書侍御史、并州大中正，贈華州刺史。

translations.literal: Yanye's younger brother Jihe held the posts of Attendant Imperial Censor and Senior Rectifier of Bing Province and was posthumously made Inspector of Hua Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yanye's younger brother Jihe served as Attendant Imperial Censor and Senior Rectifier of Bing Province and was posthumously appointed Inspector of Hua Province.

sentences.zh: 鄭羲，字幼麟，滎陽開封人，魏將作大匠渾之八世孫也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xi, courtesy name Youlin, was a native of Kaifeng in Xingyang, eighth-generation descendant of Zheng Hun, Chief Artisan of the Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xi, courtesy name Youlin, was a native of Kaifeng in Xingyang and eighth-generation descendant of Zheng Hun, Chief Artisan under the Wei.

sentences.zh: 曾祖豁，慕容垂太常卿。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Huo was Minister of Ceremonies under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Huo served Murong Chui as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 父曄，不仕。

translations.literal: His father Ye did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ye never entered government service.

sentences.zh: 娶長樂潘氏，生六子，粗有志氣，而羲第六，文學為優。

translations.literal: He married Lady Pan of Changle, who bore six sons, all with some spirit, while Xi was the sixth and excelled in letters and learning.
translations.idiomatic: He married Lady Pan of Changle, who bore six sons, each with some mettle; Xi was the sixth and excelled in letters and learning.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉秀才，尚書李孝伯以女妻之。

translations.literal: At his capping he was nominated as a xiucai, and the Director of the Department of State Affairs Li Xiaobo gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping he was nominated as a xiucai, and Director of the Department of State Affairs Li Xiaobo gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 文成末，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Wen-cheng reign he was appointed doctoral scholar of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Emperor Wen-cheng's reign he was appointed doctoral scholar of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天安初，宋司州刺史常珍奇據汝南來降，獻文詔殿中尚書元石為都將赴之，遣羲參石軍事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tian-an, Chang Zhenqi of Song, Inspector of Sizhou, held Runan and came over in surrender. Emperor Xianwen ordered Yuan Shi, Director of the Palace Department, to go as supreme commander to receive him and sent Xi to serve on Shi's staff.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tian-an, Song's Inspector of Sizhou Chang Zhenqi, who held Runan, surrendered. Emperor Xianwen ordered Director of the Palace Department Yuan Shi to go as supreme commander to receive him and sent Xi to serve on Shi's staff.

sentences.zh: 到上蔡，珍奇率文武三百人來迎。

translations.literal: When they reached Shangcai, Zhenqi led three hundred civil and military officials to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Shangcai, Zhenqi came out with three hundred civil and military officials to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 既相見，議欲頓軍汝北，未即入城。

translations.literal: After they met, they discussed halting the army north of the Ru and not entering the city at once.
translations.idiomatic: After the meeting they discussed halting the army north of the Ru River rather than entering the city at once.

sentences.zh: 羲謂石曰：「機事尚速，今珍奇雖來，意未可量。

translations.literal: Xi said to Shi: "Critical affairs favor speed. Though Zhenqi has come now, his intentions cannot yet be gauged.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said to Shi, "Critical affairs favor speed. Zhenqi may have come, but his intentions cannot yet be gauged.

sentences.zh: 不如直入其城，奪其管籥，據有府庫。

translations.literal: Better to enter his city at once, seize the keys of authority, and take possession of the treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Better to enter the city at once, seize the keys of authority, and take possession of the treasuries.

sentences.zh: 雖出珍奇非意，要以全制為勝。

translations.literal: Even if this goes against Zhenqi's wishes, securing full control is the winning move.
translations.idiomatic: Even if Zhenqi did not intend this, securing full control is what wins.

sentences.zh: 」石從羲言，遂策馬徑入其城。

translations.literal: " Shi followed Xi's advice and spurred his horse straight into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shi followed Xi's advice and spurred his horse straight into the city.

sentences.zh: 城中尚有珍奇親兵數百人，在珍奇宅內。

translations.literal: Within the city there were still several hundred of Zhenqi's personal troops in Zhenqi's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred of Zhenqi's personal troops still remained in the city, quartered at his residence.

sentences.zh: 石既克城，意益憍怠，置酒嬉戲，無警防之虞。

translations.literal: Once Shi had taken the city, his mind grew all the more arrogant and lax; he set out wine and amused himself, with no thought of guard or defense.
translations.idiomatic: Once the city was taken, Shi grew arrogant and careless, set out wine, and made merry, giving no thought to defense.

sentences.zh: 羲勸嚴兵設備，以待非常。

translations.literal: Xi urged strict arms and preparations against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Xi urged him to keep the troops under strict discipline and stand ready for any emergency.

sentences.zh: 其夜，珍奇果使人燒府，欲因救火作難，以石有備，乃止。

translations.literal: That night Zhenqi indeed sent men to burn the government offices, intending to raise trouble under cover of firefighting, but because Shi was prepared they desisted.
translations.idiomatic: That night Zhenqi sent men to set fire to the government offices, planning to stage a revolt under cover of fighting the blaze, but finding Shi prepared they abandoned the attempt.

sentences.zh: 明旦，羲齎白武幡安慰郭邑，眾心乃定。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day Xi carried white military banners to reassure the wards and suburbs, and popular sentiment then settled.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day Xi carried white military banners through the wards and suburbs to reassure the people, and order was restored.

sentences.zh: 明年，又引軍東討汝陰。

translations.literal: The next year they again led troops east to attack Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they led troops east again to attack Ruyin.

sentences.zh: 宋汝陰太守張超城守不下，石攻之不克，議欲還軍長社，待秋擊之。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao of Song, Administrator of Ruyin, held the city and could not be taken; Shi attacked without success and they discussed returning the army to Changshe to wait until autumn before striking.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Administrator of Ruyin Zhang Chao held the city and could not be dislodged. After Shi's assault failed, they discussed withdrawing to Changshe and waiting until autumn to attack again.

sentences.zh: 羲曰：「今超驅市人，命不延月，宜安心守之。

translations.literal: Xi said: "Zhang Chao now drives market folk; his fate will not last a month. We should settle in and hold the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "Zhang Chao is driving townsfolk to the walls; he cannot last a month. We should settle in and maintain the siege.

sentences.zh: 超食已盡，不降當走。

translations.literal: When Chao's provisions are exhausted, if he does not surrender he will flee.
translations.idiomatic: When his food runs out, he will flee if he does not surrender.

sentences.zh: 而欲棄還長社，超必修城深塹，多積薪穀，將來恐難圖矣。

translations.literal: Yet if we abandon the siege and return to Changshe, Chao is sure to repair the walls and deepen the moats and stockpile fuel and grain; when we come again he will be hard to overcome.
translations.idiomatic: If we withdraw to Changshe now, Chao will surely repair the walls, deepen the moats, and stockpile fuel and grain. When we return he will be far harder to take.

sentences.zh: 」石不納，遂旋師長社。

translations.literal: " Shi did not accept this and withdrew the army to Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: Shi would not listen and withdrew the army to Changshe.

sentences.zh: 至冬，復往攻超，超果設備，無功而還。

translations.literal: When winter came they attacked Chao again; Chao had indeed made preparations, and they returned without success.
translations.idiomatic: In winter they attacked again, but Chao had made his preparations as predicted, and they returned without success.

sentences.zh: 歷年，超死，楊文長代戍，食盡城潰，乃克之，竟如羲策。

translations.literal: After some years Chao died; Yang Wenchang replaced him on garrison duty; when provisions were exhausted the city collapsed, and they took it—exactly as Xi had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later Zhang Chao died. Yang Wenchang took over the garrison; when provisions ran out the city fell, and they took it—exactly as Xi had predicted.

sentences.zh: 淮北平，遷中書侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Huai region north of the river was pacified, he was transferred to Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: After the north bank of the Huai was pacified, he was promoted to Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 延興初，陽武人田智度年十五，妖惑動眾，擾亂京索。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanxing, Tian Zhidu of Yangwu, aged fifteen, used sorcery to stir the masses and disturbed the capital region and the Suo.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yanxing era, Tian Zhidu of Yangwu, aged fifteen, used sorcery to rouse the people and threw the capital region and the Suo corridor into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 以羲河南人望，為州郡所信，遣乘傳慰喻。

translations.literal: Because Xi enjoyed standing among the notables of Henan and was trusted by the provinces and commanderies, he was sent by post carriage to console and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Xi was a man of standing in Henan and trusted by the provinces and commanderies, he was sent by courier to console and instruct the people.

sentences.zh: 羲到，宣示禍福，眾皆散，智度尋見禽斬。

translations.literal: When Xi arrived he proclaimed fortune and misfortune; the crowds all dispersed, and Zhidu was soon captured and executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi arrived he explained the consequences of rebellion and loyalty; the crowds dispersed, and Zhidu was soon captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 以功賜爵泰昌男。

translations.literal: For this merit he was granted the title Baron of Taichang.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was ennobled as Baron of Taichang.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，兼員外散騎常侍、甯朔將軍、陽武子，使于宋。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was concurrently supernumerary attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary, General Who Pacifies the North, and Baron of Yangwu, and was sent on mission to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign he served concurrently as supernumerary attendant cavalier attendant-in-ordinary and General Who Pacifies the North, held the title Baron of Yangwu, and was sent on embassy to Song.

sentences.zh: 中山王睿寵倖當世，並置王官，羲為其傅。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhongshan Rui enjoyed favor and privilege in his day and established a full staff of princely officials; Xi served as his tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhongshan Rui enjoyed extraordinary favor and maintained a full princely staff; Xi served as his tutor.

sentences.zh: 是後歷年不轉，資產亦乏，因請假歸，遂盤桓不返。

translations.literal: After this he went years without promotion, his means grew scant, and he asked leave to return home and then lingered without coming back.
translations.idiomatic: For years afterward he received no promotion, his means grew thin, and he asked leave to return home, where he lingered without returning to office.

sentences.zh: 及李沖貴寵，與羲昏姻，乃就家徵為中書令。

translations.literal: When Li Chong rose to high favor and entered a marriage alliance with Xi, Xi was summoned from his home to be Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chong rose to high favor and allied with Xi by marriage, Xi was summoned from his home to serve as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 文明太后為父燕宣王立廟于長安，初成，以羲兼太常卿，假滎陽侯，具官屬，詣長安拜廟，建碑於廟門。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming had a temple built for her father, Prince Xuan of Yan, at Chang'an. When it was first completed, Xi was made concurrent Minister of Ceremonies with acting rank as Marquis of Xingyang, given a full staff, sent to Chang'an to perform the temple rites, and had a stele erected at the temple gate.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming built a temple to her father, Prince Xuan of Yan, at Chang'an. When it was completed she appointed Xi concurrent Minister of Ceremonies and acting Marquis of Xingyang, gave him a full staff, and sent him to Chang'an to perform the rites and erect a stele at the temple gate.

sentences.zh: 還，以使功，仍賜侯爵。

translations.literal: On his return, for merit on the mission, he was again granted a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was granted a marquisate in recognition of his mission.

sentences.zh: 出為西兗州刺史，假南陽公。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Western Yan Province with acting rank as Duke of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Inspector of Western Yan Province with acting rank as Duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 羲多所受納，政以賄成。

translations.literal: Xi accepted many bribes, and his administration was accomplished through gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Xi accepted many bribes, and his administration ran on graft.

sentences.zh: 性又嗇吝，人有禮餉者，不與杯酒臠肉，而西門受羊酒，東門沽賣之。

translations.literal: His nature was also stingy: when people brought him ceremonial gifts he would not offer them a cup of wine or a slice of meat, but received sheep and wine at the west gate and sold them at the east gate.
translations.idiomatic: He was also miserly: when visitors brought gifts he would not offer them so much as a cup of wine or a slice of meat, but accepted sheep and wine at the west gate and sold them at the east.

sentences.zh: 以李沖之親，法官不之糾也。

translations.literal: Because of his kinship with Li Chong, the judicial officers did not prosecute him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his connection to Li Chong, the judicial authorities did not prosecute him.

sentences.zh: 酸棗令鄭伯孫、鄄城令董騰、別駕賈懷德、中從事申靈度並在任廉貞，勤恤百姓，羲皆申表稱薦，時論多之。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Suozao Zheng Bosun, the magistrate of Juancheng Dong Teng, the vice administrator Jia Huaide, and the senior clerk Shen Lingdu were all upright in office and diligent in caring for the people; Xi memorialized recommending them all, and contemporary opinion praised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrates of Suozao and Juancheng, Zheng Bosun and Dong Teng, the vice administrator Jia Huaide, and the senior clerk Shen Lingdu were all upright and attentive to the people. Xi memorialized recommending them all, and contemporaries praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 文明太后為孝文納其女為嬪，徵為秘書監。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming had his daughter taken into Emperor Xiaowen's harem as a consort, and he was summoned to be Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming had his daughter taken into Emperor Xiaowen's harem as a consort, and he was recalled to serve as Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 太和十六年卒，尚書奏諡曰宣。

translations.literal: He died in the sixteenth year of Taihe; the Department of State Affairs memorialized a posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year of Taihe. The Department of State Affairs proposed the posthumous epithet Xuan.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「蓋棺定諡，先典成式；

translations.literal: An edict said: "When the coffin is closed the posthumous name is fixed—this is the established pattern of the ancients;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "To fix the posthumous name when the coffin is closed is the established pattern of the ancients;

sentences.zh: 激揚清濁，政道明範。

translations.literal: it exalts the pure and censures the base, making clear the norms of governance;
translations.idiomatic: it exalts the worthy and censures the base, setting forth the norms of governance.

sentences.zh: 羲雖宿有文業，而政闕廉清。

translations.literal: Xi, though long possessed of literary accomplishment, was deficient in integrity in office.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, though long accomplished in letters, was deficient in integrity in office.

sentences.zh: 尚書何乃情遺至公，愆違明典？

translations.literal: How could the Department let private feeling override impartial justice and violate the bright statutes?
translations.idiomatic: How could the Department let private feeling override impartial justice and violate the statutes?

sentences.zh: 依諡法，博聞多見曰文，不勤成名曰靈，可贈以本官，加諡文靈。」

translations.literal: By the rules of posthumous naming, 'broadly learned and widely informed' is Wen, and 'achieving a name without diligence' is Ling. Let him be granted his former office and given the additional epithet Wen Ling."
translations.idiomatic: By the rules of posthumous naming, 'broadly learned and widely informed' yields Wen, and 'achieving renown without diligence' yields Ling. Grant him his former office and add the epithet Wen Ling."

sentences.zh: 長子懿，字景伯，涉歷經史。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yi, courtesy name Jingbo, ranged through the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yi, courtesy name Jingbo, was versed in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 位太子中庶子，襲爵滎陽伯。

translations.literal: He held the post of junior mentor to the heir apparent and inherited the title Baron of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as junior mentor to the heir apparent and inherited the title Baron of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 懿閒雅有政事才，為孝文所器遇，拜長兼給事黃門侍郎、司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Yi was refined and possessed talent for administration; Emperor Xiaowen valued him and appointed him senior concurrent attendant in regular attendance at the Yellow Gate and senior clerk on the left of the Minister of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was refined and capable in administration. Emperor Xiaowen favored him and appointed him senior concurrent attendant at the Yellow Gate and senior clerk on the left of the Minister of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，以從弟思和同咸陽王禧逆，與弟通直常侍道昭俱坐緦親出禁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanwu's reign, because his cousin Sikong joined Prince of Xianyang Xi's rebellion, he and his younger brother Daozhao, attendant in regular attendance for direct communication, were both punished as distant kin and expelled from the inner precinct.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xuanwu's reign, because his cousin Sikong had joined Prince of Xianyang Xi's rebellion, he and his younger brother Daozhao, attendant for direct communication, were both punished as distant kin and barred from the inner precinct.

sentences.zh: 拜太常少卿，出為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Ceremonies and went out as Inspector of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Ceremonies and later sent out as Inspector of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 懿好勸課，善斷決，雖不清潔，義然後取，百姓猶思之。

translations.literal: Yi was fond of urging agriculture and skilled in judgments; though not clean-handed, he took only when right and proper, and the common people still remember him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi encouraged agriculture and judged cases well. Though not scrupulously honest, he took only what he considered justified, and the people still remember him fondly.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兗州刺史，諡曰穆。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Inspector of Yan Province with the epithet Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously appointed Inspector of Yan Province with the epithet Mu.

sentences.zh: 子恭業襲爵，武定三年，坐與房子遠謀害齊神武，伏誅。

translations.literal: His son Gongye inherited the title; in the third year of Wuding, for plotting with Fang Ziyuan to harm Qi Shenwu, he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongye inherited the title. In the third year of Wuding he was executed for plotting with Fang Ziyuan to assassinate Qi Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 懿弟道昭，字僖伯，少好學，綜覽群言。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Daozhao, courtesy name Xibo, loved learning from youth and surveyed the breadth of writings.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Daozhao, courtesy name Xibo, loved learning from youth and surveyed the breadth of classical writings.

sentences.zh: 兼中書侍郎，從征沔北。

translations.literal: He was concurrently Secretariat Vice Director and followed the campaign north of the Mian.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as Secretariat Vice Director and accompanied the campaign north of the Mian.

sentences.zh: 孝文饗侍臣于縣瓠方丈竹堂，道昭與兄懿俱侍坐。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen feasted his attendants in the one-zhang-square bamboo hall at Xianhuo county, and Daozhao sat in attendance with his elder brother Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen feasted his courtiers in the one-zhang bamboo hall at Xianhuo, and Daozhao sat in attendance with his elder brother Yi.

sentences.zh: 樂作酒酣，孝文歌曰：「白日光天兮無不曜，江左一隅獨未照。

translations.literal: When the music had begun and the wine was deep, Emperor Xiaowen sang: "White sun, bright heaven—nothing left unlit; only one corner east of the river still waits in shadow."
translations.idiomatic: As the music rose and the wine deepened, Emperor Xiaowen sang, "The white sun fills the heavens and leaves nothing unlit—only one corner east of the River still waits in shadow."

sentences.zh: 」彭城王勰續曰：「願從聖明兮登衡、會，萬國馳誠混日外。

translations.literal: " Prince of Pengcheng Xie continued: "May we follow the sage brightness to ascend Heng and Hui; all lands rush their loyalty and mingle beyond the sun."
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Pengcheng Xie took up the verse: "May we follow the sage brightness to ascend Heng and Hui; let all lands rush their loyalty and mingle beyond the sun's reach."

sentences.zh: 」鄭懿歌曰：「雲雷大振兮天門辟，率土來賓一正曆。

translations.literal: " Zheng Yi sang: "Clouds and thunder shake the heavens; the celestial gate opens; all within the realm come as guests under one true calendar."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi sang, "Cloud and thunder shake the heavens; the celestial gate opens; all within the realm come as guests under one true calendar."

sentences.zh: 」邢巒歌曰：「舜舞幹戚兮天下歸，文德遠被莫不思。

translations.literal: " Xing Luan sang: "Shun danced with shield and axe and the realm returned; civil virtue spread far, and none failed to yearn for it."
translations.idiomatic: Xing Luan sang, "Shun danced with shield and axe and the realm returned; civil virtue spread far, and none failed to yearn for it."

sentences.zh: 」道昭歌曰：「皇風一鼓兮九地匝，戴日依天清六合。

translations.literal: " Daozhao sang: "One beat of the imperial wind circles the nine realms; bearing sun and leaning on heaven, the six directions grow clear."
translations.idiomatic: Daozhao sang, "One beat of the imperial wind circles the nine realms; bearing sun and leaning on heaven, the six directions grow clear."

sentences.zh: 」孝文又歌曰：「遵彼汝墳兮昔化貞，未若今日道風明。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xiaowen sang again: "Along that bank of the Ru—once the place of true transformation; nothing like today, when the Way's wind shines clear."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen sang again, "Along the bank of the Ru—once the ground of true transformation; nothing like today, when the Way's wind shines clear."

sentences.zh: 」宋弁歌曰：「文王政教兮暉江召，寧如大化光四表。

translations.literal: " Song Bian sang: "King Wen's governance and teaching once summoned radiance to the river; how could it match the great transformation that now lights the four quarters?"
translations.idiomatic: Song Bian sang, "King Wen's governance and teaching once summoned radiance to the river—how could it match the great transformation that now lights the four quarters?"

sentences.zh: 」孝文謂道昭曰：「自比遷豫雖猥，與諸才俊不廢詠綴，未若今日。

translations.literal: " Emperor Xiaowen said to Daozhao: "Since we moved the capital to Yu it has been humble, yet with all you talented men we never ceased composing verse—still, nothing equals today."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said to Daozhao, "Since we moved the capital to Yu the setting has been modest, yet with all you talented men we never ceased composing verse—still, nothing equals today."

sentences.zh: 」遂命邢巒總集敘記。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Xing Luan to compile and record the whole affair.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Xing Luan to compile a full record of the occasion.

sentences.zh: 「當爾之年，卿頻丁艱私，每眷文席，常用慨然」。

translations.literal: "In those years you often suffered private bereavements; whenever you looked back on literary gatherings, you were always deeply moved."
translations.idiomatic: It noted, "In those years you were often in mourning; whenever you recalled our literary gatherings, you were always deeply moved."

sentences.zh: 尋正除中書郎，累遷國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was formally made Secretariat Gentleman and was promoted in stages to Libationer of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon formally appointed Secretariat Gentleman and rose in stages to Libationer of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 廣平王懷為司州牧，以道昭與宗正卿元匡為州都督。

translations.literal: When Prince of Guangping Huai was Governor of Sizhou, Daozhao and the Director of the Imperial Clan Yuan Kuang were made regional commanders of the province.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Guangping Huai served as Governor of Sizhou, Daozhao and Director of the Imperial Clan Yuan Kuang were appointed regional commanders of the province.

sentences.zh: 道昭上表曰：臣聞唐、虞啟運，以文德為本；

translations.literal: Daozhao submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that when Tang and Yu opened their mandates, they took civil virtue as the foundation;
translations.idiomatic: Daozhao submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that when Tang and Yu opened their mandates, they took civil virtue as the foundation;

sentences.zh: 殷、周創業，以道藝為先。

translations.literal: when Yin and Zhou founded their enterprises, they put the Way and the arts first;
translations.idiomatic: when Yin and Zhou founded their enterprises, they put the Way and the arts first.

sentences.zh: 然則禮樂者，為國之基，不可斯須廢也。

translations.literal: Thus rites and music are the foundation of a state and may not be abandoned even for a moment.
translations.idiomatic: Thus rites and music are the foundation of a state and must not be abandoned even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大魏，定鼎伊、瀍，惟新寶曆。

translations.literal: I consider that Great Wei has fixed the tripod at Yi and Chan and renewed the imperial calendar.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that Great Wei has fixed the tripod at Yi and Chan and renewed the imperial calendar.

sentences.zh: 九服感至德之和，四垠懷擊壤之慶。

translations.literal: The nine domains feel the harmony of utmost virtue; the four borders cherish the joy of the clod-beaters' song.
translations.idiomatic: The nine domains feel the harmony of utmost virtue; the four borders share the joy of a peaceful age.

sentences.zh: 而蠢爾閩吳，阻化江湫；

translations.literal: Yet foolish Min and Wu still block transformation along the river's shallows;
translations.idiomatic: Yet foolish Min and Wu still resist civilization along the river's shallows;

sentences.zh: 先帝爰震武怒，戎車不息。

translations.literal: the late emperor then shook his martial wrath, and the war chariots did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: the late emperor then shook his martial wrath, and the war chariots never rested.

sentences.zh: 而停鑾駐蹕，留心典墳。

translations.literal: yet he halted the imperial carriage and attended to the canonical texts.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he halted the imperial progress and devoted himself to the canonical texts.

sentences.zh: 命故御史中尉臣李彪，與吏部尚書任城王臣澄等，妙選英儒，以崇學校。

translations.literal: He ordered the late Imperial Censor-in-Chief Li Biao, together with the Director of the Department of State Affairs, the Prince of Rencheng Chen, and others, to select outstanding scholars and exalt the schools.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the late Imperial Censor-in-Chief Li Biao, together with Director of the Department of State Affairs Prince of Rencheng Chen and others, to select outstanding scholars and strengthen the schools.

sentences.zh: 澄等依旨，置四門博士四十人。

translations.literal: Chen and the others followed the edict and appointed forty doctoral scholars of the Four Gates.
translations.idiomatic: Chen and the others followed the edict and appointed forty doctoral scholars of the Four Gates.

sentences.zh: 其國子博士、太學博士及國子助教，宿已簡置。

translations.literal: The doctoral scholars of the Imperial University, the doctoral scholars of the Grand Academy, and the assistant instructors of the Imperial University had long since been selected and appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The doctoral scholars of the Imperial University and Grand Academy, together with the assistant instructors of the Imperial University, had long since been selected and appointed.

sentences.zh: 伏尋先旨，意在速就；

translations.literal: Prostrate myself and trace the former edict—its intent was speedy completion;
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the former edict, its intent was swift completion;

sentences.zh: 但軍國多事，未遑營立。

translations.literal: but military and state affairs were many, and there was no leisure to establish it.
translations.idiomatic: but with so many military and state affairs, there was no leisure to establish it.

sentences.zh: 自爾迄今，垂將一紀，學官雕落，四術寢廢。

translations.literal: From then until now, nearly a full cycle has passed; academic offices have withered away, and the four arts lie dormant and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: From then until now, nearly twelve years have passed; academic offices have declined, and the four arts lie neglected.

sentences.zh: 遂使碩儒耆德，卷經而不談；

translations.literal: thus great scholars and venerable elders roll up their classics and do not discourse;
