translations.idiomatic: Thus eminent scholars and venerable elders roll up their classics and cease to teach;

sentences.zh: 俗學後生，遺本而逐末。

translations.literal: vulgar students and younger generations abandon the root and pursue the branch.
translations.idiomatic: vulgar students and younger generations abandon fundamentals and chase trivialities.

sentences.zh: 進競之風，實由於此矣。

translations.literal: The wind of advancement and rivalry truly arises from this.
translations.idiomatic: The culture of ruthless competition truly stems from this.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，欽明文思，玄鑒洞遠，垂心經素。

translations.literal: I consider that Your Majesty, reverent in civil brilliance and literary thought, with profound insight penetrating far, lowers his mind to the classics and plain texts.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that Your Majesty, reverent in civil brilliance and literary attainments, with insight penetrating far, devotes your mind to the classics.

sentences.zh: 優柔墳籍，屢發中旨，敦營學館，房宇既修，生徒未立。

translations.literal: lingering over tomb records and canonical books, repeatedly issuing central edicts, earnestly establishing academies—the buildings already repaired, yet students not yet appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to the canonical texts, you have repeatedly issued central edicts to establish academies—the buildings are already repaired, yet the students have not yet been appointed.

sentences.zh: 臣往年刪定律令，謬預議筵。

translations.literal: Your servant in former years revised and fixed laws and ordinances, and by error participated in the deliberation assembly.
translations.idiomatic: In former years I helped revise laws and ordinances, and was undeservedly included in the deliberation assembly.

sentences.zh: 謹依准前修，尋訪舊事，參定學令，事訖封呈。

translations.literal: Respectfully following the prior standards for restoration, I searched out old precedents, consulted on and fixed the academy regulations, and when the matter was finished sealed and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Following the prior standards, I have searched out old precedents and drafted academy regulations, which I respectfully present now that the work is finished.

sentences.zh: 請早敕施行，使選授有依，生徒可准。

translations.literal: I request an early imperial order for implementation, so that selection and appointment may have a basis and students may have a standard.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that you promptly issue an edict to put them into effect, so that appointments may have a basis and students may be enrolled.

sentences.zh: 」詔褒美之，而尚未允遂。

translations.literal: " The edict praised him, yet still did not grant his request.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor issued an edict praising him, yet still did not grant his request.

sentences.zh: 道昭又表曰：「臣自往年以來，頻請學令，並置生員，前後累上，未蒙一報。

translations.literal: Daozhao again submitted a memorial: "Since last year your servant has repeatedly requested academy regulations and the appointment of students; memorials piled up one after another, yet I have received not a single reply.
translations.idiomatic: Daozhao again submitted a memorial: "Since last year I have repeatedly requested academy regulations and the appointment of students; memorial after memorial has gone up, yet I have received not a single reply.

sentences.zh: 當以臣識淺濫官，無能有所感悟者也。

translations.literal: It must be that your servant's learning is shallow and his office undeserved, and that I am incapable of offering anything to move Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Surely this is because my learning is shallow and my office undeserved, and I am incapable of offering anything that might move Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 館宇既修，生房粗構，博士見員，足可講習。

translations.literal: The academy buildings are already repaired, dormitories roughly constructed, and the doctoral posts on the roster are sufficient for instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The academy buildings are already repaired, dormitories roughly built, and the doctoral posts on the roster are sufficient for instruction.

sentences.zh: 雖新令未班，請依舊權置國子學生，漸開訓業，使播教有章，儒風不墜。

translations.literal: Although the new regulations have not yet been promulgated, I ask that by the old precedent Imperial University students be provisionally appointed, that instruction gradually begin, so that the dissemination of teaching may have order and Confucian culture may not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Although the new regulations have not yet been promulgated, I ask that Imperial University students be provisionally appointed by the old precedent, that instruction gradually begin, so that teaching may be orderly and Confucian culture may not decline.

sentences.zh: 至若孔廟既成，釋奠告始，揖讓之容，請俟令出。

translations.literal: As for the Confucian temple now completed and the libation ceremony about to begin, the forms of bowing and yielding should await the issuing of the regulations.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Confucian temple now completed and the libation ceremony about to begin, the forms of bowing and yielding should await the issuing of the regulations.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: " No reply was given.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監，滎陽邑中正，出曆光、青二州刺史，復入為秘書監。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, Director of the Xingyang district kinship register, went out and served as Governor of Guang and Qing provinces in succession, then returned and again became Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Xingyang district kinship register, then served in succession as Governor of Guang and Qing provinces before returning as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰文恭。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously titled Cultivated and Respectful.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Cultivated and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 道昭好為詩賦，凡數十篇。

translations.literal: Daozhao enjoyed composing shi and fu poetry; in all there were several dozen pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Daozhao enjoyed composing shi and fu poetry; in all there were several dozen pieces.

sentences.zh: 其在二州，政務寬厚，不任威刑，為吏人所愛。

translations.literal: When he was in the two provinces, his administration was generous and lenient; he did not rely on harsh punishments, and was loved by clerks and common people.
translations.idiomatic: In the two provinces his administration was generous and lenient; he did not rely on harsh punishments, and was beloved by clerks and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 子嚴祖，頗有風儀，粗觀文史，輕躁薄行，不修士業。

translations.literal: His son Yanzu had considerable presence and bearing, had roughly surveyed literature and history, but was frivolous, rash, and of shallow conduct and did not cultivate scholarly pursuits.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanzu had considerable presence and bearing and had roughly surveyed literature and history, but was frivolous and rash, of shallow conduct, and did not cultivate scholarly pursuits.

sentences.zh: 孝武時，御史中尉綦俊劾嚴祖與宋氏從姊奸通，人士咸恥言之，而嚴祖聊無愧色。

translations.literal: During Emperor Xiaowu's reign, the Imperial Censor-in-Chief Qi Jun impeached Yanzu for adultery with a maternal cousin of the Song clan; gentlemen all felt ashamed to speak of it, yet Yanzu showed scarcely any shame.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Xiaowu's reign, Imperial Censor-in-Chief Qi Jun impeached Yanzu for adultery with a maternal cousin of the Song clan; gentlemen were ashamed to speak of it, yet Yanzu showed scarcely any shame.

sentences.zh: 孝靜初，除驃騎將軍、左光祿大夫、鴻臚卿，出為北豫州刺史，還除鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Minister of Ceremonial Hosts, went out as Governor of North Yuzhou, and on return was again appointed Minister of Ceremonial Hosts.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaojing's reign he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Minister of Ceremonial Hosts, then served as Governor of North Yuzhou before returning as Minister of Ceremonial Hosts.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈司空公。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted the title of Duke of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title Duke of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 庶子仲禮，少輕險，有膂力。

translations.literal: A son by a concubine, Zhongli, was in youth reckless and dangerous, and had physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: A son by a concubine, Zhongli, was reckless and dangerous in youth and possessed great physical strength.

sentences.zh: 齊神武嬖寵其姊火車，以親戚被昵，擢為帳內都督。

translations.literal: Northern Qi Shenwu favored his elder sister Huoche; because of kinship ties he was treated with intimacy and promoted to Colonel within the Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi Shenwu favored his elder sister Huoche; through this kinship Zhongli was treated with intimacy and promoted to Colonel within the Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 掌神武弓矢，出入隨從。

translations.literal: He managed Shenwu's bows and arrows and attended him in and out.
translations.idiomatic: He managed Shenwu's bows and arrows and attended him wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 與任胄俱好酒，不憂公事，神武責之。

translations.literal: He and Ren Zhou were both fond of wine, heedless of official business; Shenwu reprimanded them.
translations.idiomatic: He and Ren Zhou were both fond of wine and heedless of official business; Shenwu reprimanded them.

sentences.zh: 胄懼，潛通西魏，為人糾告，懼，遂謀逆。

translations.literal: Zhou grew afraid, secretly communicated with Western Wei, was denounced by someone, grew afraid, and then plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou grew afraid, secretly communicated with Western Wei, was denounced, grew still more afraid, and then plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 事發，火車欲乞哀，神武避不見。

translations.literal: When the affair was exposed, Huoche wished to beg for mercy; Shenwu avoided her and would not see her.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was exposed, Huoche wished to beg for mercy, but Shenwu avoided her and would not see her.

sentences.zh: 賴武明皇后及文襄爭為言，故仲禮死而不及其家。

translations.literal: Thanks to Empress Wuming and Wenxiang contending to speak on his behalf, Zhongli was executed but his family was not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Empress Wuming and Wenxiang speaking on his behalf, Zhongli was executed but his family was spared.

sentences.zh: 嚴祖更無子，弟敬祖以子紹元嗣。

translations.literal: Yanzu had no other sons; his younger brother Jingzu made his son Shaoyuan the heir.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzu had no other sons; his younger brother Jingzu made his son Shaoyuan the heir.

sentences.zh: 紹元小字安都，位太尉諮議、趙郡太守，卒。

translations.literal: Shaoyuan, courtesy name Andu, held the posts of Adviser to the Grand Commandant and Governor of Zhao commandery, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoyuan, courtesy name Andu, served as Adviser to the Grand Commandant and Governor of Zhao commandery, and died.

sentences.zh: 子子翻，字靈雀。

translations.literal: His son Zifan, courtesy name Lingque.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zifan, courtesy name Lingque.

sentences.zh: 少有器識，學涉，好文章。

translations.literal: In youth he had talent and insight, broad learning, and loved literature.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he had talent and insight, broad learning, and loved literature.

sentences.zh: 齊武平末，位司徒記室參軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Qi Wuping he held the post of Recorder in the Secretariat of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Qi Wuping era he served as Recorder in the Secretariat of the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 尋遇齊亡，曆周、隋，遂不仕，隱居滎陽三窟山。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Qi fell; he lived through Zhou and Sui, and then did not take office, living in seclusion on Three Grottoes Mountain in Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Qi fell; he lived through Zhou and Sui without taking office, living in seclusion on Three Grottoes Mountain in Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 傲誕不自羈束，或有所之造，乘驢衣韉，破弊而往。

translations.literal: Proud and unrestrained, when he went somewhere on a visit he would ride a donkey in saddlecloth, tattered and worn, and go.
translations.idiomatic: Proud and unrestrained, when he went visiting he would ride a donkey in tattered saddlecloth and go.

sentences.zh: 遠近欽其高名，皆謂有異狀，觀者如堵。

translations.literal: Near and far admired his lofty reputation; all thought he had an extraordinary appearance; viewers gathered like a wall.
translations.idiomatic: Near and far admired his lofty reputation; all expected an extraordinary appearance, and onlookers gathered thick as a wall.

sentences.zh: 及見，形乃短陋，不副所聞。

translations.literal: When they saw him, his form was short and homely, not matching what they had heard.
translations.idiomatic: When they saw him, his form was short and homely, not matching what they had heard.

sentences.zh: 然風神俊發，無貴賤並敬服之。

translations.literal: Yet his bearing and spirit were brilliant; without regard to noble or base, all respected and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his bearing and spirit were brilliant; noble and base alike respected and submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 納言楊素聞其名，因使過滎陽，迎與相見，言談彌日，深加禮重。

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Yang Su heard his name and therefore sent someone through Xingyang to welcome and meet him; they talked for a full day, and Su deeply honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Yang Su heard his name and sent someone through Xingyang to welcome and meet him; they talked for a full day, and Su deeply honored him.

sentences.zh: 及歸，言之朝廷，累徵不至。

translations.literal: On returning he spoke of him at court; summons came repeatedly, but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he spoke of him at court; summons came repeatedly, but Zifan did not come.

sentences.zh: 終於家。

translations.literal: He died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home.

sentences.zh: 子翻二弟子騰、天壽，俱仕隋。

translations.literal: Zifan's two younger brothers, Ziteng and Tianshou, both served in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Zifan's two younger brothers, Ziteng and Tianshou, both served in Sui.

sentences.zh: 子騰位蔣州司馬，天壽開府參軍，並以雅素稱。

translations.literal: Ziteng held the post of Administrator of Jiang province; Tianshou was Staff Officer of the Eastern Palace—they were both known for refined simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Ziteng served as Administrator of Jiang province; Tianshou as Staff Officer of the Eastern Palace—both were known for refined simplicity.

sentences.zh: 嚴祖弟敬祖，起家著作郎。

translations.literal: Yanzu's younger brother Jingzu began his career as Gentleman of Composition.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzu's younger brother Jingzu began his career as Gentleman of Composition.

sentences.zh: 鄭儼之敗也，為鄉人所害。

translations.literal: When Zheng Yan fell from power, Jingzu was killed by men of his native place.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Yan fell from power, Jingzu was killed by men of his native place.

sentences.zh: 子元禮，字文規。

translations.literal: His son Yuanli, courtesy name Wengui.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanli, courtesy name Wengui.

sentences.zh: 少好學，愛文藻，有名望。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, cherished literary adornment, and had reputation and standing.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he loved learning, cherished literary adornment, and enjoyed reputation and standing.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄引為館客，曆兼中書舍人、南主客郎中、太尉諮議參軍、長廣樂陵二郡守，待詔文林館，太子中舍人。

translations.literal: Qi Wenxiang brought him in as a hall guest; he successively served concurrently as Attendant of the Secretariat, Director of the Southern Bureau of Foreign Guests, Adviser in the Secretariat of the Grand Commandant, Governor of the two commanderies of Changguang and Leling, awaited imperial summons at the Wulin Hall, and Attendant in the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Wenxiang brought him in as a hall guest; he served in succession as Attendant of the Secretariat, Director of the Southern Bureau of Foreign Guests, Adviser in the Secretariat of the Grand Commandant, Governor of Changguang and Leling commanderies, awaited imperial summons at the Wulin Hall, and Attendant in the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 崔昂後妻，元禮姊也，魏收又昂之妹夫。

translations.literal: Cui Ang's second wife was Yuanli's elder sister, and Wei Shou was also Ang's brother-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ang's second wife was Yuanli's elder sister, and Wei Shou was also Ang's brother-in-law.

sentences.zh: 昂嘗持元禮數篇詩示盧思道，乃曰：「看元禮比來詩詠，亦曾不減魏收。

translations.literal: Ang once took several of Yuanli's poems to show Lu Sidao and said: "Look at Yuanli's recent poetry—not at all inferior to Wei Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Ang once took several of Yuanli's poems to show Lu Sidao and said, "Look at Yuanli's recent poetry—not at all inferior to Wei Shou.

sentences.zh: 」思道答云：「未覺元禮賢于魏收，且知妹夫疏于婦弟。

translations.literal: " Sidao replied: "I do not find Yuanli superior to Wei Shou, and I know that a brother-in-law through a younger sister is less close than a wife's younger brother."
translations.idiomatic: " Sidao replied, "I do not find Yuanli superior to Wei Shou—and I see that a brother-in-law through one's younger sister is less close than a wife's younger brother."

sentences.zh: 」元禮，大象中卒於始州別駕。

translations.literal: " Yuanli died in the Daxiang era while serving as Vice-Governor of Shizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuanli died in the Daxiang era while serving as Vice-Governor of Shizhou.

sentences.zh: 敬祖弟述祖，字恭文。

translations.literal: Jingzu's younger brother Shuzu, courtesy name Gongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzu's younger brother Shuzu, courtesy name Gongwen.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，好屬文，有風檢，為先達所稱譽。

translations.literal: In youth clever and keen, fond of composing prose, had moral bearing, and was praised by earlier worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was clever and keen, fond of composing prose, possessed moral bearing, and was praised by earlier worthies.

sentences.zh: 歷位司徒左長史、尚書、侍中、太常卿、丞相右長史。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Palace Attendant, Director of the Imperial Sacrifices, and Right Chief Clerk of the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Works, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Palace Attendant, Director of the Imperial Sacrifices, and Right Chief Clerk of the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 齊天保中，曆太子少保、左光祿大夫、儀同三司、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: During Qi Tianbao he successively served as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qi Tianbao era he served in succession as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, and Governor of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 時穆子容為巡省使，歎曰：「古人有言，聞伯夷之風，貪夫廉，懦夫有立志，今于鄭兗州見之矣。

translations.literal: At the time Mu Zirong was touring inspector and sighed: "The ancients said that hearing of Boyi's conduct makes the greedy man honest and the timid man resolute—today I have seen this in Governor Zheng of Yan province."
translations.idiomatic: At the time Mu Zirong was touring inspector and sighed, "The ancients said that hearing of Boyi's conduct makes the greedy honest and the timid resolute—today I have seen this in Governor Zheng of Yan province."

sentences.zh: 」遷光州刺史。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Governor of Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: " He was transferred to Governor of Guang province.

sentences.zh: 初，述祖父為兗州，于鄭城南小山起齋亭，刻石為記。

translations.literal: Initially, when Shuzu's grandfather was Governor of Yan, on a small hill south of Zheng city he built a retreat pavilion and carved stone to record it.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuzu's grandfather was Governor of Yan, he built a retreat pavilion on a small hill south of Zheng city and carved stone to record it.

sentences.zh: 述祖時年九歲。

translations.literal: Shuzu was then nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu was then nine years old.

sentences.zh: 及為刺史，往尋舊跡，得一破石，有銘云：「中嶽先生鄭道昭之白雲堂。

translations.literal: When he became governor he went to seek the old site and found a broken stone with an inscription: "The Hall of White Clouds of Zheng Daozhao, Master of the Central Marchmount."
translations.idiomatic: When he became governor he went to seek the old site and found a broken stone inscribed: "The Hall of White Clouds of Zheng Daozhao, Master of the Central Marchmount."

sentences.zh: 」述祖對之嗚咽，悲動群寮。

translations.literal: " Facing it Shuzu sobbed, and his grief moved the whole staff.
translations.idiomatic: " Facing it Shuzu sobbed, and his grief moved the whole staff.

sentences.zh: 有人入市盜布，其父怒曰：「何負吾君？

translations.literal: Someone entered the market and stole cloth; his father grew angry and said: "How have you failed my lord?
translations.idiomatic: Someone entered the market and stole cloth; his father grew angry and said, "How have you failed my lord?

sentences.zh: 」執之以歸首。

translations.literal: " He seized him and brought him to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized him and brought him in to surrender.

sentences.zh: 述祖特原之，自是境內無盜。

translations.literal: Shuzu specially pardoned him; from then on there were no thieves within his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu specially pardoned him; from then on there were no thieves in his territory.

sentences.zh: 百姓歌曰：「大鄭公，小鄭公，相去五十載，風教猶尚同。」

translations.literal: The common people sang: "The great Lord Zheng, the little Lord Zheng—fifty years apart, yet their customs and teaching are still the same."
translations.idiomatic: The common people sang, "The great Lord Zheng, the little Lord Zheng—fifty years apart, yet their customs and teaching are still the same."

sentences.zh: 述祖能鼓琴，自造《龍吟十弄》，雲嘗夢人彈琴，寤而寫得。

translations.literal: Shuzu could play the zither and himself composed the "Ten Pieces of Dragon Song"; he said that once he dreamed someone playing the zither and on waking wrote it down.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu could play the zither and composed the "Ten Pieces of Dragon Song" himself; he said he once dreamed someone playing the zither and wrote it down on waking.

sentences.zh: 當時以為絕妙。

translations.literal: At the time it was considered matchlessly fine.
translations.idiomatic: At the time it was considered matchlessly fine.

sentences.zh: 所在好為山池，松竹交植，盛肴饌以待賓客，將迎不倦。

translations.literal: Wherever he was he liked to make hill pools; pine and bamboo interplanted; he set out lavish feasts to await guests and welcomed them tirelessly.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he liked to build hill pools with pine and bamboo interplanted, set out lavish feasts for guests, and welcome them tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 少時在鄉，單馬出行，忽有騎者數百，見述祖皆下馬，曰「公在此」，行列而拜。

translations.literal: When young in the countryside, riding alone, suddenly several hundred horsemen appeared; seeing Shuzu they all dismounted, saying "The lord is here," and lined up to bow.
translations.idiomatic: When young in the countryside, riding alone, he suddenly encountered several hundred horsemen who, seeing Shuzu, all dismounted, saying "The lord is here," and lined up to bow.

sentences.zh: 述祖顧問從人，皆不見，心甚異之。

translations.literal: Shuzu looked back to ask his attendants—they all saw nothing—and his heart was deeply startled.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu looked back to ask his attendants—they saw nothing—and his heart was deeply startled.

sentences.zh: 未幾被徵，終曆顯位。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned and in the end passed through eminent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned and in the end rose to eminent posts.

sentences.zh: 及病篤，乃自言之。

translations.literal: When gravely ill he spoke of it himself.
translations.idiomatic: When gravely ill he spoke of it himself.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「吾老矣，一生富貴足矣，以清白之名遺子孫，死無所恨。

translations.literal: And he said: "I am old; a lifetime of wealth and honor is enough; to leave a name of integrity to my descendants—in death I have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: And he said, "I am old; a lifetime of wealth and honor is enough; to leave a name of integrity to my descendants—in death I have no regret.

sentences.zh: 」前後行瀛、殷、冀、滄、趙、定六州事，正除懷、兗、光三州刺史，又重行殷、懷、趙三州刺史，所在皆有惠政。

translations.literal: " Before and after he administered the affairs of six provinces—Ying, Yin, Ji, Cang, Zhao, and Ding; was formally appointed Governor of Huai, Yan, and Guang provinces; and again served as Governor of Yin, Huai, and Zhao—in every place he had benevolent administration.
translations.idiomatic: " He administered the affairs of six provinces—Ying, Yin, Ji, Cang, Zhao, and Ding; was formally appointed Governor of Huai, Yan, and Guang; and again served as Governor of Yin, Huai, and Zhao—in every place his administration was benevolent.

sentences.zh: 天統元年卒，年八十一，贈開府、中書監、北豫州刺史，諡曰平簡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiantong he died at age eighty-one; posthumously granted Grand Vanguard General, Director of the Secretariat, Governor of North Yuzhou; posthumous title Lord Pingjian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tiantong he died at age eighty-one; posthumously granted Grand Vanguard General, Director of the Secretariat, and Governor of North Yuzhou; posthumous title Lord Pingjian (Balanced and Simple).

sentences.zh: 述祖女為趙郡王睿妃，述祖常坐受王拜，命坐，王乃坐。

translations.literal: Shuzu's daughter was consort of Prince of Zhao commandery Rui; Shuzu would habitually sit and receive the prince's bow; when ordered to sit, the prince then sat.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu's daughter was consort to Prince of Zhao commandery Rui; Shuzu would habitually sit and receive the prince's bow, and only when ordered to sit would the prince sit.

sentences.zh: 妃薨後，王更娶鄭道廕女，王坐受道廕拜。

translations.literal: After the consort died, the prince married the daughter of Zheng Daoyin; the prince sat and received Daoyin's bow.
translations.idiomatic: After the consort died, the prince married the daughter of Zheng Daoyin; the prince sat and received Daoyin's bow.

sentences.zh: 王命坐，乃敢坐。

translations.literal: When the prince ordered him to sit, only then did he dare to sit.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the prince ordered him to sit did he dare to sit.

sentences.zh: 王謂道廕曰：「鄭尚書風德如此，又貴重宿舊，君不得並之。」

translations.literal: The prince said to Daoyin: "Director Zheng's bearing and virtue are such, and he also honors old friends of long standing—you cannot be put on a par with him."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said to Daoyin, "Director Zheng's bearing and virtue are such, and he also honors old friends of long standing—you cannot be put on a par with him."

sentences.zh: 述祖子元德，多藝術，官琅邪太守。

translations.literal: Shuzu's son Yuande was skilled in many arts and held the post of Governor of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu's son Yuande was skilled in many arts and served as Governor of Langye.

sentences.zh: 述祖弟遵祖，秘書郎，贈光州刺史。

translations.literal: Shuzu's younger brother Zunzu was Gentleman of the Secretariat; posthumously granted Governor of Guang province.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu's younger brother Zunzu was Gentleman of the Secretariat; posthumously granted Governor of Guang province.

sentences.zh: 遵祖弟順祖，卒于太常丞。

translations.literal: Zunzu's younger brother Shunzu died while serving as Assistant Director of the Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Zunzu's younger brother Shunzu died while serving as Assistant Director of the Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 自靈太后豫政，淫風稍行；

translations.literal: From the time Empress Lingyu took forehand in government, dissolute conduct gradually spread;
translations.idiomatic: From the time Empress Lingyu took forehand in government, dissolute conduct gradually spread;

sentences.zh: 及元叉擅權，公為奸穢，自此素族名家，遂多亂雜。

translations.literal: When Yuan Cha monopolized power, openly practiced wicked and defiling acts, and from then on great clans and eminent families became much mixed and disorderly.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Cha monopolized power and openly practiced wicked and defiling acts, great clans and eminent families became increasingly mixed and disorderly.

sentences.zh: 法官不加糾正，婚宦無貶，于時有識，咸以歎息矣。

translations.literal: The law officers did not correct them, marriages and offices suffered no disgrace—in that age the discerning all sighed over it.
translations.idiomatic: The law officers did not correct them, and marriages and offices suffered no disgrace—in that age the discerning all sighed over it.

sentences.zh: 羲長兄白驎，次小白，次洞林，次叔夜，次連山，並恃豪門，多行無禮，鄉黨之內，疾之若仇。

translations.literal: Xi's eldest brother Bailin, next Xiaobai, next Donglin, next Shuye, next Lianshan—all relied on their powerful house, often behaved without propriety; within the native community they were hated as enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's eldest brother Bailin, next Xiaobai, next Donglin, next Shuye, next Lianshan—all relied on their powerful house and often behaved without propriety; within the native community they were hated as enemies.

sentences.zh: 小白位中書博士。

translations.literal: Xiaobai held the post of Doctor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobai held the post of Doctor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 子胤伯，有當世器幹，孝文納其女為嬪，位東徐州刺史，卒于鴻臚少卿，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: His son Yinbo had talent and capability for the age; Emperor Xiaowen took his daughter as an imperial concubine; he held the post of Governor of East Xuzhou, died while serving as Vice Minister of Ceremonial Hosts; posthumous title Jian (Simple).
translations.idiomatic: His son Yinbo had talent and capability for the age; Emperor Xiaowen took his daughter as an imperial concubine; he served as Governor of East Xuzhou and died while serving as Vice Minister of Ceremonial Hosts; posthumous title Jian (Simple).

sentences.zh: 子希俊，未官而卒。

translations.literal: His son Xijun died before taking office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xijun died before taking office.

sentences.zh: 子道育，武定中，開封太守。

translations.literal: His son Daoyu, during Wuding, was Governor of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daoyu served as Governor of Kaifeng during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 希俊弟幼儒，好學修謹，丞相、高陽王雍以女妻之。

translations.literal: Xijun's younger brother Youru loved learning and cultivated prudence; the Chancellor, Prince of Gaoyang Yong, gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Xijun's younger brother Youru loved learning and cultivated prudence; the Chancellor, Prince of Gaoyang Yong, gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 位司州別駕，有當官稱。

translations.literal: He held the post of Vice-Governor of Sizhou and had a reputation suited to office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice-Governor of Sizhou and had a reputation suited to office.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈散騎常侍、兗州刺史，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Governor of Yan province; posthumous title Su (Solemn).
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously granted Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and Governor of Yan province; posthumous title Su (Solemn).

sentences.zh: 幼儒亡後，妻淫蕩凶悖，肆行無禮。

translations.literal: After Youru's death, his wife was dissolute, violent, and rebellious, and behaved without propriety at will.
translations.idiomatic: After Youru's death, his wife was dissolute, violent, and rebellious, and behaved without propriety at will.

sentences.zh: 幼儒時望甚優，其從兄伯猷每謂所親曰：「從弟人才，足為令德，不幸得如此婦。

translations.literal: Youru's reputation in his time was excellent; his older cousin Boyou often told those close to him: "My younger cousin's talent is sufficient for fine virtue—unfortunately he obtained such a wife."
translations.idiomatic: Youru had enjoyed an excellent reputation in his day. His elder cousin Boyou often told intimates, "My younger cousin's talent was sufficient for a life of fine virtue—yet fate gave him such a wife."

sentences.zh: 今死復重死，可為悲歎。」

translations.literal: Now he has died and again there is a second death—how lamentable."
translations.idiomatic: Now he is dead, and she will visit death upon him a second time—how lamentable!"

sentences.zh: 幼儒子敬道、敬德，俱仕西魏。

translations.literal: Youru's sons Jingdao and Jingde both served Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Youru's sons Jingdao and Jingde both served Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 敬道並巴、開、新三州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingdao together [served as governor of] the three prefectures of Ba, Kai, and Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Jingdao served in turn as governor of Ba, Kai, and Xin prefectures.

sentences.zh: 敬道子正則仕周，復州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingdao's son Zhengze served Zhou; [he was] Governor of Fu prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jingdao's son Zhengze served the Zhou dynasty as Governor of Fu prefecture.

sentences.zh: 胤伯弟平城，廣陵王羽納其女為妃，位東平原太守。

translations.literal: Yinbo's younger brother Pingcheng—Prince of Guangling Yu took his daughter as consort—held the post of Administrator of Eastern Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yinbo's younger brother Pingcheng had his daughter taken as consort by Prince of Guangling Yu and held the post of Administrator of Eastern Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 性猜狂使酒，為政貪殘。

translations.literal: By nature suspicious, reckless, and given to drink; in governance greedy and cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious by nature, reckless with wine, he governed with greed and cruelty.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈南青州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Governor of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted the title Governor of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 長子伯猷，博學有文才，早知名。

translations.literal: The eldest son Boyou was broadly learned, possessed literary talent, and early gained renown.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Boyou was broadly learned and possessed literary talent; he gained renown early.

sentences.zh: 舉司州秀才，曆太學博士，領殿中御史。

translations.literal: Nominated as xiucai of Sizhou; successively served as Erudite of the Imperial University and concurrently as Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated as a xiucai of Sizhou, he served successively as Erudite of the Imperial University and concurrently as Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 與當時名勝，咸申遊款。

translations.literal: With the celebrated figures of the time, he all extended friendly visits.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated cordial ties with all the celebrated figures of the age.

sentences.zh: 明帝釋奠，詔伯猷錄義。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming performed the libation sacrifice, he ordered Boyou to record the ritual exposition.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming performed the libation sacrifice, he ordered Boyou to record the ritual exposition.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書外兵郎中，典起居注，以軍功賜爵陽武子。

translations.literal: Later he was External Troops Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, in charge of the Imperial Diary, and for military achievement was granted the title Viscount of Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as External Troops Gentleman of the Masters of Writing and kept the Imperial Diary; for military achievement he was granted the title Viscount of Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 節閔帝初，以舅氏超授征東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Jiemin's reign, because of his maternal uncle's house he was exceptionally granted General Who Pacifies the East and Household Counsellor with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and concurrently Director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Jiemin's reign, through his maternal uncle's influence he was exceptionally granted the posts of General Who Pacifies the East and Household Counsellor with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and concurrently served as Director of the National University.

sentences.zh: 轉護軍將軍，賜爵武城子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General Who Protects the Army and granted the title Viscount of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General Who Protects the Army and granted the title Viscount of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 元象初，以本官兼散騎常侍使梁。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanxiang, in his original office he concurrently served as Regular Cavalier Attendant and envoy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanxiang era, retaining his original post he concurrently served as Regular Cavalier Attendant and envoy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 前後使人，梁武令其侯王于馬射之日宴對申禮。

translations.literal: Envoys before and after him—Emperor Wu of Liang ordered his marquises and kings on the day of mounted archery to feast together and extend ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: For earlier and later envoys alike, Emperor Wu of Liang had his marquises and kings feast with them and extend full ritual courtesy on the day of mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 伯猷之行，梁武令其領軍將軍臧盾與之接。

translations.literal: When Boyou went on his mission, Emperor Wu of Liang ordered General of the Garrison Zang Dun to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: When Boyou went on his mission, Emperor Wu of Liang ordered General of the Garrison Zang Dun to receive him instead.

sentences.zh: 議者以此貶之。

translations.literal: Commentators thereby demeaned him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators demeaned him for this slight.

sentences.zh: 使還，除南青州刺史。

translations.literal: On returning from his mission, he was appointed Governor of Southern Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his mission, he was appointed Governor of Southern Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 在官貪婪，妻安豐王元延明女，專為聚斂，貨賄公行，潤及親戚。

translations.literal: In office he was greedy; his wife was daughter of Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming—she alone engaged in squeezing wealth, bribes went openly, profit reaching kin.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy in office, he took as wife the daughter of Prince of Anfeng Yuan Yanming, who alone squeezed the province for wealth; bribes flowed openly and profit reached their kin.

sentences.zh: 戶口逃散，邑落空虛。

translations.literal: Households fled and scattered; districts became empty and desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Households fled until the districts stood empty and desolate.

sentences.zh: 乃誣陷良善，雲欲反叛，籍其資財，盡以入己，誅其丈夫，婦女配沒。

translations.literal: Then he framed good people, saying they intended rebellion, registered their property, and took it all for himself; he executed their husbands and assigned their women to penal service.
translations.idiomatic: Then he framed upright citizens on charges of rebellion, seized their property for himself, executed their husbands, and consigned their wives to penal servitude.

sentences.zh: 百姓冤苦，聲聞四方。

translations.literal: The common people suffered injustice; the clamor reached the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The people groaned under injustice until word of it reached the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 為御史糾劾，死罪數十條。

translations.literal: The Censorate impeached him; several dozen capital offenses.
translations.idiomatic: The Censorate impeached him on several dozen capital counts.

sentences.zh: 遇赦免，因以頓廢。

translations.literal: He encountered an amnesty and was spared; thereby he fell into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty spared his life, but his career was ruined.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄作相，每誡厲朝士，常以伯猷及崔叔仁為喻。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang of Qi served as chancellor, he often admonished court officials, always taking Boyou and Cui Shuren as cautionary examples.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxiang of Qi served as chancellor, he often warned court officials, holding up Boyou and Cui Shuren as cautionary examples.

sentences.zh: 武定七年，除太常卿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Wuding, he was appointed Minister of Ceremonial Hosts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wuding, he was appointed Minister of Ceremonial Hosts.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈驃騎大將軍、中書監、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and Governor of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 子蘊，太子舍人、陽夏太守。

translations.literal: His son Yun [served as] Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Governor of Yangxia.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yun served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Governor of Yangxia.

sentences.zh: 伯猷弟仲衡，武定中，儀同開府中郎。

translations.literal: Boyou's younger brother Zhongheng, during Wuding, was Parallel Opening-Fu Secretariat Gentleman with Protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Boyou's younger brother Zhongheng served during Wuding as Parallel Opening-Fu Secretariat Gentleman with Protocol.

sentences.zh: 仲衡弟輯之，司徒諮議。

translations.literal: Zhongheng's younger brother Jizhi was Consulting Censor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongheng's younger brother Jizhi served as Consulting Censor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 齊大寧中，以軍功賜爵成皋男，位金紫光祿大夫，東濟北太守、肥城戍主。

translations.literal: During the Daning era of Qi, for military achievement he was granted the title Baron of Chenggao; he held the post of Household Counsellor with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Governor of Eastern Jibei, and Garrison Commander of Feicheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daning era of Qi, for military achievement he was granted the title Baron of Chenggao and held the posts of Household Counsellor with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Governor of Eastern Jibei, and Garrison Commander of Feicheng.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈度支尚書、北豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously granted Minister of Revenue and Governor of Northern Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Minister of Revenue and Governor of Northern Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 輯之弟懷孝，司徒諮議。

translations.literal: Jizhi's younger brother Huaixiao was Consulting Censor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhi's younger brother Huaixiao served as Consulting Censor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 齊大寧中，仁州刺史。

translations.literal: During the Daning era of Qi, [he was] Governor of Ren prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daning era of Qi, he served as Governor of Ren prefecture.

sentences.zh: 洞林子敬叔，滎陽邑中正、濮陽太守，坐貪穢除名。

translations.literal: Donglin's son Jingshu was Rectifier of Yingyang district and Governor of Puyang; for greed and corruption he was dismissed from name.
translations.idiomatic: Donglin's son Jingshu served as Rectifier of Yingyang district and Governor of Puyang; for greed and corruption he was stricken from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 子籍，字承宗，徐州平東府長史。

translations.literal: His son Ji, styled Chengzong, was Chief Clerk of Pingdong Prefectural Headquarters in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji, styled Chengzong, served as Chief Clerk of the Pingdong Prefectural Headquarters in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 籍弟瓊，字祖珍，有強幹稱，位范陽太守，頗有聲，卒。

translations.literal: Ji's younger brother Qiong, styled Zuzhen, had a reputation for strong capability; he held the post of Governor of Fanyang, had considerable renown, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's younger brother Qiong, styled Zuzhen, was known for strong capability; he served as Governor of Fanyang with considerable renown until his death.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，弟儼寵要，重贈青州刺史。

translations.literal: During Xiaochang, because his younger brother Yan was favored and influential, [Qiong] was again posthumously granted Governor of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiaochang era, because his younger brother Yan was favored and influential at court, Qiong was again posthumously granted the title Governor of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 瓊兄弟雍睦，其諸娣姒亦咸相親愛，閨門之內，有無相通，為時人所稱美。

translations.literal: The Qiong brothers were harmonious; their sisters-in-law also all cherished one another; within the women's quarters, when there was something to have or not have they communicated it—praised by people of the time.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiong brothers lived in harmony, and their sisters-in-law cherished one another as well; within the inner quarters they shared whatever they had or lacked—a bond people of the time praised.

sentences.zh: 子道邕。

translations.literal: His son Daoyong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Daoyong.

sentences.zh: 道邕字孝穆。

translations.literal: Daoyong styled Xiaomu.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyong, styled Xiaomu.

sentences.zh: 幼謹厚，以清約自居，年未弱冠，涉歷經史。

translations.literal: In youth prudent and honest, he made austerity his standard; before reaching twenty he had traversed the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Prudent and honest from youth, he held to austerity as his standard; before he was twenty he had traversed the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 父叔四人並早歿，昆服季之中，道邕居長，撫訓諸弟，有如同生，閨庭之中，怡怡如也。

translations.literal: His father and four uncles all died early; among his brothers in the mourning garments, Daoyong was eldest—instructing and guiding his younger brothers as if they shared one birth; within the family, all was harmonious delight.
translations.idiomatic: His father and four uncles had all died young; among the brothers in mourning garments Daoyong was eldest, raising and guiding his younger brothers as though they were born of one womb, and the household was filled with harmonious delight.

sentences.zh: 魏孝昌初，解褐太尉行參軍，累以戰功進至左光祿大夫、太師咸陽王長史。

translations.literal: In early Xiaochang of Wei, he left the turban for the post of Acting Aide of the Grand Marshal; through successive military achievements he advanced to Household Counsellor of the Left and Chief Clerk to Prince of Xianyang, Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In early Xiaochang of Wei he entered service as Acting Aide of the Grand Marshal, and through successive military achievements advanced to Household Counsellor of the Left and Chief Clerk to the Grand Master, Prince of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 及孝武西遷，從入關，除司徒左長史，領臨洮王友，賜爵永甯縣侯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, he followed into Guan; was appointed Chief Clerk of the Left of the Secretariat, concurrently Friend to the Prince of Lintao, and granted the title Marquis of Yongning county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu moved west, Daoyong followed him into Guan, was appointed Chief Clerk of the Left of the Secretariat, concurrently Friend to the Prince of Lintao, and granted the title Marquis of Yongning county.

sentences.zh: 大統中，行岐州刺史，在任未幾，有能名。

translations.literal: During the great enterprise [of Western Wei], he served as acting Governor of Qi prefecture; in office not many days, he had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: During the great enterprise he served as acting Governor of Qi prefecture; though his tenure was brief, he earned a reputation for competence.

sentences.zh: 王羆時為雍州刺史，欽其善政，貽書盛相稱述。

translations.literal: Wang Pi at the time was Governor of Yong prefecture; he admired his good governance and sent a letter lavishing praise.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi, then Governor of Yong prefecture, admired his governance and sent a letter lavishing praise upon it.

sentences.zh: 先是，所部百姓，久遭離亂，逃散殆盡。

translations.literal: Before this, the common people of his district had long suffered disorder and dispersal; those who fled were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: Before his arrival, the people of his district had long suffered war and chaos until nearly all had fled.

sentences.zh: 道邕下車之日，戶止三千，留情綏撫，遠近咸至，數年之內，有四萬家。

translations.literal: On the day Daoyong took office, registered households numbered only three thousand; he devoted care to soothing and gathering them, and those far and near all came; within several years there were forty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: On the day Daoyong took office, registered households numbered only three thousand; he devoted himself to soothing and gathering the people, and those far and near all returned; within a few years the district held forty thousand households.

sentences.zh: 歲考績為天下最，周文帝賜書歎美之。

translations.literal: In the annual performance review he ranked first in the realm; the Duke of Zhou sent a letter sighing in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: In the annual review of officials he ranked first in the realm, and the Duke of Zhou sent a letter sighing in admiration.

sentences.zh: 徵拜京兆尹。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Governor of Jingzhao [the capital region].
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed Governor of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 及梁岳陽王蕭察稱蕃，乃假道邕散騎常侍，持節拜察為梁王。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Yueyang of Liang, Xiao Cha, declared himself a vassal, [the court] provisionally appointed Daoyong Regular Cavalier Attendant and commissioned him with credentials to invest Cha as King of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang Prince of Yueyang, Xiao Cha, declared himself a vassal, the court appointed Daoyong Regular Cavalier Attendant and sent him with credentials to invest Cha as King of Liang.

sentences.zh: 使還，稱旨，進儀同三司，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: On returning from his mission, his performance matched the imperial wish; he advanced to Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and was given additional appointment as Regular Cavalier Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his mission, his performance matched the emperor's intent; he was advanced to Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies and given additional appointment as Regular Cavalier Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時周文東討，除大丞相府右長史，封金鄉縣男。

translations.literal: At the time the Duke of Zhou campaigned eastward; he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Right of the Grand Chancellor's Office and enfeoffed as Baron of Jinxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke of Zhou campaigned eastward, he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Right of the Grand Chancellor's Office and enfeoffed as Baron of Jinxiang county.

sentences.zh: 軍次潼關，命道邕與左長史孫儉、司馬楊寬、尚書蘇亮、諮議劉孟良等分掌眾務。

translations.literal: The army halted at Tong Pass; he ordered Daoyong with Chief Clerk of the Left Sun Jian, Major Sun Kuan, Master of Writing Su Liang, Consulting Censor Liu Mengliang and others to divide and manage the mass of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Tong Pass, and the Duke ordered Daoyong, with Chief Clerk of the Left Sun Jian, Major Sun Kuan, Master of Writing Su Liang, Consulting Censor Liu Mengliang, and others, to divide the management of affairs among themselves.

sentences.zh: 仍令道邕引接關東歸附人士，並品藻才行而任用之，撫納銓敘，咸得其宜。

translations.literal: He then ordered Daoyong to receive and deal with gentry of the eastern passes who had submitted, appraising their ability and conduct and assigning office accordingly—soothing, accepting, and arranging ranks, all obtaining what was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: He then charged Daoyong with receiving the gentry of the eastern passes who had submitted, appraising their ability and conduct before assigning office, so that in soothing them and arranging their ranks all was done as it should be.

sentences.zh: 後拜中書令，賜姓宇文氏，尋以疾免。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Master of Writing; granted the surname Yuwen; soon after, on account of illness he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed Master of Writing and granted the surname Yuwen; soon after he resigned on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 周孝閔帝踐阼，加驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司，進爵為子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, he was given additional appointment as General of Agile Cavalry and Parallel Opening-Fu with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies; his noble rank advanced to viscount.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin of Zhou ascended the throne, Daoyong was given additional appointment as General of Agile Cavalry and Parallel Opening-Fu with Protocol Equal to the Three Excellencies, and his noble rank advanced to viscount.

sentences.zh: 曆禦伯中大夫、禦正、宜、華、虞、陝四州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively held the posts of Grandee of the Imperial Chariots, Director of the Left, and governor of Yi, Hua, Yu, and Shaan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He successively held the posts of Grandee of the Imperial Chariots, Director of the Left, and governor of Yi, Hua, Yu, and Shaan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 頻歷數州，皆有政績。

translations.literal: Serving in several prefectures in succession, he all had achievements in governance.
translations.idiomatic: In each prefecture he served, he left a record of achievement.

sentences.zh: 入為少司空，卒。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Vice Minister of Works and died.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Vice Minister of Works and died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈本官，加鄭、梁、北豫三州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: His original office was posthumously granted; additionally Governor of Zheng, Liang, and Northern Yu prefectures; posthumous title Zhen (Upright).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted his final offices plus governorship of Zheng, Liang, and Northern Yu prefectures, with the posthumous title Zhen (Upright).

sentences.zh: 子詡嗣，歷位納言，為聘陳使。

translations.literal: His son Xu inherited; successively held the post of Director of Statements and served as envoy on a mission of betrothal to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu inherited the line, served in turn as Director of Statements, and led a betrothal mission to Chen.

sentences.zh: 後至開府儀同大將軍、邵州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he reached Parallel Opening-Fu Great General and Governor of Shao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later he rose to Parallel Opening-Fu Great General and Governor of Shao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詡弟譯于隋文帝有翊贊功，開皇初，又追贈道邕大將軍、徐兗等六州刺史，改諡曰文。

translations.literal: Xu's younger brother Yi had merit in assisting Emperor Wen of Sui; in early Kaihuang, Daoyong was again posthumously granted Great General and Governor of the six prefectures of Xu and Yan, and his posthumous title changed to Wen (Cultured).
translations.idiomatic: Xu's younger brother Yi had aided Emperor Wen of Sui in securing the throne; in early Kaihuang, Daoyong was again posthumously granted Great General and governorship of six prefectures including Xu and Yan, and his posthumous title was changed to Wen (Cultured).

sentences.zh: 譯字正義。

translations.literal: Yi styled Zhengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Zhengyi.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，涉獵群書，工騎射，尤善音樂，有名於世。

translations.literal: In youth clever and keen, he ranged through many books, skilled at mounted archery, especially skilled at music—famed in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Clever and keen from youth, he ranged through many books, was skilled at mounted archery, and above all excelled at music—a name known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 譯從祖文寬，尚周文帝元後妹魏平陽公主，無子，周文命譯後之。

translations.literal: Yi's paternal cousin Wen Kuan married the younger sister of Empress Yuan, Princess of Pingyang of Wei, to Emperor Wen of Zhou—without sons; Emperor Wen ordered Yi to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's paternal cousin Wen Kuan had married the younger sister of Empress Yuan, Princess of Pingyang of Wei, yet had no sons; Emperor Wen of Zhou ordered Yi to succeed the line.

sentences.zh: 由是譯少為周文所親，恆令與諸子遊集。

translations.literal: Because of this, from youth Yi was close to Emperor Wen, who constantly had him join in roaming and gatherings with the [imperial] sons.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Yi was close to Emperor Wen from youth, who constantly had him join the princes in their gatherings.

sentences.zh: 年十餘歲，嘗詣府司錄李長宗。

translations.literal: When he was not yet fully grown, he once went to visit the Chief Clerk of the Office Li Changzong.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was fully grown, he once visited the Chief Clerk of the office, Li Changzong.

sentences.zh: 長宗於眾中戲之，譯斂容謂曰：「明公位望不輕，瞻仰斯屬，輒相玩狎，無乃喪德也。

translations.literal: Changzong toyed with him before the assembly; Yi composed himself and said to him: "Your Lordship's position and dignity are not light—the hopes of many look to you; yet you casually jest and toy—would this not be losing virtue?
translations.idiomatic: In the assembly Changzong jested with him, but Yi composed himself and said, "Your Lordship's station and dignity are no light matter—many eyes look to you. To jest and toy so casually—would that not be to lose virtue?

sentences.zh: 」長宗甚異之。

translations.literal: " Changzong was greatly struck by him.
translations.idiomatic: Changzong was deeply struck by this.

sentences.zh: 文寬後誕二子，譯復歸本生。

translations.literal: Wen Kuan later bore two sons; Yi returned to his birth father.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Kuan later fathered two sons, and Yi returned to his birth family.

sentences.zh: 周明帝時，詔令事輔城公，是為武帝。

translations.literal: During the time of Emperor Ming of Zhou, he was ordered to attend the Prince of Fucheng—that is, Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Ming of Zhou he was ordered to attend Prince of Fucheng—who would become Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 及帝即位，為左侍上士，與儀同劉昉，恆侍帝側。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, [Yi] was Left Attendant Upper Gentleman; with Parallel Protocol Liu Fang he constantly attended at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor ascended the throne, Yi served as Left Attendant Upper Gentleman and, with Parallel Protocol Liu Fang, constantly attended at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 譯時喪妻，帝令譯尚梁安固公主。

translations.literal: At the time Yi was in mourning for his wife; the emperor ordered Yi to marry the Princess of Angu of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yi was mourning his wife; the emperor ordered him to marry the Princess of Angu of Liang.

sentences.zh: 及帝親總萬機，以為禦正下大夫，頗被顧遇。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally took charge of all affairs, [Yi] was made Lower Grand Master of the Imperial Rectification, and received considerable favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally took charge of affairs, Yi was made Lower Grand Master of the Imperial Rectification and enjoyed considerable favor.

sentences.zh: 東宮建，轉太子宮尹下大夫，特被太子親待。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was transferred to Lower Grand Master of the Heir Apparent's Household and received the heir apparent's personal regard.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Palace was established, he was transferred to Lower Grand Master of the Heir Apparent's Household and won the heir apparent's personal regard.

sentences.zh: 時太子多失德，內史中大夫烏丸軌每勸帝廢太子立秦王，由是太子恆不自安。

translations.literal: At the time the heir apparent often fell short in conduct; Internal Historian Zhongheng Wuyuan Gui often urged the emperor to depose the heir apparent and establish the Prince of Qin—wherefore the heir apparent was constantly ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent often fell short in conduct, and Internal Historian Wuyuan Gui frequently urged the emperor to depose him and establish the Prince of Qin; the heir apparent therefore lived in constant unease.

sentences.zh: 建德二年，為聘齊使副。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiande, he served as deputy on the betrothal mission to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiande he served as deputy on a betrothal mission to Qi.

sentences.zh: 後詔太子西征吐谷渾，太子陰謂譯曰：「秦王，上愛子也；

translations.literal: Later the emperor ordered the heir apparent to campaign west against Tuyuhun; the heir apparent secretly said to Yi: "The Prince of Qin is the emperor's beloved son;
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor ordered the heir apparent to campaign west against Tuyuhun; the heir apparent told Yi in private, "The Prince of Qin is the emperor's beloved son;

sentences.zh: 烏丸軌，上信臣也，今吾此行，得無扶蘇之事乎？

translations.literal: Wuyuan Gui is the emperor's trusted minister; now on this expedition of mine, might there not be a matter like Fusu?"
translations.idiomatic: Wuyuan Gui is the emperor's trusted minister. On this expedition of mine, might there not come to pass what befell Fusu?"

sentences.zh: 」譯曰：「願殿下勉著仁孝，無失子道而已。

translations.literal: Yi said: "I hope Your Highness will strive to display benevolence and filial piety, not failing in the son's way—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Your Highness need only strive to show benevolence and filial piety and not fail in a son's duty—that is all."

sentences.zh: 」太子然之。

translations.literal: The heir apparent assented.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent accepted this.

sentences.zh: 既破賊，譯以功最，賜爵開國子。

translations.literal: After defeating the enemy, Yi for greatest achievement was granted the title Viscount Who Establishes the State.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating the enemy, Yi was granted the title Viscount Who Establishes the State for the greatest achievement.

sentences.zh: 後坐褻狎皇太子，烏丸軌、宇文孝伯等以聞。

translations.literal: Later for indecent familiarity with the crown prince, Wuyuan Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo and others reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for indecent familiarity with the crown prince, Wuyuan Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo, and others reported him to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，除譯名。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and struck Yi's name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and struck Yi's name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 宮臣親幸者咸被譴。

translations.literal: The palace attendants who were personally favored were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: All the palace attendants who had enjoyed the crown prince's favor were punished.

sentences.zh: 太子復召譯，戲狎如初。

translations.literal: The heir apparent summoned Yi again, and their indecent jesting was as before.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent summoned Yi again, and their familiar jesting resumed as before.

sentences.zh: 因曰：「殿下何時可得據天下？

translations.literal: He then said: "Your Highness, when will you be able to possess the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi then asked, "Your Highness, when will you be able to possess the realm?"

sentences.zh: 」太子悅而益昵之。

translations.literal: The heir apparent was pleased and drew even closer.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent was pleased and grew even more intimate with him.

sentences.zh: 例復官，仍拜吏部下大夫。

translations.literal: By precedent his office was restored; he was again appointed Lower Grand Master of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent his office was restored, and he was again appointed Lower Grand Master of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 及武帝崩，宣帝嗣位，超拜開府儀同大將軍、內史中大夫，封歸昌縣公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died, Emperor Xuan succeeded; [Yi] was exceptionally granted Parallel Opening-Fu Great General and Internal Historian, enfeoffed as Duke of Guichang county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu died and Emperor Xuan succeeded, Yi was exceptionally granted Parallel Opening-Fu Great General and Internal Historian and enfeoffed as Duke of Guichang county.

sentences.zh: 既以恩舊，任遇甚重，委以朝政。

translations.literal: Because of this old favor, his appointment and treatment were very weighty; he was entrusted with court government.
translations.idiomatic: Because of their old bond of favor, his appointment and treatment were weighty indeed, and court government was entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 遷內史上大夫，進封沛國公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Internal Historian Grand Master; advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Pei.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Internal Historian Grand Master and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Pei.

sentences.zh: 上大夫之官，自譯始也。

translations.literal: The office of Grand Master—from Yi it began.
translations.idiomatic: The office of Senior Grand Master began with Yi.

sentences.zh: 以其子善願為歸昌公，元琮為永安縣男。

translations.literal: His son Shanyuan was made Duke of Guichang; Yuancong was made Baron of Yong'an county.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shanyuan was made Duke of Guichang; Yuancong was made Baron of Yong'an county.

sentences.zh: 又監國史。

translations.literal: He also supervised the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He also supervised compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 譯頗專權，時帝幸東京，譯擅取官材，自營私第，坐除名。

translations.literal: Yi was quite autocratic in power; at the time the emperor was visiting the Eastern Capital, Yi on his own authority took official timber and built a private residence for himself; on account of this he was dismissed and his name struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had grown quite autocratic. While the emperor was away at the Eastern Capital, Yi seized official timber on his own authority and built himself a private mansion; for this he was dismissed and struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 劉昉數言於帝，帝復召之，顧待如初，詔領內史事。

translations.literal: Liu Fang spoke repeatedly to the emperor; the emperor summoned him again, treated him attentively as before, and ordered him to take charge of Internal Historian affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang spoke repeatedly on his behalf, and the emperor summoned Yi again, treating him with the same attentive favor as before and ordering him to oversee Internal Historian affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，隋文帝與譯有同學之舊，譯又素知隋文相表有奇，傾心相結。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Wen of Sui and Yi had the old bond of classmates; Yi had also long known from Yang Jian's physiognomy that there was something extraordinary about him, and devoted his heart to forming a bond.
translations.idiomatic: Long before, Yang Jian and Yi had been classmates, and Yi had long read something extraordinary in Yang Jian's countenance; he gave his heart to forging a bond with him.

sentences.zh: 至是，隋文為宣帝所忌，情不自安，嘗在永巷，私於譯曰：「久願出籓，公所悉也，敢布心腹，少留意焉。

translations.literal: By then Yang Jian was regarded with suspicion by Emperor Xuan and could not feel at ease in his own mind; once in the Eternal Lane he spoke privately to Yi: "For long I have wished to go out to a frontier post—this Your Lordship well knows. I venture to lay bare my inmost heart; give it a little heed."
translations.idiomatic: By then Yang Jian had fallen under Emperor Xuan's suspicion and could not rest easy in his own mind. Once in the Eternal Lane he spoke privately to Yi: "I have long wished to take a post beyond the capital—you know this well. I lay bare my inmost heart to you; give it a little heed."

sentences.zh: 」譯曰：「以公德望，天下歸心，欲求多福，豈敢忘也？

translations.literal: " Yi said: "By virtue of Your Lordship's virtue and standing, all under Heaven turn their hearts to you. Wishing to gain great good fortune—how could I dare forget?"
translations.idiomatic: " Yi said, "By Your Lordship's virtue and standing, the hearts of the realm already turn to you. If I wish my own share of fortune, how could I dare forget you?"

sentences.zh: 謹即言之。

translations.literal: "I shall speak of it at once with due care."
translations.idiomatic: "I shall speak of it at once."

sentences.zh: 」時將遣譯南征。

translations.literal: " At that time they were about to send Yi on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court was about to send Yi on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 譯曰：「若定江東，自非懿戚重臣，無以鎮撫。

translations.literal: Yi said: "If we pacify the lands east of the Yangtze, unless it is an imperial clansman or a weighty minister there will be no means to pacify and console [the region]."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "If we pacify the lands east of the Yangtze, only an imperial kinsman or a minister of the first rank can hold and console the region."

sentences.zh: 可令隋公行，且為壽陽總管，以督軍事。

translations.literal: "Let the Duke of Sui go, and moreover appoint him Shouyang Regional Commander to oversee military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: "Let the Duke of Sui go himself, and appoint him Shouyang regional commander to oversee the armies."

sentences.zh: 」帝從之，乃下詔，以隋文為揚州總管，譯發兵俱會壽陽以代陳。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this; he then issued an edict appointing Yang Jian Yangzhou Regional Commander, and Yi was to raise troops and all meet at Shouyang to replace Chen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed. He issued an edict appointing Yang Jian regional commander of Yangzhou and ordering Yi to raise troops and join him at Shouyang for the campaign against Chen.

sentences.zh: 行有日矣，帝不悆，譯遂與禦正下大夫劉昉謀，引隋文入受顧托。

translations.literal: The day of departure was near when the emperor fell ill; Yi then plotted with Imperial Correctness Lower Grand Master Liu Fang to bring Yang Jian in to receive the dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: The day of departure was near when the emperor fell gravely ill. Yi then plotted with Imperial Correctness Lower Grand Master Liu Fang to bring Yang Jian in and receive the dying charge.

sentences.zh: 既而譯宣詔，文武百官，皆受隋文節度。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi proclaimed the edict; civil and military officials all came under Yang Jian's command.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yi proclaimed the edict, and civil and military officials alike came under Yang Jian's command.

sentences.zh: 時禦正中大夫顏之儀與宦者謀，引大將軍宇文仲輔政。

translations.literal: At the time Imperial Correctness Grand Master Yan Zhiyi plotted with eunuchs to bring in Great General Yuwen Zhong to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Imperial Correctness Grand Master Yan Zhiyi plotted with the eunuchs to bring in Great General Yuwen Zhong to assist in government.

sentences.zh: 仲已至御坐，譯知之，遽率開府楊惠及劉昉、皇甫績、柳裘俱入。

translations.literal: Zhong had already reached the imperial seat when Yi learned of it; he hastily led Parallel Opening-Fu Yang Hui and Liu Fang, Huangfu Ji, and Liu Qiu—all entered together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong had already reached the imperial seat when Yi learned of it. He hastily led Parallel Opening-Fu Yang Hui, Liu Fang, Huangfu Ji, and Liu Qiu in together.

sentences.zh: 仲與之儀見譯等，愕然，逡巡欲出。

translations.literal: Zhong and Zhiyi saw Yi and the others, were startled, and hesitatingly wished to go out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Zhiyi saw Yi and his party, froze in shock, and hesitated as if to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 隋文因執之。

translations.literal: Yang Jian thereupon seized them.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian seized them on the spot.

sentences.zh: 於是矯詔，復以譯為內史上大夫。

translations.literal: Thereupon by a forged edict Yi was again made Internal Historian Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: By a forged edict Yi was restored as Internal Historian Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 明日，隋文為丞相，拜譯柱國、府長史，行內史上大夫事。

translations.literal: The next day Yang Jian became Chancellor; Yi was appointed Pillar of the State and Chief Secretary of the Office, acting Internal Historian Grand Master affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yang Jian became chancellor. Yi was appointed Pillar of the State and chief secretary of the chancellery, with acting authority as Internal Historian Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 及隋文為大塚宰，總百揆，以譯兼領天官都府司會，總六府事。

translations.literal: When Yang Jian became Grand Commander, overseeing all administration, Yi was additionally made Director of the Celestial Office Metropolitan Directorate, overseeing the Six Offices.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became grand commander and took charge of all administration, Yi was additionally made director of the Celestial Office metropolitan directorate, with overall charge of the Six Offices.

sentences.zh: 出入臥內，言無不從，賞賜玉帛，不可勝計，每出入以甲士從。

translations.literal: Entering and leaving the sleeping quarters—his words were never refused; rewards of jade and silk could not be counted; each time he went out and in armored soldiers followed.
translations.idiomatic: He came and went within the ruler's sleeping quarters, and none of his words went unheeded. Rewards of jade and silk poured in beyond counting, and armored guards attended him whenever he went abroad.

sentences.zh: 拜其子元璹為儀同。

translations.literal: His son Yuansui was appointed Parallel Opening-Fu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuansui was appointed Parallel Opening-Fu.

sentences.zh: 時尉遲迥、王謙、司馬消難等作亂，隋文逾加親禮，進上柱國，恕以十死。

translations.literal: When Yuchi Jiong, Wang Qian, Sima Xiaonan and others rebelled, Yang Jian increased his personal courtesy even more, advanced him to Pillar of the State Senior Rank, and pardoned ten capital offenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong, Wang Qian, Sima Xiaonan, and others rose in rebellion, Yang Jian treated him with still greater personal favor, advanced him to senior pillar of the state, and granted pardon for ten capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 譯性輕險，不親職務，而贓貨狼籍。

translations.literal: Yi's nature was frivolous and treacherous; he did not attend to his duties, and bribe goods lay strewn in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was frivolous and treacherous by nature, neglected his duties, and left a trail of bribes strewn in every direction.

sentences.zh: 隋文陰疏之，然以其有定冊功，不忍廢放，陰敕官屬不得白事於譯。

translations.literal: Yang Jian secretly kept him at a distance, yet because he had merit in establishing the succession could not bear to dismiss him; secretly he ordered officials not to report affairs to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian quietly kept him at arm's length, yet because Yi had helped secure the succession he could not bring himself to cast him aside; he secretly ordered officials not to bring business before Yi.

sentences.zh: 譯猶坐査事，無所關預，懼，頓首求解職。

translations.literal: Yi still sat investigating affairs yet had nothing to intervene in; afraid, he kowtowed asking to resign his office.
translations.idiomatic: Yi still sat hearing cases yet had nothing he could actually decide; in fear he kowtowed and asked to be released from office.

sentences.zh: 隋文寬喻之，接以恩禮。

translations.literal: Yang Jian comforted him generously and received him with favor and ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian comforted him generously and received him with the honors due an old ally.

sentences.zh: 及帝受禪，譯以上柱國歸第。

translations.literal: When the emperor accepted the abdication, Yi returned to his residence as Pillar of the State Senior Rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor took the throne, Yi retired to his residence bearing the rank of senior pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 賞賜豐厚，進子元璹成皋郡公，元珣永安男，追贈其父及亡兄二人並為刺史。

translations.literal: Rewards were rich and thick; his son Yuansui was advanced to Duke of Chenggao commandery, Yuanxun Baron of Yong'an; his father and two deceased elder brothers were all posthumously granted governorships of prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: His rewards were lavish: his son Yuansui was advanced to Duke of Chenggao commandery and Yuanxun to Baron of Yong'an; his father and two deceased elder brothers were all posthumously made prefectural governors.

sentences.zh: 譯自以被疏，陰呼道士章醮，以祈福助。

translations.literal: Yi himself thought he was kept at a distance and secretly summoned Daoist priests for liturgical invocations to seek blessing and aid.
translations.idiomatic: Believing himself cast aside, Yi secretly summoned Daoist priests to perform liturgical rites for blessing and aid.

sentences.zh: 其婢奏譯厭蠱左道。

translations.literal: His maidservant reported that Yi practiced malign sorcery and the heterodox Way.
translations.idiomatic: A maidservant reported that Yi had been practicing malign sorcery and heterodox rites.

sentences.zh: 帝謂譯曰：「我不負公，此何意也？

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yi: "I have not failed you—what is the meaning of this?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Yi, "I have never failed you—what is the meaning of this?"

sentences.zh: 」譯無以對。

translations.literal: " Yi had nothing with which to reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi had no answer.

sentences.zh: 譯又與母別居，為憲司所劾，由是除名。

translations.literal: Yi also lived apart from his mother and was impeached by the censorate; because of this his name was struck off.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was also living apart from his mother and was impeached by the censorate; for this his name was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 下詔云：「譯嘉謀良策，寂爾無聞；

translations.literal: An edict was issued saying: "Yi's fine plans and good strategies—in silence no word is heard of them;
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Yi's fine plans and good strategies are heard of no more;

sentences.zh: 鬻獄賣官，沸騰盈耳。

translations.literal: selling judgments and selling offices—these boil and bubble, filling the ears."
translations.idiomatic: yet selling judgments and selling offices boils up everywhere one turns."

sentences.zh: 若留之於世，在人為不道之臣；

translations.literal: If he is kept in the world, among men he is an inhumane minister;
translations.idiomatic: If he is kept among the living, he is an inhumane minister;

sentences.zh: 戮之於朝，入地為不孝之鬼。

translations.literal: if executed in court, entering the earth he becomes an unfilial ghost.
translations.idiomatic: if executed at court, he becomes an unfilial ghost in the earth below.

sentences.zh: 有累幽顯，無以置之。

translations.literal: He burdens both the hidden and the manifest realms; there is no way to place him.
translations.idiomatic: He burdens both the living and the dead; there is no fitting place for him.

sentences.zh: 宜賜以《孝經》，令其熟讀，仍遣與母共居。」

translations.literal: He should be given the Classic of Filial Piety, made to read it thoroughly, and still sent to dwell with his mother."
translations.idiomatic: Let him be given the Classic of Filial Piety to read until he knows it well, and sent home to live with his mother."

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔譯參撰律令。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict ordered Yi to participate in compiling statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict summoned Yi to help compile statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 復授開府、隆州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again granted Parallel Opening-Fu and made Governor of Long prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was again granted Parallel Opening-Fu and appointed governor of Long prefecture.

sentences.zh: 請還療疾，有詔征之，見於醴泉宮，賜宴甚歡。

translations.literal: He requested to return to treat his illness; there was an edict summoning him; he was seen at Liquan Palace and given a banquet with great enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: He asked leave to return and treat his illness; the emperor summoned him back, received him at Liquan Palace, and gave him a banquet of rare warmth.

sentences.zh: 因謂譯曰：「貶退已久，情相矜湣。

translations.literal: He thereupon said to Yi: "Your demotion and withdrawal have lasted long; in my heart I pity and commiserate with you."
translations.idiomatic: He then said to Yi, "Your demotion has lasted long; my heart goes out to you in pity."

sentences.zh: 」於是顧謂侍臣曰：「鄭譯與朕同生共死，間關危難，興言念此，何日忘之。

translations.literal: He then turned to the attending ministers and said: "Zheng Yi and I share life and death; we passed through dangers in peril—raising the subject and thinking on this, what day could I forget it?"
translations.idiomatic: Turning to his attendants he said, "Zheng Yi and I have shared life and death and passed together through every peril. Whenever I speak of it, I wonder what day I could ever forget."

sentences.zh: 」譯因奉觴上壽。

translations.literal: " Yi thereupon raised his goblet and offered wishes for long life.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi raised his goblet and offered wishes for the emperor's long life.

sentences.zh: 帝令內史李德林立作詔書，復爵沛國公，位上柱國。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Internal Historian Li Delin to compose the edict forthwith; [Yi] was restored to Duke of Pei and to the rank of Pillar of the State Senior.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Internal Historian Li Delin to draft the edict on the spot; Yi was restored as Duke of Pei and senior pillar of the state.

sentences.zh: 高熲戲謂譯曰：「筆幹。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong jestingly said to Yi: "The writing stem [your brush]."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong teased Yi: "Quite the brushwork."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「出為方嶽，杖策言歸，不得一錢，何以潤筆！

translations.literal: " He replied: "Going out as a regional lord, returning staff in hand without a single coin—how can I moisten the brush!"
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Sent out as a regional governor, I came home staff in hand without a single coin—how was I to grease the brush?"

sentences.zh: 」上大笑。
