translations.literal: " The emperor laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor laughed aloud.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔譯參議樂事。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict ordered Yi to participate in deliberating musical matters.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict ordered Yi to take part in deliberations on music.

sentences.zh: 譯以周代七聲廢缺，自大隋受命，禮樂宜新。

translations.literal: Yi held that the Zhou dynasty's seven tones had fallen into disuse and were lacking; since the Great Sui received the Mandate, ritual and music ought to be renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi argued that the Zhou dynasty's seven tones had fallen into neglect and disrepair; now that the Great Sui had received the Mandate, ritual and music should be made anew.

sentences.zh: 更修七始之義，名曰《樂府聲調》，凡八篇，奏之。

translations.literal: He further revised the meaning of the Seven Beginnings, titling it Musical Office Tone Modes, eight chapters in all, and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He revised the doctrine of the Seven Beginnings into a work entitled Musical Office Tone Modes, eight chapters in all, and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉美焉。

translations.literal: The emperor commended and admired it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised it highly.

sentences.zh: 俄拜岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Governor of Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed governor of Qi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復奉詔定樂於太常。

translations.literal: More than a year later, he again received an edict to fix music at the Director of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: A year and more later he again received an edict to fix the music at the Directorate of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 帝勞譯曰：「律、令，則公定之；

translations.literal: The emperor comforted Yi saying: "Statutes and ordinances—you fixed them;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Yi, saying, "Statutes and ordinances—you fixed them;

sentences.zh: 音樂，則公正之。

translations.literal: music—you corrected it.
translations.idiomatic: music—you set it right.

sentences.zh: 禮、樂、律、令，公居其三，良足美也。

translations.literal: Of ritual, music, statutes, and ordinances you hold three—quite enough to admire."
translations.idiomatic: Of ritual, music, statutes, and ordinances you hold three—enough to be proud of."

sentences.zh: 」尋還岐州。

translations.literal: " Soon he returned to Qi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he returned to Qi prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開皇十一年卒，年五十二，諡曰達。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang he died, age fifty-two; posthumous title: Da (Accomplished).
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Kaihuang he died at fifty-two; his posthumous title was Da (Accomplished).

sentences.zh: 子元璹嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yuansui succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuansui succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 煬帝初立，五等悉除，以譯佐命元功，詔追改封譯莘公，以元璹襲。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang first took the throne, the five ranks were all abolished; because Yi had primal merit in assisting the mandate, an edict retroactively changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Shen, with Yuansui inheriting.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang first took the throne the five noble ranks were abolished altogether; because Yi had been a founding pillar of the dynasty, an edict retroactively changed his enfeoffment to Duke of Shen, which Yuansui inherited.

sentences.zh: 元璹歷位右光祿大夫、右衛將軍。

translations.literal: Yuansui successively held the posts of Right Director of the Brilliant Fortune Office and Right Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Yuansui rose through the posts of Right Director of the Brilliant Fortune Office and Right Guard General.

sentences.zh: 大業末，為文城太守，以城歸國。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era he was Governor of Wencheng and surrendered the city to [Tang] the state.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he was governor of Wencheng and surrendered the city to the new dynasty.

sentences.zh: 瓊弟儼。

translations.literal: Qiong's younger brother Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong's younger brother Yan.

sentences.zh: 儼字季然，容貌壯麗。

translations.literal: Yan, courtesy name Jiran, with a stalwart and handsome appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, courtesy name Jiran, was tall and strikingly handsome.

sentences.zh: 初為司徒胡國珍行參軍，因為靈太后所幸，時人未知之。

translations.literal: At first he was Acting Retainer under the Minister of Education Huguo Zhen; because he was favored by Empress Dowager Ling, at the time people did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as acting retainer under Minister of Education Huguo Zhen; he had won the favor of Empress Dowager Ling, though at the time the court did not yet know it.

sentences.zh: 後太后廢，蕭寶夤西征，以儼為友。

translations.literal: Later when the empress dowager was deposed, Xiao Baoyin marched west on campaign and made Yan a Friend [of the army].
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the empress dowager was deposed, Xiao Baoyin marched west on campaign and took Yan along as a companion officer.

sentences.zh: 及太后反政，儼請使還朝，復見寵待。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager restored her rule, Yan requested an envoy to return to court and again received favor and attention.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager restored her rule, Yan asked to be sent back to court and again received lavish favor.

sentences.zh: 拜諫議大夫、中書舍人，領尚食典禦，晝夜禁中，寵愛尤甚。

translations.literal: He was appointed Remonstrating and Advising Grand Master and Secretariat Gentleman, concurrently Director of Imperial Food Service; day and night in the inner palace—favor and love were especially great.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed remonstrating adviser and secretariat gentleman, with concurrent charge of the imperial food service; he remained day and night within the inner palace, and the emperor's favor toward him was extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 儼每休沐，太后常遣閹童隨侍，儼見其妻，唯得言家事而已。

translations.literal: Whenever Yan had his rest day, the empress dowager often sent eunuch youths to attend him; when Yan saw his wife he could only speak of household affairs, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Yan took his day of rest, the empress dowager sent eunuch attendants to follow him; when he saw his wife he was permitted to speak only of household matters.

sentences.zh: 與徐紇俱為舍人，儼以紇有智數，仗為謀主。

translations.literal: He and Xu He were both gentlemen of the Secretariat; Yan because He had skill at stratagems relied on him as chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xu He were both secretariat gentlemen; Yan, seeing He's gift for stratagem, relied on him as his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 紇以儼寵倖既盛，傾身承接。

translations.literal: He because Yan's favor and intimacy were already at their height poured body and heart into receiving him.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yan's favor was already at its height, He gave himself over to Yan entirely.

sentences.zh: 共相表裏，勢傾內外。

translations.literal: Together they were inside and outside [allies]; their power overturned inner and outer [court].
translations.idiomatic: Working inside and outside together, their power dominated the court within and without.

sentences.zh: 城陽王徽亦與之合，當時政令，歸於儼等。

translations.literal: Prince of Chengyang Hui also joined with them; the government orders of the time went to Yan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Chengyang, Hui, also joined them, and government orders of the day passed through Yan and his circle.

sentences.zh: 遷散騎常侍、車騎將軍，舍人、常侍如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and Chariots and Cavalry General; Secretariat Gentleman and Regular Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to regular attendant of scattered cavalry and chariots-and-cavalry general, while retaining his posts as secretariat gentleman and regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，事出倉卒，天下咸言儼計。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, the affair came out in haste; all under Heaven said it was Yan's plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died suddenly, all under Heaven said the deed was Yan's doing.

sentences.zh: 爾硃榮舉兵向洛陽，以儼、紇為辭。

translations.literal: Erzhu Rong raised troops toward Luoyang, using Yan and He as his pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Erzhu Rong raised his army toward Luoyang, using Yan and He as his pretext.

sentences.zh: 榮逼京師，儼走歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Rong pressed the capital; Yan fled and returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: As Rong pressed the capital, Yan fled home to his native place.

sentences.zh: 儼從兄仲明欲據郡起眾，尋為其部下所殺，與仲明俱傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: Yan's paternal cousin Zhongming wished to seize the commandery and raise a host; soon he was killed by his subordinates; together with Zhongming their heads were sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's cousin Zhongming tried to seize the commandery and raise troops; soon his own men killed him, and both their heads were sent to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 子文寬從武帝入關西。

translations.literal: His son Wenkuan followed Emperor Wu in entering west of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenkuan followed Emperor Wu west of the Pass.

sentences.zh: 敬叔弟子恭，燕郡太守。

translations.literal: Jingshu's younger brother's son Gong, Governor of Yan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Jingshu's nephew Gong served as governor of Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 孝昌中，因儼勢，除衛尉少卿，遷衛將軍、左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the Xiaochang era, relying on Yan's power, he was appointed Lesser Director of the Guard Command; transferred to Guard General and Left Director of the Brilliant Fortune Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiaochang era, riding Yan's influence, he was made lesser director of the guard command, then transferred to guard general and left director of the brilliant fortune office.

sentences.zh: 卒後，贈尚書右僕射，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: After his death he was posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; posthumous title Zhen (Upright).
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made right vice director of the imperial secretariat, with the posthumous title Zhen (Upright).

sentences.zh: 叔夜子伯夏，位東萊太守。

translations.literal: Shuye's son Bojia, holding the post of Governor of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye's son Bojia served as governor of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈青州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted Governor of Qing prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made governor of Qing prefecture.

sentences.zh: 伯夏弟謹，字仲恭，琅邪太守。

translations.literal: Bojia's younger brother Jin, courtesy name Zhonggong, Governor of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: Bojia's younger brother Jin, courtesy name Zhonggong, was governor of Langye.

sentences.zh: 連山性嚴暴，撾撻僮僕，酷過人理。

translations.literal: Lianshan's nature was severe and violent; he beat and flogged servant boys, cruelty exceeding human reason.
translations.idiomatic: Lianshan was severe and violent by nature, beating and flogging his servants with a cruelty beyond ordinary bounds.

sentences.zh: 父子一時為奴所害，斷首投馬槽下，乘馬北逃。

translations.literal: Father and sons at one time were killed by slaves; their heads were cut off and cast under the horse trough; [the slaves] mounted horses and fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Father and sons were killed at once by their slaves, who cut off their heads and threw them under the horse trough, then mounted horses and fled north.

sentences.zh: 其第二子思明，驍勇善騎射，被髮率村義馳追之。

translations.literal: His second son Siming, brave and skilled at mounted archery, with hair unbound led village volunteers in swift pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: His second son Siming, brave and skilled in mounted archery, let his hair fall loose and led the village militia in hot pursuit.

sentences.zh: 及河，奴乘馬投水。

translations.literal: When they reached the river, the slaves mounted horses and threw themselves into the water.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the river the slaves spurred their horses into the water.

sentences.zh: 思明止將從，自射之，一發而中，落馬墮流，禽至家，臠殺之。

translations.literal: Siming stopped his companions and shot himself; one shot and he hit; [the slave] fell from the horse into the current, was seized and brought home, and butchered alive.
translations.idiomatic: Siming halted his followers and shot himself; with one arrow he struck the man down into the current, seized him, brought him home, and cut him to pieces while still alive.

sentences.zh: 思明，弟思和，並以武力自效。

translations.literal: Siming and his younger brother Sihe both offered their martial prowess in service.
translations.idiomatic: Siming and his younger brother Sihe both made their martial prowess available to the state.

sentences.zh: 思明位直閣將軍，坐弟思和同元禧逆，徙邊。

translations.literal: Siming held the post of Direct-Pavilion General; sitting with his younger brother Sihe in the same crime as Yuan Xi's rebellion, he was exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Siming held the post of direct-pavilion general; implicated with his brother Sihe in Yuan Xi's rebellion, he was exiled to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 會赦，免。

translations.literal: An amnesty came; he was released.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty followed, and he was released.

sentences.zh: 卒後，贈濟州刺史。

translations.literal: After his death he was posthumously granted Governor of Ji prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously made governor of Ji prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子先護，少有武幹。

translations.literal: His son Xianhu, in youth had martial ability.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xianhu showed martial talent from youth.

sentences.zh: 莊帝居籓也，先護得自結托。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was in his fief, Xianhu was able to attach and bind himself to him of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Zhuang was still in his princely fief, Xianhu won his trust and attached himself to him.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮稱兵向洛，靈太后令先護與鄭季明等守河梁。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong proclaimed troops heading for Luo, Empress Dowager Ling ordered Xianhu and Zheng Jiming and others to guard the River Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong raised his army toward Luoyang, Empress Dowager Ling ordered Xianhu, Zheng Jiming, and others to hold the River Bridge.

sentences.zh: 先護聞莊帝即位于河北，遂開門納榮。

translations.literal: Xianhu heard that Emperor Zhuang had taken the throne in Hebei; he then opened the gates and admitted Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Emperor Zhuang had taken the throne in Hebei, Xianhu opened the gates and admitted Rong.

sentences.zh: 以功封平昌縣侯，廣州刺史。

translations.literal: For achievements he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingchang county and made Governor of Guang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Pingchang county and made governor of Guang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元顥入洛，莊帝北巡，先護據州起義兵，不受命。

translations.literal: Yuan Hao entered Luo; Emperor Zhuang toured north; Xianhu held his province, raised righteous troops, and did not accept orders.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao entered Luoyang and Emperor Zhuang toured north, Xianhu held his province, raised righteous troops, and refused to obey orders.

sentences.zh: 莊帝還京，進爵郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang returned to the capital, his title was advanced to Duke of a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Xianhu's title was advanced to duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 曆東雍、豫二州刺史，兼尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He served successively as Governor of the two prefectures Eastern Yong and Yu, and concurrently as Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as governor of Eastern Yong and Yu prefectures and as concurrent right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及爾硃榮死，徐州刺史爾硃仲遠擁兵向洛。

translations.literal: When Erzhu Rong died, Erzhu Zhongyuan, Governor of Xu prefecture, mustered troops and marched toward Luo.
translations.idiomatic: When Erzhu Rong died, Erzhu Zhongyuan, governor of Xu prefecture, mustered troops and marched on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 詔先護與都督賀拔勝、行台楊昱同討之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Xianhu together with Commissioner-in-Chief Heba Sheng and Mobile Corps Commander Yang Yu jointly to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Xianhu to join Commissioner-in-Chief Heba Sheng and Mobile Corps Commander Yang Yu in punishing him.

sentences.zh: 聞京師不守，先護部眾逃散，因奔梁。

translations.literal: Hearing that the capital was not secure, Xianhu's troops scattered in flight; he thereupon fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the capital had fallen, Xianhu's troops scattered in flight, and he fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 尋歸，為仲遠所害。

translations.literal: Before long he returned and was killed by Zhongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned, but Zhongyuan killed him.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，贈使持節、都督、四州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu, he was posthumously granted Staff with Credentials of Authority, Commissioner-in-Chief, and Governor of four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he was posthumously granted staff with credentials of authority, commissioner-in-chief, and governorship of four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 子偉。

translations.literal: His son was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Wei.

sentences.zh: 偉字子直，少倜儻有大志，每以功名自許，善騎射，膽力過人。

translations.literal: Wei, style Zizhi, from youth was unconstrained and had great ambition; he constantly pledged himself to merit and fame, excelled at mounted archery, and his courage and strength surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, whose style was Zizhi, was unconstrained and ambitious from youth; he constantly pledged himself to merit and fame, excelled at mounted archery, and his courage and strength surpassed other men.

sentences.zh: 爾硃氏滅後，自梁歸魏。

translations.literal: After the Erzhu clan was destroyed, he returned to Wei from Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Erzhu clan was destroyed, he returned to Wei from Liang.

sentences.zh: 及武帝西遷，偉亦歸鄉里，不求仕進。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu moved west, Wei also returned to his native place and sought no advancement in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu moved west, Wei also returned to his native place and sought no office.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，河內公獨孤信既復洛陽，偉乃與宗人榮業，糾合州裏舉兵于陳留，信宿間，眾有萬人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, after Duke of Henei Dugu Xin had recovered Luoyang, Wei together with his clansman Rong Ye rallied men of the province and raised troops at Chenliu; within a night or two their force numbered ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, after Duke of Henei Dugu Xin had recovered Luoyang, Wei and his clansman Rong Ye rallied men of the province and raised troops at Chenliu; within a night or two their force numbered ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 遂拔梁州，禽東魏刺史鹿永及鎮城守將令狐德，並獲陳留郡守趙季和。

translations.literal: He then captured Liang prefecture, took captive Eastern Wei Governor Lu Yong and garrison commander Linghu De, and also captured Chenliu commandery administrator Zhao Jihe.
translations.idiomatic: He then captured Liang prefecture, took captive Eastern Wei governor Lu Yong and garrison commander Linghu De, and also captured Chenliu commandery administrator Zhao Jihe.

sentences.zh: 乃率眾西附。

translations.literal: He then led his host west to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his troops west to submit.

sentences.zh: 因是，梁、陳間相次降款。

translations.literal: Because of this, between Liang and Chen surrender offers came one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, districts between Liang and Chen offered surrender one after another.

sentences.zh: 偉弛入關西，周文帝與語，歎美之，拜北徐州刺史，封武陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Wei made his way west of the Pass; Duke Wen of Zhou conversed with him and admired him, appointing him Governor of Northern Xu prefecture and enfeoffing him as Baron of Wuyang county.
translations.idiomatic: Wei made his way west of the Pass; Duke Wen of Zhou spoke with him and admired him, appointing him governor of Northern Xu prefecture and enfeoffing him as baron of Wuyang county.

sentences.zh: 從戰河橋及解玉壁圍，偉常先鋒陷陣。

translations.literal: In the battles at River Bridge and in raising the siege of Yu Fortress, Wei constantly led the van and broke the enemy lines.
translations.idiomatic: In the battles at River Bridge and in raising the siege of Yu Fortress, Wei constantly led the van and broke the enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 侯景歸款，周文命偉率所部應接。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing submitted, Duke Wen ordered Wei to lead his troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing submitted, Duke Wen ordered Wei to lead his troops to meet him.

sentences.zh: 及景叛，偉亦全軍而還。

translations.literal: When Jing rebelled, Wei also brought his entire army back intact.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing rebelled, Wei also brought his entire army back intact.

sentences.zh: 除滎陽郡守，進爵襄城郡公，侍中、驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was made Administrator of Xingyang commandery, advanced to Duke of Xiangcheng commandery, and appointed Attendant-in-Chief, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry, and Opening-Fu with Peerage Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrator of Xingyang commandery, advanced to duke of Xiangcheng commandery, and appointed attendant-in-chief, general-in-chief of agile cavalry, and opening-fu with peerage equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝二年，進位大將軍、江陵防主、都督十五州諸軍事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei, he was promoted to Great General, Defender of Jiangling, and Commissioner-in-Chief over all military affairs in fifteen prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Gong of Wei he was promoted to great general, defender of Jiangling, and commissioner-in-chief over all military affairs in fifteen prefectures.

sentences.zh: 偉性粗獷，不遵法度，睚眥之間，便行殺戮。

translations.literal: Wei was rough and fierce by nature, did not observe the law, and would kill at the slightest grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was rough and fierce by nature, paid no heed to law, and would kill over the slightest grudge.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其有立義之效，每優容之。

translations.literal: Because he had rendered the service of raising righteous troops, the court for the most part indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had raised righteous troops, the court for the most part indulged him.

sentences.zh: 及在江陵，乃專戮副防主杞賓王，坐除名。

translations.literal: But at Jiangling he arbitrarily executed Deputy Defender Qi Binwang and was dismissed from office on that charge.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangling he arbitrarily executed Deputy Defender Qi Binwang and was dismissed from office on that charge.

sentences.zh: 保定元年，詔復官爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoding, an edict restored his titles and offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoding an edict restored his titles and offices.

sentences.zh: 天和六年，為華州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was made Governor of Hua prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianhe he was made governor of Hua prefecture.

sentences.zh: 偉前後蒞職，皆以威猛為政，吏人莫敢犯禁，盜賊亦為之休止。

translations.literal: Throughout his successive offices Wei governed by severity and might; officials and people dared not violate prohibitions, and even bandits ceased their depredations on his account.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his successive offices Wei governed by severity and might; officials and commoners dared not violate prohibitions, and even bandits ceased their depredations on his account.

sentences.zh: 雖非仁政，然頗以此見稱。

translations.literal: Though this was not benevolent government, he was nevertheless praised for it to a considerable degree.
translations.idiomatic: Though this was not benevolent government, he was nevertheless praised for it to a considerable degree.

sentences.zh: 卒於州，贈本官，加少傅、都督、司州刺史，諡曰肅。

translations.literal: He died in office; his former posts were conferred posthumously, with addition of Junior Tutor, Commissioner-in-Chief, and Governor of Si prefecture; his posthumous title was Su.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office; his former posts were conferred posthumously, with the additions of junior tutor, commissioner-in-chief, and governor of Si prefecture; his posthumous title was Su.

sentences.zh: 偉性吃，少時嘗逐鹿於野。

translations.literal: Wei stuttered; in youth he once chased a deer in the wild.
translations.idiomatic: Wei stuttered; in youth he once chased a deer in the wild.

sentences.zh: 失之，遇牧豎，問焉。

translations.literal: He lost it, met a shepherd boy, and asked him about it.
translations.idiomatic: He lost the trail, met a shepherd boy, and asked him about it.

sentences.zh: 牧豎答之，其言亦吃。

translations.literal: The shepherd boy answered him, and his speech too was halting.
translations.idiomatic: The shepherd boy answered him, and his speech too was halting.

sentences.zh: 偉怒，謂其效己，遂射殺之。

translations.literal: Wei flew into a rage, thinking the boy was mimicking him, and shot him dead.
translations.idiomatic: Wei flew into a rage, thinking the boy was mocking him, and shot him dead.

sentences.zh: 其忍暴如此。

translations.literal: His cruelty was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: His cruelty was such as this.

sentences.zh: 子大士嗣。

translations.literal: His son Dashi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dashi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 述祖族子雛，有識尚，操行清整，仕至膠州刺史。

translations.literal: Shuzu's clansman Chu had discernment and lofty standards, his conduct pure and ordered, and in office rose to Governor of Jiao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu's clansman Chu had discernment and lofty standards, his conduct pure and ordered, and in office rose to governor of Jiao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 初，齊文宣為皇太子納其女為良娣，雛時為尚書郎，趙郡李祖升兄弟微相敬憚。

translations.literal: Early on, when Emperor Wenxuan of Qi was crown prince, he took Chu's daughter as Worthy Concubine; at the time Chu was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and the brothers Li Zusheng of Zhao commandery were slightly respectful yet wary of him.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Emperor Wenxuan of Qi was crown prince, he took Chu's daughter as worthy concubine; at the time Chu was a gentleman of the Masters of Writing, and the brothers Li Zusheng of Zhao commandery were slightly respectful yet wary of him.

sentences.zh: 楊愔奏授雛趙郡太守，祖升兄弟具服至雛門，投刺拜謁。

translations.literal: Yang Yin memorialized to appoint Chu Administrator of Zhao commandery; Zusheng and his brothers put on full dress, came to Chu's gate, and left calling cards to pay their respects.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin memorialized to appoint Chu administrator of Zhao commandery; Zusheng and his brothers put on full dress, came to Chu's gate, and left calling cards to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 文宣聞之喜，笑曰：「足得殺李家兒矣。」

translations.literal: Wenxuan heard of it with delight and said with a laugh: "Now we are more than able to kill those Li boys."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan heard of it with delight and said with a laugh, "Now we're more than able to kill those Li boys."

sentences.zh: 論曰：王慧龍拔難自歸，間關夷險，撫人督眾，見憚嚴敵。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Wang Huilong pulled free from hardship and returned of himself, passed through difficulties in perilous straits, comforted men and commanded troops, and inspired dread in formidable foes.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Wang Huilong pulled free from hardship and returned of his own accord, passed through perilous straits, comforted men and commanded troops, and inspired dread in formidable foes.

sentences.zh: 世珍實有令子，克播家聲。

translations.literal: Shizhen truly had a fine son who could broadcast the family's reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhen truly had a fine son who could broadcast the family's reputation.

sentences.zh: 松年之送終戀舊，有古人風矣。

translations.literal: Songnian's care for the dead and attachment to old ties had the air of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Songnian's care for the dead and attachment to old ties had the air of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 劭爰自幼童，訖于白首；

translations.literal: Shao, from the time he was a child to the end of his white-haired years—
translations.idiomatic: Shao, from childhood to the end of his white-haired years—

sentences.zh: 好學不倦，究極群書，晉紳洽聞之士，無不推其博物。

translations.literal: loved learning without weariness and exhausted every book; none of the well-informed gentlemen of Jin failed to praise his encyclopedic knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: loved learning without weariness and exhausted every book; none of the well-informed gentlemen of Jin failed to praise his encyclopedic knowledge.

sentences.zh: 雅好著述，久在史官，既撰《齊書》，兼修隋典。

translations.literal: He delighted in composition, long served as historiographer, wrote the 'History of Qi,' and also compiled the statutes of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in composition, long served as historiographer, wrote the 'History of Qi,' and also compiled the statutes of Sui.

sentences.zh: 好詭怪之說，尚委曲之談；

translations.literal: Yet he loved strange and supernatural tales and prized roundabout discourse—
translations.idiomatic: Yet he loved strange and supernatural tales and prized roundabout discourse—

sentences.zh: 文詞鄙穢，體統煩雜，直愧南、董，才無遷、固，徒煩翰墨，不足觀采。

translations.literal: his wording was base and foul, his structure tedious and confused—he was truly ashamed to face the historians of Nan and Dong, but lacked the talent of Qian and Gu; he merely wasted ink and was not worth reading.
translations.idiomatic: his wording was base and foul, his structure tedious and confused—he was truly ashamed to face the historians of Nan and Dong, but lacked the talent of Qian and Gu; he merely wasted ink and was not worth reading.

sentences.zh: 經營符瑞，雜以妖訛。

translations.literal: He arranged prophetic omens and mixed in demonic falsehoods.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged prophetic omens and mixed in demonic falsehoods.

sentences.zh: 為河朔清流而乾沒榮利，得不以道而頹其家聲。

translations.literal: A pure stream of Hebei, yet he pursued profit by foul means—could he fail to bring down his family's reputation by unorthodox conduct?
translations.idiomatic: A pure stream of Hebei, yet he pursued profit by foul means—could he fail to bring down his family's reputation by unorthodox conduct?

sentences.zh: 惜矣！

translations.literal: How pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: How pitiable!

sentences.zh: 鄭羲機識明悟，為時所許。

translations.literal: Zheng Xi was quick-witted and perceptive, acknowledged by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xi was quick-witted and perceptive, acknowledged by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 懿兄弟風尚，俱有可觀，故能並當榮遇，共濟其美。

translations.literal: The Yi brothers' moral tone was alike worth viewing, and so they could both enjoy glory at once and jointly add luster to each other's repute.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi brothers' moral tone was alike worth viewing, and so they could both enjoy glory at once and jointly add luster to each other's repute.

sentences.zh: 述祖德業，足嗣家聲。

translations.literal: Shuzu's virtue and achievement were enough to continue the family's renown.
translations.idiomatic: Shuzu's virtue and achievement were enough to continue the family's renown.

sentences.zh: 嚴祖、仲禮，大虧門素。

translations.literal: Yanzu and Zhongli greatly damaged the family character.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzu and Zhongli greatly damaged the family character.

sentences.zh: 幼儒令問促年。

translations.literal: Youru had a fine reputation but died young.
translations.idiomatic: Youru had a fine reputation but died young.

sentences.zh: 伯猷以賄敗德。

translations.literal: Boyou ruined his virtue through bribery.
translations.idiomatic: Boyou ruined his virtue through bribery.

sentences.zh: 道邕撫寧離散，仁惠克舉。

translations.literal: Daoyong comforted and settled the scattered, his benevolence and grace achieving fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Daoyong comforted and settled the scattered, his benevolence and grace achieving fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 譯實受顧托，適足為敗。

translations.literal: Yi in truth received a deathbed entrustment, yet was fit only to bring ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Yi in truth received a deathbed entrustment, yet was fit only to bring ruin.

sentences.zh: 及帝行明德，義非簡在；

translations.literal: When the emperor practiced bright virtue, the appointment was not by personal selection;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor practiced bright virtue, the appointment was not by personal selection;

sentences.zh: 鹽梅之寄，固不攸歸。

translations.literal: the charge as salt and plum advisor was assuredly not his to hold.
translations.idiomatic: the charge as salt-and-plum advisor was assuredly not his to hold.

sentences.zh: 言追昔款，內懷觖望，恥居吳、耿之末，羞與絳、灌為伍。

translations.literal: Speaking of old ties while nursing resentment within, he was ashamed to stand behind Wu and Geng, and loath to rank with Jiang and Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of old ties while nursing resentment within, he was ashamed to stand behind Wu and Geng, and loath to rank with Jiang and Guan.

sentences.zh: 事君盡禮，既闕於夙心；

translations.literal: Serving his lord with full ritual—yet this fell short of his early resolve;
translations.idiomatic: Serving his lord with full ritual—yet this fell short of his early resolve;

sentences.zh: 不愛其親，遽彰於物議。

translations.literal: not loving his kin, he soon made himself conspicuous in public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: not loving his kin, he soon made himself conspicuous in public criticism.

sentences.zh: 格之名教，君子所深尤也。

translations.literal: Striking against the name-and-teaching of the sages—this is what gentlemen deeply condemn.
translations.idiomatic: Striking against the name-and-teaching of the sages—this is what gentlemen deeply condemn.

sentences.zh: 儼名編《恩倖》，取辱前載。

translations.literal: Yan's name was entered in 'Favored Favorites' and brought disgrace on past records.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's name was entered in 'Favored Favorites' and brought disgrace on past records.

sentences.zh: 偉翻然豹變，蓋知機之士乎。

translations.literal: Wei suddenly transformed like a leopard—was he not a man who knew the moment?
translations.idiomatic: Wei suddenly transformed like a leopard—was he not a man who knew the moment?
